also use the AI helpersadd nothing: SEO suggestions and translation follow content.write_own; alt text needs media.write
  • _own permissions reach only entries created with the same key; another key of the same user gets 403 content.not_owner. Agents never archive, move, schedule or delete (deleting needs content.delete).
  • When done, the agent asks for a review: POST /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/request-review (event content.review_requested — forward it to editors with a webhook).
  • Requests with an API key are rate limited per key (AUTOXIDE_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY_PER_MINUTE, default 120), and every change is in the audit log with the key that made it.

Telling readers about AI-generated content

Entries carry ai_generated (set by the server for its translations; agents should send "ai_generated": true for what they write). When a person (signed in, not with an API key) publishes such an entry after reviewing it, they send {"ai_reviewed": true} to POST /entries/{id}/publish; the published version records who and when. The public endpoints return ai_generated and ai_reviewed, so your website can show a notice where the rules ask for one — for example Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which applies from 2 August 2026 to AI-generated text published to inform the public on matters of public interest; its exception for human-reviewed text with editorial responsibility is read narrowly. Autoxide records the facts; it does not give legal advice.

When something goes wrong

CodeMeaningWhat to do
ai.disabled, ai.embedding_disablednot configuredset AUTOXIDE_AI_* / AUTOXIDE_EMBEDDING_*
ai.misconfiguredthe provider refused the key or settingsrun autoxide ai check; the server log names the HTTP status
ai.provider_unavailablebusy, rate limited or unreachableretry after Retry-After; translations retry by themselves
ai.quota_exceededdaily token limit reachedwait for midnight UTC or raise the limit
ai.request_rejectedthe provider rejected the request (content too long for the model, a setting it does not accept)read the reason in the server log; lower AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_TRANSLATE_BATCH_TOKENS or change the model
ai.refusedthe model declined the contentchange the content or do it by hand
ai.output_truncatedthe answer was too longlower AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_TRANSLATE_BATCH_TOKENS
ai.output_invalid, content.translation_invalidwrong shape twiceretry, or use a more capable model
ai.unsupported_inputthe model reads no imagesset AUTOXIDE_AI_IMAGES right, or use a vision model

Settings

Every setting, with its default, is in .env.example: AUTOXIDE_AI_*, AUTOXIDE_EMBEDDING_*, AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AI_SEND_PRIVATE, AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_TRANSLATE_BATCH_TOKENS, AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_PUBLIC_SEMANTIC_SEARCH, AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_PUBLIC_SEARCH_PER_MINUTE, AUTOXIDE_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY_*.

Analytics

Tiếng Việt: ANALYTICS.vi.md

The analytics module counts the visits of your websites inside Autoxide: how many people came, which pages and objects (products, posts) they viewed, where they came from (search, social networks, UTM campaigns) and where a funnel such as “product → cart → paid order” loses them. Nothing is sent to a third party, no cookie is set, and only daily totals are kept for long.

How it works

  1. Pages of the website send events to POST /api/v1/analytics/public/events.
  2. Other modules declare their event types (e.g. catalog.product_viewed) and funnels; events the server knows better (a paid order) are taken from that module’s own events, never from the browser.
  3. Every hour a job adds the events up into daily totals per website. Reports only read those totals, so they stay fast on large sites. Today’s numbers lag by up to an hour.
  4. Single events are deleted after AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS (7); daily totals after AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS (790, two years and two months).

Privacy by default

  • No cookie, no fingerprint. A visit is told apart by a session key: a keyed hash of the website, the network block of the address (IPv4 /24, IPv6 /64) and a coarse browser label (chrome|android|mobile, no version). The key is random per day and deleted once the day is over: sessions of two days cannot be linked, and nobody can work an address back out.
  • Neither the address nor the full user agent is stored. Query strings and fragments are cut from page paths (they may hold emails); only the host of the referring page is kept.
  • Per-person tracking only with consent. When a signed-in user consented to the purpose analytics.personal in the consent ledger of the compliance module, their events carry their account, so modules can show “recently viewed”. Withdrawing stops it at once and removes the link from past events; daily totals, which hold nobody, stay.
  • Visitors over several days are the sum of the daily unique visitors: without cookies one person on two days counts twice.

Sending events from a website

const queue = [];
function track(type, extra = {}) {
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  queue.push({
    type,
    path: location.pathname,
    referrer: document.referrer || undefined,
    utm: {
      source: params.get("utm_source") || undefined,
      medium: params.get("utm_medium") || undefined,
      campaign: params.get("utm_campaign") || undefined,
    },
    ...extra,
  });
}
function flush() {
  if (!queue.length) return;
  const events = queue.splice(0, 20);
  fetch("https://api.shop.example/api/v1/analytics/public/events", {
    method: "POST",
    keepalive: true, // still sent while the page closes, like sendBeacon
    credentials: "include", // only if signed-in users should be linked (with consent)
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ events }),
  });
}
track("analytics.page_view");
// On a product page:
track("catalog.product_viewed", { object: "catalog.product:0190…" });
addEventListener("visibilitychange", () => document.visibilityState === "hidden" && flush());
  • At most 20 events per call. The answer is always 202 with accepted and dropped counts.
  • GET /api/v1/analytics/event-types lists every type the installed modules declare, with their props and object kind.
  • Events are dropped, never refused, when: the type is unknown or recorded by the server only; props holds an undeclared name or a wrong type; object is missing or of the wrong kind for a type that names one; the caller is a known bot or sends no user agent; the page (its Origin, else Referer) is not on this website; more than AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_PER_MINUTE (120) events came from the same network block in a minute, or more than AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_PER_DAY (20000) in a day. A client outside a browser can fake Origin and the user agent, so these limits bound how much one network can skew the reports; treat the reports as estimates, not as figures to pay or rank on.
  • The website is the one of the domain called. A page served from another host than the API (one tenant, no verified domain) is accepted when its host is listed in AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTS. Set ?site=<unit id> when the API is not called on the website’s own domain.

Reports

All need analytics.read at the website’s organization unit; site defaults to the website of the whole tenant, from / to (UTC days) to the last 30 days, at most 400 days at once.

EndpointWhat
GET /api/v1/analytics/overviewvisitors, page views, events, bounce rate, top sources, one entry per day
GET /api/v1/analytics/pagesmost viewed pages
GET /api/v1/analytics/sourceswhere visits came from: utm_source, else the referring site, else direct
GET /api/v1/analytics/campaignsutm_campaign values
GET /api/v1/analytics/objects?kind=catalog.productmost viewed objects
GET /api/v1/analytics/typesevents by type
GET /api/v1/analytics/funnels, /funnels/{key}declared funnels; sessions per step

The bounce rate is the share of visits that saw exactly one page. Funnel steps are counted on their own (cookieless visits cannot be linked to an order recorded by the server), so a later step may exceed an earlier one.

MCP tools (read only): analytics.overview, analytics.top_pages, analytics.top_objects, analytics.funnel. The summary metric analytics.visitors (last 7 days) appears on the overview page of the admin interface.

For module authors

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_kernel::analytics::{AnalyticsEvent, Funnel, Prop, PropKind, ServerHit};

const VARIANT: &[Prop] = &[Prop::new("variant", PropKind::Text)];

fn analytics_events(&self) -> Vec<AnalyticsEvent> {
    vec![
        AnalyticsEvent::browser("catalog.product_viewed", "A product page was shown.")
            .object_kind("catalog.product")
            .props(VARIANT),
        // Taken from this module's own event `orders.order_confirmed`.
        AnalyticsEvent::server("orders.purchased", "An order was paid.", "orders.order_confirmed", |event| {
            Ok(Some(ServerHit::new(event.occurred_at).object(format!("orders.order:{}", event.id))))
        }),
    ]
}

fn funnels(&self) -> Vec<Funnel> {
    vec![Funnel::new("orders.checkout", "From product to paid order.",
        &["catalog.product_viewed", "orders.cart_added", "orders.purchased"])]
}
}

Other modules read numbers through autoxide_analytics::api::Analytics: top_objects (what is trending) and recently_viewed (empty without consent).

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_ENABLEDtruetake events at all
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS7days single events are kept (2–90)
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_RETENTION_DAYS790days daily totals are kept (30–3650)
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_PER_MINUTE120events per network block per minute
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_EVENTS_PER_DAY20000events per network block per day
AUTOXIDE_ANALYTICS_ALLOWED_HOSTSemptyextra website hosts allowed to send

Legal notes

Vietnamese law (Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15, Decree 356/2025) asks for consent per purpose before linking behaviour to a person, and for keeping only what is needed. Whether anonymous daily totals are personal data, and whether a cookieless site needs a consent banner, is not settled: check the original texts or ask someone qualified for your case. Behaviour-based advertising messages need consent (Decree 91/2020/NĐ-CP).

Bookings (module bookings)

The bookings module takes appointments for services: spas, salons, clinics, studios, classes, sports courts. Customers pick a service, a staff member (or anyone free) and a free time; the shop manages staff, rooms and equipment, working hours, time off, reminders, cancellations and no-shows by its own policy, and can hold a booking with a deposit paid through its licensed payment partner. It needs none of the selling modules.

Vietnamese: BOOKINGS.vi.md.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
bookings.services.manageServices, staff, rooms, equipment, weekly schedules, time off and extra hours
bookings.manageEvery booking of the unit: book for customers, confirm, check in, no-show, cancel, move
bookings.readSeeing every booking of the unit, without changing them
bookings.staffYour own appointments (resources linked to your account): check in, done, no-show

All four work per organization unit (a shop or a branch). Customers need no permission: any signed-in user books for themselves and sees their bookings at GET /api/v1/bookings/me/bookings. Guests book with a code sent to their phone.

Set up

  1. Time zone. Working hours are local to the unit: set organizations.timezone (e.g. Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh) on the unit or its parent. Without it, UTC.
  2. Staff, rooms, equipment — POST /api/v1/bookings/resources with kind staff, room or equipment. Link a staff member to their account (user_id) so they see their own appointments.
  3. Weekly schedule — PUT /api/v1/bookings/resources/{id}/schedule with ranges such as {"weekday": 1, "start_minute": 540, "end_minute": 1020} (Monday 09:00–17:00 local time). Staff without a schedule are never free; rooms and equipment without one are always open.
  4. Time off and extra hours — POST /api/v1/bookings/exceptions with kind closed (holiday, leave) or open (an extra shift), starts_at, ends_at (UTC).
  5. Services — POST /api/v1/bookings/services: duration_minutes, buffer_before_minutes (setup) and buffer_after_minutes (cleaning), price, deposit (none, percent of the price, or a fixed amount), capacity (1 for a haircut, more for a class), performers (who can give it) and required (rooms or machines every booking also needs).

Durations and buffers are in steps of 5 minutes.

Policy per unit

Organization settings, inherited down the tree:

SettingDefaultMeaning
bookings.free_cancel_hours24Cancel at least this many hours before the start: the whole deposit is refunded
bookings.late_cancel_retain_percent100Share of the deposit kept on a later cancellation
bookings.no_show_retain_percent100Share of the deposit kept on a no-show
bookings.require_approvalfalseBookings without a deposit wait for the shop to confirm them
bookings.hold_minutes10Minutes a booking is held while the customer pays the deposit

The availability answer repeats these terms, so the shop can show the price, deposit and cancellation conditions before the customer books, as consumer protection law asks.

Free times

GET /api/v1/bookings/public/availability?service_id=…&from=…&to=… (no sign-in; resource_id and org_id are optional; at most 31 days at a time) lists free start times every 15 minutes of local time: the weekly schedule plus extra hours, minus time off, minus what is already booked with its buffers. Each time has starts_at (UTC), local_start (with the unit’s offset) and seats_left. The answer is cached for 15 seconds, so a time shown may be taken by the time you book.

Booking

  • Customers — POST /api/v1/bookings/public/bookings with service_id, starts_at (from the availability), optional resource_id (omitted: the first staff member free), customer (name, phone, email).
    • No deposit: confirmed at once, or pending when the unit approves bookings (POST /bookings/{id}/confirm).
    • Deposit: held for bookings.hold_minutes; the answer has a checkout (checkout_url, qr_payload) of the payment partner. When the partner reports the payment the booking becomes confirmed. Unpaid holds are released every minute and the time is free again; money that arrives after the hold ended is refunded in full.
  • Guests — first POST /api/v1/bookings/public/phone-codes with phone; send the challenge_id and the 6 digits received by SMS as phone_code in the booking. A code works once, for 10 minutes. Guests cancel with a new code at POST /api/v1/bookings/public/bookings/{id}/cancel.
  • The shop — POST /api/v1/bookings/bookings (phone calls, walk-ins): confirmed at once, no deposit.

Two people never get the same time: every booking takes 5-minute cells of each staff member, room and machine it uses, under a unique key, in one transaction. The second request gets 409 bookings.slot_taken — on SQLite and PostgreSQL alike. A class counts its seats with one conditional update and answers 409 bookings.capacity_full when full.

After booking

ActionWhoEndpoint
Check in, doneshop, own staffPOST /api/v1/bookings/bookings/{id}/check-in, /complete
No-show (after the start)shop, own staffPOST /api/v1/bookings/bookings/{id}/no-show — keeps bookings.no_show_retain_percent of the deposit
Cancelshop (any time, full refund), customer (until the start, by policy)POST /api/v1/bookings/bookings/{id}/cancel
Moveshop (any time), customer (within the free window)POST /api/v1/bookings/bookings/{id}/reschedule
Calendar fileshop, staff, customerGET /api/v1/bookings/bookings/{id}/calendar.ics, GET /api/v1/bookings/me/bookings/{id}/calendar.ics

Refunds go through the payment partner, never from the platform’s own money (ledger), with a fixed reference: a retried refund is not paid twice.

Reminders

With the notifications module, customers get a transactional reminder (bookings.reminder) 24 hours and 2 hours before the start, on the channels they have (app inbox, email, SMS, Zalo ZNS, push). Bookings made within 24 hours only get the 2-hour one. A reminder is never sent twice, even when the job runs again; a moved booking is reminded again at its new time. The message links to the booking’s calendar file.

For AI agents (MCP)

ToolPermission
bookings.availability— (read only)
bookings.list_bookingsbookings.read or bookings.manage (read only)
bookings.create_bookingbookings.manage
bookings.reschedule_bookingbookings.manage
bookings.cancel_bookingbookings.manage

Errors

CodeStatusMeaning
bookings.slot_taken409The time was just taken; ask for the free times again
bookings.capacity_full409The class is full
bookings.outside_hours422Outside the working hours of the staff member or room
bookings.too_late_to_cancel409The booking has started
bookings.too_late_to_change409Customers move bookings only within the free cancellation window
bookings.invalid_status409Not possible in the booking’s status
bookings.code_invalid422Guest code wrong, used or expired
bookings.payments_unavailable503The service asks for a deposit but payments are not set up

Legal notes

Check with the original texts or a legal professional: consumer protection (Law 19/2023/QH15, Decree 55/2024) asks that price, deposit and cancellation terms are shown before booking; deposits go through a licensed payment service provider (Decree 52/2024); clinics have their own rules on medical records (Law 15/2023/QH15) — bookings stores no health information, notes are short text only.

Catalog

Tiếng Việt

The catalog module holds the products every commerce module reads: products with variants, a category tree, and price lists with a full price history. Inventory, promotions, shipping, orders and sales channels read products and prices through autoxide_catalog::api::Catalog, never through the catalog_… tables. Everything is under /api/v1/catalog; every endpoint is described in docs/openapi.json, and the same operations are MCP tools (catalog.*).

Products and variants

  • POST /products creates a product as a draft together with its first variant. kind is physical (shipped, stocked), digital, service or bundle. tax_category is a code of the tax engine (GET /api/v1/tax/categories), e.g. vat.standard.
  • Texts are per language (PUT /products/{id}/translations/{locale}); the languages allowed are AUTOXIDE_CATALOG_LOCALES. Each translation has its public path, /<AUTOXIDE_CATALOG_PRODUCT_PATH_PREFIX>/<slug>. An empty slug is made from the name, with -2, -3… when taken. The description is plain text (blank lines separate paragraphs); HTML is not interpreted.
  • Options (colour, size…) are set with PUT /products/{id}/options: up to 3 options of up to 100 values. Adding an option gives every existing variant the option’s first value. Each variant holds one value of each option, and no two variants share a combination (catalog.option_combination_taken).
  • SKUs and barcodes are unique in a tenant (catalog.sku_taken, catalog.barcode_taken); SKUs are compared ignoring case and spaces. A numeric barcode of 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits must have a right GTIN check digit.
  • Sale mode per variant: in_stock, backorder or preorder (with preorder_available_on after today and an optional preorder_limit).
  • Images are public media of the media module (PUT /products/{id}/media).
  • Status (POST /products/{id}/status, permission catalog.products.publish): draft → active or archived; active ↔ inactive; any → archived; archived → draft. Going on sale needs a tax category, a name and an active variant. A product that was on sale once cannot be deleted, only archived.
  • Bundles (kind: bundle) list their components with PUT /variants/{id}/components; a bundle cannot contain a bundle, itself or a service.

The number of products is the plan limit catalog.products (archived products count). Plan features: catalog.variants (more than one variant), catalog.price_lists (more than one price list), catalog.bundles, catalog.digital, catalog.ai.

Categories

One tree per tenant, at most 7 levels deep (/categories, permission catalog.categories.manage). POST /categories/{id}/move moves a category with everything below it; moving it under itself is refused (catalog.category_cycle). Filtering products by a category includes its subcategories.

Attributes, restricted goods and readiness

  • Attributes (/attributes, permission catalog.categories.manage) are typed: text, integer, decimal (with scale), boolean, date, option, options. Products set their values with PUT /products/{id}/attributes.
  • A category lists its attributes with PUT /categories/{id}/attributes; an attribute can be required, from effective_from until effective_to, for the category and (by default) its subcategories. Required attributes are data: new labelling rules are added with their start date.
  • Prohibited and conditional goods are shared rules with their legal basis (GET /restriction-rules). The operator loads them with autoxide task catalog.load_restrictions (the vn pack ships with the server; the same command creates sample product-label attributes such as origin and use-by date for a tenant). Link rules to a category with PUT /categories/{id}/restrictions. The rules were compiled from secondary sources — check them against the source texts with a legal professional.
  • A conditional product needs valid documents (/products/{id}/documents, permission catalog.documents.manage), e.g. an alcohol retail licence.
  • Every product has a readiness: restricted (prohibited goods), missing_attributes, missing_documents or ready. Only ready products go on sale. Filter with ?readiness= and count with GET /products/counts?group_by=readiness. Expired documents are noticed by a daily job.
  • Going on sale also checks that the tax category exists in the tax engine for the unit’s tax profile (catalog.tax_category_unknown).

Prices

A price list belongs to an organization unit (a chain or a store) and applies there and below. It has a currency, tax_inclusive, an audience (consumer or business), an optional customer group and a priority.

Price rows are only ever added. A new price is a new row with its own valid_from; a future valid_from schedules a price, and valid_to makes it temporary — when it ends, the earlier price applies again. The history is GET /price-lists/{id}/prices. POST /price-lists/{id}/prices adds up to 500 rows under your reference: sending the same reference and content again returns the rows already written.

Which list wins. For a store, customer group and time, the lists that apply are the active lists in the currency, at the store or a unit above it, whose customer group (and company, channel, market) is empty or matches. They are ordered: the unit closest to the store first, then a matching company, customer group, channel and market, then higher priority, then id. Each variant takes its price from the first list in that order that has one. GET /variants/{id}/price?org_id=…&currency=… shows the price and the ordered candidate lists.

Consumer prices in Viet Nam must be in VND and include tax when the unit has a Vietnamese tax profile (Price Law 16/2023/QH15 — check the source text with a legal professional before relying on it).

Derived price lists take their prices from a source list (derived_from; one level only, catalog.derived_chain), adjusted by adjust_bp (basis points, signed: -1000 = 10% off) and adjust_minor, then rounded by a rounding rule (/rounding-rules: multiples of step_minor, or k × step_minor + ending_minor, e.g. step 10,000 and ending 9,000 give 129,000 and 199,000). A job writes real price rows into the derived list whenever the source gets prices, so reading a price never computes a formula. A manual row in the derived list pins that variant’s price while it is in effect.

Bulk price changes (/price-lists/{id}/changes): create (set, percent or amount, for categories, products or variants, optionally temporary with valid_to) → preview (counts, 20 sample rows, price-floor violations; nothing is written) → approve (catalog.prices.approve; with the unit setting catalog.price_change_requires_second_person on, someone other than the maker must approve) → a job writes the rows (source = bulk). Undo a change with a new change back to the old prices.

Price floors (/price-guards): a minimum price and / or a minimum margin over unit cost, per unit and optionally per category, acting as warn (the price is saved with a warning) or block (catalog.price_below_floor). The rule of the closest unit wins; within a unit, the rule of the closest category wins. Unit costs come from the inventory.cost_changed event.

Public reads for websites

No sign-in needed (/api/v1/catalog/public/…). Only products that are active, have a price on the website asking and a text in the language asked; the website comes from the domain or ?site=<unit>. Every answer has an ETag (send it back in If-None-Match to get 304) and Cache-Control: public, no-cache.

EndpointWhat
GET /public/products?locale=viproduct cards; filters category=<slug> (with sub-categories), attr.<code>=<value>[,<value>] (filterable attributes), price_min / price_max, q (with or without accents), on_sale, seller=<unit>, sold_by=own|marketplace, min_rating; sort=newest|price_asc|price_desc|best_selling|rating
GET /public/products/by-slug/{slug}?locale=vithe product page: variants with current prices, images, attributes, categories, other languages
GET /public/categories?locale=vi · GET /public/categories/{slug}?locale=vivisible categories (a category under a hidden one is hidden)
GET /public/sitemapevery product address in every language, at most 200 per page
GET /public/products/{id}/similar?locale=viup to 12 products whose texts mean something close (AI embeddings); without embeddings, products of the same categories, best sellers first
GET /public/products/{id}/frequently-bought-together?locale=viup to 12 products found in the same completed orders over the last 90 days, most orders first

Product cards carry variant_summary (“3 sizes”), brand (the attribute with code brand) and unit_price (price per kg, l, m or piece) when a variant has a net content (net_quantity + net_unit, e.g. 500 and g). Product pages give each variant a path with ?variant=<id>, unit_price, and for a temporary price price_valid_until and regular_price (the price just before it) — what structured data (Product, ProductGroup, Offer) needs; the GTIN is barcode.

Search helpers:

  • GET /public/search/suggest?q=…&locale=vi — suggestions as the shopper types (products, categories, and what other modules add), exact accents first, at most 10.
  • GET /public/products/facets — takes the filters of /public/products and counts products per attribute value and per seller (the counts of one filter ignore that filter).
  • GET / PUT /synonyms — the tenant’s synonym groups ([["áo thun", "áo phông", "tee"]]); search and suggestions use them (catalog.categories.manage).

Best sellers and ratings come from module orders: each completed order (orders.order_completed) counts its products once (a redelivered event is not counted twice), over a rolling 90-day window that a daily job (catalog.refresh_sales) moves forward; review events carry the product’s current review count and star total. The same orders feed “frequently bought together”. “Similar” needs the ai module with embeddings on (AUTOXIDE_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER and the other AUTOXIDE_EMBEDDING_* settings): each product on sale gets one vector per language, and its list of similar products is computed when it is indexed, not on each read.

Which products a website shows: those of its own unit, of the units above it, and of sellers below it (seller.own = false on the card). A store hides a product of its chain with PUT /stores/{org_id}/overrides/{product_id} {"hidden": true} (catalog.products.write at the store).

Prices on these pages are the current prices of the website’s price list (the closest unit with an active price list), without customer group. They are kept ready in a derived table rebuilt by a background job after every change of price, status, price list or store choice, and every minute for scheduled prices that just started or ended (event catalog.price_effective). If the public lists ever look out of date, run autoxide task catalog.rebuild_storefront [tenant=<slug>].

Collections

A collection groups products for a page of the website (“Summer sale”, “New this month”). Manage them under /collections (catalog.collections.manage at the collection’s unit; reading needs catalog.products.read); PATCH and PUT /collections/{id}/items need If-Match.

  • kind: manual — chosen products in order: PUT /collections/{id}/items {"product_ids": [...]} (at most 500) replaces the list.
  • kind: rule — products matching every condition of rules (at most 10): {"category_ids": [...], "attributes": {"color": ["red"]}, "price_min": 100000, "price_max": 500000, "new_within_days": 30, "on_promotion": true, "match": "all"}. Prices are in the smallest unit of the website’s price list currency; on_promotion needs module promotions (catalog.rule_needs_module).
  • sort: manual (chosen order, manual collections only), newest, price_asc, price_desc, best_selling; equal values keep a stable order by id on both databases.
  • texts by language: title, slug (unique in the language), description, meta_title, meta_description; media_id (a public picture); status (draft, active, archived) and an optional starts_at / ends_at.
  • ai_assisted: the texts were written with an AI’s suggestion; the public page carries it so the website shows an AI label (Vietnam’s Law on Artificial Intelligence — check the original text). MCP tools set it by default; a person clears it with PATCH after rewriting the texts.

The website reads GET /api/v1/catalog/public/collections/{slug}?locale=vi (public; site or the domain): the collection’s texts and one page of its products, with the same cards as /public/products, only products still shown on that website, in the collection’s order. Only active collections in their time window, of the website or a unit above it, are public. Banners and menus point to a collection as catalog.collection of the object directory (/collections/<slug>). MCP tools: catalog.list_collections, catalog.save_collection (drafts only: a person sets a collection active). A worked home-page example: docs/guides/storefront.md.

For other modules

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
let catalog = context.require::<dyn autoxide_catalog::api::Catalog>()?;
}

variants, variant_by_code, prices (price in effect at a time), reference_prices (the price in effect just before a time — for “price before the discount”), price_floors and bundle_components. Every call takes at most 500 ids and runs a fixed number of queries. Events are listed in autoxide_catalog::api::events.

A module registered after catalog plugs in through dyn CatalogExtensions: a promotions module gives the public lists their automatic sale prices with set_sale_price_source (a SalePriceSource), and emits promotions.automatic_prices_changed (after.variant_ids) when they change. A marketplace module can refuse to put a product on sale with set_listing_gate (a ListingGate); the status change then answers 422 catalog.listing_denied.

catalog.display_price_changed tells when the public price of a product on a website changes (the automatic sale price when there is one, otherwise the lowest variant price; null when it is not on sale there; never the crossed-out compare_at). A rebuild that leaves the price as it was sends nothing.

Import and export (CSV)

Both run in the background and need file storage (module files); without it they answer 503 catalog.storage_unavailable. Files are kept 7 days.

  • POST /imports?org_id=<unit> with the file itself as the body (Content-Type: text/csv, UTF-8, at most 20 MiB and 50 000 rows; catalog.import). Columns, first line, any order: sku (required), name, locale, short_description, description, kind, tax_category, barcode, weight_grams. A known SKU updates that variant and the product’s text in locale (the address stays); a new SKU creates a draft product with one variant (needs name and tax_category). Nothing is put on sale by an import, so importing the same file again changes nothing. Each row is checked like a manual change with your rights: a bad row is reported and the others are written.
  • GET /imports/{id}: status is queued, running, succeeded, succeeded_with_errors (see errors: line, column, code, message), rejected (the file is not valid; nothing was written) or failed. Only the person who started it sees it. Products with several variants or options are completed through the API after the import.
  • POST /exports {"org_id": …} (catalog.export): every variant of the products you can read, with the same columns, so the file can be edited and imported back. Cells a spreadsheet would run as a formula (=, +, -, @) start with '; an import removes that ' again. When GET /exports/{id} says succeeded, download content_path.

MCP tools: catalog.start_import, catalog.import_status.

AI drafts of descriptions and SEO

POST /products/{id}/suggestions {"locale": "vi"} (catalog.products.write, plan feature catalog.ai, the ai module on) asks the model for a short description, a description and SEO texts using only what the product’s texts already say. The result is a draft: nothing on the product changes. POST /suggestions/{id}/apply writes it into that language’s text (name and address unchanged) and marks the product ai_assisted; POST /suggestions/{id}/discard drops it. MCP tool: catalog.suggest_copy.

Draft a product from photos

POST /products/from-images {"media_ids": […], "locale": "vi", "tax_category": "vat.standard", "category_id": null, "org_id": null} (catalog.products.write, plan feature catalog.ai, an AI model that reads images) sends 1 to 8 photos of the media library — server-made thumbnails without metadata, never the originals — to the model, in the background. Follow Location (GET /products/from-images/{id}) until status is succeeded: product_id is a new draft product marked ai_assisted, with name, descriptions and SEO texts, a category of your tree (or the one you gave; a category outside your tree is dropped), the attribute values of that category the model was sure of, and the public photos as its images. Prices, stock and barcode are left for you; the SKU is a temporary AI-… code. Nothing is put on sale. (Refusing photos generated by AI as product images comes with step 67, which marks them.)

Product Q&A, menus and other modules

Products and categories are in the kernel’s object directory, so other modules can point at them without reading catalog tables:

  • catalog.product: public when on sale (active) with a text in the language asked; title, short description, address /<prefix>/<slug> and first image. Product questions and answers use module comments with this target type. Suggested settings: AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_TARGET_TYPES including catalog.product, AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFIED_ONLY_TYPES=catalog.product (verified accounts only, Decree 147/2024 — check the scope with the original text) and AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_MODERATION_BY_TYPE=catalog.product:user=pre (questions wait for review). Archiving or deleting a product closes and hides its questions. An author who can manage the product (catalog.products.write on its unit) gets the badge seller; module orders adds verified_buyer.
  • catalog.category: for website menus (module menus) — names and addresses (/categories/<slug>) by language, children in display order, only visible categories. A “best sellers” block in a menu is the public product list filtered by category and sorted best_selling.

Image texts by language: PUT /products/{id}/media/{media_id}/alts/{locale} {"alt": "…"} (with If-Match; DELETE removes it). Product pages in that language show it; otherwise the product’s own alt in its default language, then the media library’s text in that language. Removing an image from the product removes its texts.

What differs between variants

PUT /variants/{id}/attributes sets attribute values on one variant — how many people it serves, what is in the box, care instructions, dishwasher safe — using the tenant’s attributes (POST /attributes), so nothing is fixed to one trade. Text values may carry translations: {"attribute_id": …, "value": "Rửa tay", "texts": {"en": "Hand wash"}}. The public product page lists them under each variant (variants[].attributes) in the language asked.

Digital products

A product of kind digital is delivered as download links instead of being shipped (plan feature catalog.digital).

  1. Upload the file with POST /api/v1/files (or a direct upload, /api/v1/files/uploads).
  2. Attach it to the variant: POST /variants/{id}/digital-assets {"file_id": …, "download_limit": 5, "grant_days": 30} (catalog.products.write). The content is copied, so deleting the uploaded file later does not affect buyers. A digital product cannot go on sale without a file (catalog.digital_asset_missing).
  3. When module orders confirms a paid order (orders.order_confirmed with payment_status paid), each order line of a digital variant gets one download right per file: download_limit downloads, valid grant_days days. Receiving the event again gives nothing more. Cancelling the order, or a refund not tied to a return, revokes the rights at once.
  4. Buyers with an account list their rights with GET /downloads and spend one with POST /downloads/{id}. Staff with catalog.downloads.manage see an order’s rights (GET /orders/{id}/downloads), revoke them (POST /orders/{id}/downloads/revoke) or give new tokens to send to a buyer without an account (POST /orders/{id}/downloads/reissue, the only time a token_path is shown).
  5. Spending a download (POST /public/downloads/{token}, no sign-in) answers a signed file address valid AUTOXIDE_CATALOG_DOWNLOAD_LINK_SECONDS; it accepts Range to resume and does not spend more downloads. Addresses are signed with a key of the tenant: one tenant’s address does not work on another’s domain.

Services (service) are neither shipped nor stocked; bundles (bundle) take stock from each component (PUT /variants/{id}/components); pre-orders use the variant’s sale_mode.

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_CATALOG_LOCALESen,viLanguages product and category texts may be written in

Comments

Tiếng Việt: COMMENTS.vi.md

The comments module lets people comment on anything the website shows — a post, a page, a media item — by its kind and id (target_type, target_id). Threads have two levels: a top-level comment and its replies (a reply to a reply joins the same thread and remembers whom it answers). Signed-in users and guests can comment; every comment goes through a fixed chain of checks and, by default, guests wait for approval. People can report comments, moderators approve, reject, mark as spam, ban and close targets, and authors may change their comment for a short while and delete it at any time. It is API only: the website shows the comment box; the admin screens are a separate project. It lives under /api/v1/comments. The full contract is in openapi.json.

No third-party account is needed: spam is stopped by the core’s shared anti-spam layer (a hidden trap field, a signed form token, rate limits, duplicate detection; an optional self-hosted proof-of-work challenge) plus the module’s own word lists and link limit.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
comments.postCommenting while signed in, changing and deleting one’s own comments, one’s display name
comments.readReading every comment in any status, with author emails, network fingerprints and reports
comments.moderateApproving, rejecting, marking as spam, holding again; deleting for good
comments.manageBanning and unbanning; opening, closing and hiding targets
comments.exportExporting and erasing every comment written with an email address

Guests need none: everything under /api/v1/comments/public/ is open.

Targets

AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_TARGET_TYPES (default content.entry) lists the kinds that take comments. When another module resolves a kind (the content module resolves content.entry), a comment is only taken when the target exists and is public; other kinds are taken as given. A target gets its row on its first comment, holding its state (open / closed, hidden, closes_at) and its counts. The module owning a kind declares which of its events close or remove a target: when content archives an entry its comments close; when it deletes one they are also hidden. AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_AUTO_CLOSE_DAYS closes targets some days after their first comment.

Questions and answers

The same threads serve as product questions: a question is a top-level comment, answers are its replies. A module owning the target may give authors badges, computed when the comment is written and returned as stable codes in badges (e.g. seller for someone who manages the product, verified_buyer for someone who received it); show your own label for each code.

  • Search a target’s questions: GET /api/v1/comments/public/threads?target_type=…&target_id=…&q=bảo hành — ignores case and accents; matches with the exact accents come first.
  • Tab counts: GET /api/v1/comments/public/counts returns thread_count (shown questions) next to count (all shown comments); the target answers thread_count too, and moderators also get pending_thread_count.
  • Unanswered questions (no shown reply yet): GET /api/v1/comments?status=published&unanswered=true.
  • AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFIED_ONLY_TYPES lists kinds where only verified accounts may ask or answer: guests are refused and signed-in users are checked with the module that keeps account verification (comments.verification_required, 403). With no such module installed, every signed-in account counts as verified.

Verified accounts (Vietnam, Decree 147/2024)

The compliance module keeps account verification and answers the question for this module:

  • Levels: none, phone (a Vietnamese mobile number confirmed with a 6-digit code sent by SMS) and identity (a verified identity profile, GET /api/v1/compliance/me/kyc; it includes phone). A user sees their level with GET /api/v1/compliance/me/verification (MCP compliance.account_verification).
  • Verifying a phone: POST /api/v1/compliance/me/phone-verifications {"phone": "0912 345 678"} sends the code (landlines and foreign numbers get compliance.phone_not_allowed), then POST /api/v1/compliance/me/phone-verifications/{id}/confirm {"code": "123456"}. A code works once, expires (AUTOXIDE_COMPLIANCE_OTP_TTL_SECONDS, 5 minutes) and allows a few wrong tries (AUTOXIDE_COMPLIANCE_OTP_MAX_ATTEMPTS); codes per number, account and address are limited. One number verifies one account unless the tenant raises the posting.max_accounts_per_phone policy (compliance.phone_in_use). DELETE /api/v1/compliance/me/phone removes the number. Sending needs an SMS provider; without one the server answers sms_disabled (503). No real SMS provider ships yet — install a connector module for yours.
  • How the two settings combine:
    • Kinds in AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFIED_ONLY_TYPES need at least phone, or the level of the tenant’s posting.comments policy when that is higher (identity).
    • When the tenant sets posting.comments to phone or identity (PUT /api/v1/compliance/policies/posting.comments, permission compliance.policies.manage), every kind needs that level, and guests can no longer comment anywhere.
    • posting.comments = none (the default) leaves other kinds as they are.
    • A refused post answers comments.verification_required (403); send the user to verify, then post again.

The website

  1. GET /api/v1/comments/public/settings — limits and switches (guests allowed, edit minutes, maximum length, whether reply mails are on, whether Markdown is on).
  2. GET /api/v1/comments/public/threads?target_type=content.entry&target_id=…&order=desc&limit=20&replies_limit=3 — shown top-level comments with their first replies and reply_count; follow pagination.next_cursor. More replies: GET /api/v1/comments/public/comments/{id}/replies. Counts for a list page: GET /api/v1/comments/public/counts?target_type=content.entry&target_ids=a,b,c (up to 100). Whether the box is open: GET /api/v1/comments/public/targets/{type}/{id}.
  3. Show body_html (everything escaped, line breaks as <br>, http(s) addresses as links with rel="nofollow ugc noopener"); never insert body as HTML. Label guests as guests (author.kind). See “Text and Markdown” below.
  4. Each time the box is shown (never in cached HTML): GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=comments:content.entry. Show a hidden trap input that people leave empty.
  5. POST /api/v1/comments/public/comments:
{"target_type": "content.entry", "target_id": "0190…", "parent_id": null,
 "body": "Nice post!\nThanks.", "author_name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com",
 "notify_replies": true, "locale": "en", "form_token": "…", "trap": ""}
  • The answer is 201 with the comment, status (published, or pending: waiting for approval) and, for guests, an edit_token shown only here. A comment held for approval, held as spam or dropped by the anti-spam checks all answer pending: bots learn nothing.
  • Wrong input: 422 with every problem in errors (empty body, too long, reserved name, bad email…). A banned word: 422 comments.banned_word. A missing or expired token: 400 antispam.token_* — reload the form. A closed target: 409 comments.target_closed. A banned author: 403 comments.banned.
  • Sending the same form_token again returns the same comment (with a new edit_token; the first one stops working) and stores nothing new.
  • Signed-in users send their access token instead of a form token, need comments.post, and first choose a display name with PUT /api/v1/comments/profile {"display_name": "…"}.
  • Names (a guest’s author_name, a display name) take 1 to 50 characters, without control characters, invisible formatting characters (soft hyphen, direction marks, tag characters…), blank-looking letters (Hangul fillers and the like), or a word mixing Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters (аdmin with a Cyrillic а). Letters that look alike across scripts in whole words (a name written entirely in Cyrillic) are not caught.
  • Change: PATCH /api/v1/comments/public/comments/{id} {"body": "…", "edit_token": "…"} within AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_EDIT_MINUTES. The text is checked again, and the answer’s status says whether the comment is still shown: a shown comment waits for approval again when it now has suspect words or too many links, or when a new comment of the same author on that target would wait (mode pre, or first_time while the account has no shown comment) — so by default a guest’s change always waits for approval again. Delete: POST /api/v1/comments/public/comments/{id}/delete {"edit_token": "…"} (signed-in authors send {}) — text, name and email go, the place in the thread stays. An id that does not exist also answers 200, so a dropped comment cannot be told from a held one by deleting it. Changing one can: PATCH with the fake id of a dropped comment answers 404 comments.not_found (a known limit; it tells a bot only that this one comment was dropped).
  • Report: POST /api/v1/comments/public/comments/{id}/reports {"reason": "spam" | "abuse" | "illegal" | "other", "note": "…"}. Each account reports a comment once; guests are counted by network block (/24 for IPv4, /48 for IPv6).

Text and Markdown

A comment is sent with format: text (the default) or markdown, the latter only when GET /api/v1/comments/public/settings says markdown: true (AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_MARKDOWN, on by default; when off, markdown is refused on the field format). An edit without format keeps the comment’s format. Old comments are text and show as before.

  • text: plain text. A * stays a *; line breaks are kept; http(s) addresses become links.
  • markdown: a small part of Markdown — **bold**, *italics*, [links](https://…) and <https://…>, > quotes, `code` and code blocks. Headings and list items show as paragraphs; images show as their text (no image is ever loaded); raw HTML shows as text. Only http(s) links work, all with rel="nofollow ugc noopener".

The server builds body_html from a fixed list of tags (p, br, strong, em, a, blockquote, code, pre), so the website inserts body_html as it is in either format. Markdown links count towards AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_MAX_LINKS like bare addresses. Banned words are checked on the text as written.

Moderation

The checks run in this order: target closed → length → content (control and invisible characters refused) → duplicate → bans → banned words (refused) / suspect words (held) → too many links (held) → anti-spam → approval mode. Modes are pre (every comment waits), first_time (until the account has a comment that is shown now — one approved and later marked as spam or rejected does not count) and post (shown at once); defaults are pre for guests and first_time for users, and both can be set per target kind (AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_MODERATION_BY_TYPE). A guest’s email is never proof of who they are — anyone can type any address — so it never lets a comment skip approval, even once confirmed.

  • GET /api/v1/comments?status=pending&target_type=&target_id=&q= — the queue (q searches text and names ignoring case and accents), with emails, network fingerprints, hold reasons and report counts. Each comment carries target_title and target_url when the target’s module can describe it and the target is public.
  • GET /api/v1/comments/targets?target_type=&state=open|closed&pending=true|false — the targets that have comments, newest first, with their counts and (when public) title and url.
  • PATCH /api/v1/comments/{id} {"status": "published" | "rejected" | "spam" | "pending"} with If-Match. DELETE /api/v1/comments/{id} deletes for good (a top-level comment with its thread).
  • Reaching AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_REPORT_THRESHOLD reports holds a shown comment once; after a moderator approves it, more reports do not hide it. A comment held this way stays in the queue until a moderator decides: the cleanup never deletes a comment that was once shown. GET /api/v1/comments/{id}/reports.
  • POST /api/v1/comments/bans {"kind": "user" | "email" | "ip", "value": "…", "reason": "…", "until": null} (ip takes the comment’s ip_fingerprint), GET, DELETE /api/v1/comments/bans/{id}.
  • PUT /api/v1/comments/targets/{type}/{id} {"state": "closed", "hidden": false, "closes_at": null}.

Every decision is an event (comments.comment_status_changed, comments.comment_deleted, comments.ban_created, comments.target_closed…) that the audit module records with who and when.

Hidden by a case

A comment can be the target of a case of the compliance module (comments.comment:<id>; comments registers this type in the kernel’s resource directory, with the author as owner). When the case hides it (event compliance.target_restricted), the comment becomes rejected with hold reason compliance and remembers its former status; compliance.target_restored puts that status back. Meanwhile moderators cannot change its status (comments.restricted, 409). See COMPLIANCE.md.

Reply mails

Off until both AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFY_URL and AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL are set. With notify_replies: true and an email, a confirmation mail goes to that address (at most AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFY_MAILS_PER_DAY); the website page sends its token to POST /api/v1/comments/public/verify. From then on, each shown reply to that comment mails the address with the target’s title and link — never the reply’s text or the replier’s name, so the feature cannot carry spam — and a link whose token goes to POST /api/v1/comments/public/unsubscribe ("all": true stops every comment followed with that address).

On a server with several tenants, a token may start with t<tenant id>.: it names the tenant itself, so the verify and unsubscribe calls work on any host of the API without the Autoxide-Tenant header. Send tokens back exactly as received (they may contain a .).

Personal data

  • GET /api/v1/comments/data?email=… lists, and DELETE /api/v1/comments/data?email=… clears, every comment written with an address (permission comments.export): text, name, email and network fingerprint go, the place in the thread stays, reply mails stop. Bans of the address are kept (they exist to keep it out); lift them by hand if asked.
  • Network addresses are never stored: only a keyed hash of the network block, cleared after AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_IP_RETENTION_DAYS — from comments and from guests’ reports (the report stays, its reporter_key becomes expired:<report id>).
  • Comments waiting for approval or spam that were never shown are deleted AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_RETENTION_DAYS after they were posted. A comment that was shown once and went back to waiting (held after reports, changed by its author, held again or marked as spam by a moderator) is never deleted on its own: a moderator approves, rejects or deletes it.
  • Events (and so webhooks) carry ids, targets and statuses only, never text, names or addresses.
  • When an account is deleted, its comments are cleared the same way, its display name is deleted and its reports no longer point to it. The account’s data export includes its comments, display name and reports.

Legal

What the law asks of comments depends on where you and your readers are. The module gives you settings, not rules written in the code; the texts below were not checked against the original legal texts — check them for your case before you rely on them.

  • Vietnam, Decree 147/2024/ND-CP (internet services): as read from secondary sources, social networks may only let accounts verified by a Vietnamese phone number comment; licensed general news sites may not be allowed reader comments at all; content that breaks the law must be taken down within 24 hours of a request from the authorities, and some services must keep moderation records (2 years is mentioned). The module offers AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_ENABLED, AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_ALLOW_GUESTS, AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_SIGNED_IN_ONLY_TYPES, closing or hiding a target, deleting for good (DELETE /api/v1/comments/{id}, recorded with who and when in the audit log), and the illegal report reason. AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_VERIFIED_ONLY_TYPES asks the module that keeps phone or identity verification (not this module) before taking a comment. How long the audit log is kept is set by the audit module.
  • Vietnam, Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15 and Decree 356/2025: people may ask for their data and its erasure; the module exports and clears by email and by account, keeps network data only as a hash and for a set time. Check the deadlines for answering requests, and whether keeping moderation records after an erasure (ids, actions and times only) is enough for you.
  • Elsewhere: for example the EU GDPR (data subject rights) and the Digital Services Act (notice and action for illegal content).

AI agents (MCP)

Tools comments.queue and comments.get (comments.read), comments.moderate (comments.moderate; pass the version you read, like If-Match) and comments.set_target_state (comments.manage), with the same permissions and checks as REST. For questions: comments.unanswered (comments.read) lists shown questions without a shown answer, and comments.answer (comments.post) answers one as the caller — like a signed-in user on the website, with the same badges, verification and moderation (set a display name first with PUT /api/v1/comments/profile). There is no tool to start a thread (that is for readers on the website) and no tool to delete a comment for good (use REST).

Per tenant

With several tenants, the settings above are the default of every tenant. A tenant can replace some of them with its own (its administrator with PUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}, permission kernel.settings.manage; platform staff with PUT /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/settings/{name}):
