A wrong value is refused when it is set (422, the problem in errors). Overrides per target kind (AUTOXIDE_COMMENTS_MODERATION_BY_TYPE) still win over a tenant’s moderation mode. DELETE the setting to go back to the server’s value. GET /api/v1/comments/public/settings answers with the tenant’s own max_links.

Compatibility policy

English · Tiếng Việt

This page says what you can rely on when you upgrade Autoxide, and what may change. It applies from version 1.0.0. Before 1.0 (0.x) a minor release (0.18 → 0.19) may break any of the contracts below, the HTTP API included; every break is listed under Changed or Removed in CHANGELOG.md with what to do instead. From 1.0.0 the rules below apply in full: nothing in /api/v1 breaks.

Autoxide uses Semantic Versioning: one version number for the server, the Rust crates and the TypeScript SDK.

ReleaseExampleMay contain
Patch1.4.0 → 1.4.1Bug and security fixes. No new features, no new settings to set.
Minor1.4.1 → 1.5.0New features, new endpoints, new settings, deprecations. No breaks.
Major1.9.3 → 2.0.0Breaking changes, each one listed with what to do instead.

A “break” is any change after which a client, an installation or a module that followed the documentation stops working without being changed.

What is a stable contract

Everything in this section belongs to the core and official modules (docs/MODULES.md). Experimental modules are excluded (see What is not covered).

REST API and OpenAPI

The contract is docs/openapi.json, served at /api/v1/openapi.json.

  • Within /api/v1 nothing breaks, in any release: no endpoint is removed or renamed, no required input is added, no response field is removed or changes type, no status code changes meaning.
  • A change that would break clients is made as a new endpoint. The old one keeps working exactly as before and is declared deprecated (Module::deprecations): the OpenAPI document marks it deprecated, and its responses carry the Deprecation, Sunset and Link headers (RFC 9745, RFC 8594) pointing to the replacement.
  • A deprecated endpoint is removed only after its sunset date, which is at least six months after the release that deprecated it and never in a patch release.
  • Minor releases may add: endpoints, optional request fields, query parameters, response fields, headers, and new values in enums of responses. Clients must ignore response fields they do not know and treat an unknown enum value as “other”.
  • A new /api/v2 would only appear in a major release, and /api/v1 would keep running alongside it for at least one more major release.
  • cargo xtask api-diff checks every change against the last release in the gate, and fails on a break.

Error codes

The code field of an error (notes.title_taken, validation_failed…) is a contract for programs.

  • A code is never renamed, and never reused with another meaning.
  • A request that failed with a given code fails with the same code after a minor release.
  • New codes may be added in a minor release, for new failures. Clients must handle codes they do not know as the HTTP status says.
  • The message text, its translations and errors[].detail are for people and may change in any release.

Configuration

Environment variables (.env.example lists all of them), their meaning and their default values.

  • A setting is never removed or renamed in a minor release. When a name has to change, the new name is added and the old name keeps working, with a warning in the startup log that names the new one, for at least one minor release and at least six months; it goes away only in a major release.
  • A default value that changes behaviour (for example a stricter limit) changes only in a major release, unless it fixes a security problem; then the changelog says so under Security.
  • New settings always have a default, so an existing .env keeps working.
  • The same rules apply to AUTOXIDE_MODULES: a module never moves from official to experimental (which would turn it off by default) within a major version.

Database and migrations

  • A newer release always reads the data of an older one: start the new binary (or run autoxide migrate up) and migrations bring the database forward. Upgrading from any 1.x to any later 1.x works directly, without stopping at each minor release. The CI tests this upgrade from the previous release on both SQLite and PostgreSQL.
  • A migration that was released is never edited; changes come as new migrations.
  • Every migration has a down step, so you can go back to the previous release: with the new binary, run autoxide migrate down <module> --steps <n> for each migration it added (the changelog and autoxide migrate status show which), then start the old binary. Take a backup first; going down may drop data that only the new release stores.
  • SQLite and PostgreSQL are both supported in every release. Support for a PostgreSQL major version that its upstream project no longer maintains may end in a minor release, announced in the changelog one minor release ahead.
  • The tables themselves are not a contract: they belong to their module and may change shape in any release. Read and write data through the API, not with SQL.

MCP tools

The tool list (docs/mcp-tools.json, served by the MCP endpoint) follows the REST rules: a tool keeps its name, accepts every input it accepted and returns every field it returned. A tool that has to change is replaced by a new tool and deprecated with a sunset date (Deprecation::tool), at least six months ahead. A tool never needs a broader permission than before.

Events and webhooks

Event names and the fields of their payloads (what modules receive and what webhooks deliver) may gain fields in a minor release, but never lose or retype one. An event that has to change shape is published under a new name, and the old one keeps being published until the next major release.

Command line

The autoxide commands and options that the documentation describes, their exit codes, and the output of --json options follow the same rules as configuration: added in minor releases, removed or changed only in a major release. Text printed for people may change.

Rust API for modules

For people who write modules in their own repository (guide), the contract is the public Rust API of:

  • autoxide-kernel and autoxide-testkit;
  • autoxide::Autoxide, the only public item of the autoxide crate;
  • pub mod api and pub fn module(…) of every core and official module crate.

Rules, as in Cargo’s SemVer guide:

  • A breaking change (removing or renaming a public item, changing a function signature, adding a required trait method without a default, …) happens only in a major release.
  • Before it is removed, an item is marked #[deprecated] with a note naming the replacement, for at least one minor release.
  • New features for modules arrive as new trait methods with a default implementation, so existing modules compile unchanged.
  • cargo-semver-checks compares these crates with the previous release on every pull request that touches them and on every release pull request; from 1.0 a break fails the check.
  • The libraries whose types appear in this API (axum, sea-orm, utoipa, tokio, serde… — the table in docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md) are part of it: moving one of them to a new major version is a breaking change, so it waits for a major release.
  • The minimum supported Rust version follows recent stable Rust (rust-toolchain.toml). Raising it happens only in a minor release, never in a patch release, and is listed in the changelog.

TypeScript SDK

The SDK (sdk/typescript) is generated from docs/openapi.json and carries the same version. It follows the REST rules: a minor release adds methods and optional fields; a method or type disappears only in a major release. Deprecated endpoints stay in the SDK until their sunset date.

What is not covered

These may change in any release, including patch releases where it fixes a bug:

  • Experimental modules (tier experimental in docs/MODULES.md, off by default): their endpoints, tools, events, settings and Rust API may change between minor releases, breaking changes included. Every change is in the changelog, and moving their data to a new release is described in the upgrade notes when it needs a manual step.
  • Anything marked experimental elsewhere: OpenAPI operations with "x-stability": "experimental", MCP tools with "stability": "experimental", and features whose documentation says “experimental”.
  • Rust items that are not public: pub(crate) and private items, #[doc(hidden)] items, and everything in a module crate outside api and module(…). The sample module notes and the xtask crate are not part of the contract at all.
  • Log lines: their format, messages and fields. Metric names and labels follow the changelog but are not frozen.
  • Human-readable text: error messages, translations, descriptions in OpenAPI and MCP, CLI output without --json.
  • Database tables, columns and indexes (see above), the order of items where the API does not promise one, and performance figures.

Building from source

Minimum supported Rust version (MSRV)

The MSRV is the rust-version of the workspace Cargo.toml (today the release before the pinned toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml). Policy:

  • The repository builds and its library crates compile with the MSRV; CI has a job that builds the workspace with exactly that version, so a newer language feature cannot slip in unnoticed.
  • The pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml, used by developers, CI and the Docker image) is newer than the MSRV and moves forward with stable Rust; the MSRV is raised only when a dependency or a feature needs it, never in a patch release, and the raise is listed in the changelog.
  • Modules in other repositories need at least the MSRV. The external-module example uses the same rust-version (checked by cargo xtask check).

Cargo features

The default build has every feature a production server needs. These optional features exist:

CrateFeatureWhat it doesIn releasesContract
autoxideavifAVIF thumbnails (AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AVIF); pulls the rav1e encoderOffStable
autoxidebench-seedtask <module>.bench_seed generates sample data for measurementsOffNone
autoxide-kernelpermission-auditTest-only: builds routes without the permission layer for auditsOffNone
module cratestestingTest helpers a module shares with autoxide-testkitOffNone
module cratesbench-seed, avifForwarded from the autoxide features aboveOffAs above

“None” means not part of the compatibility promise: never enable these in an application. Features are additive; a new feature never changes the default build.

Reproducible builds

The release image is built with the aim that the same source gives the same binary. This is a goal: no automated test builds twice and compares yet, so do not rely on byte-for-byte identity. What is in place:

  • Cargo.lock is committed and every release build uses --locked; the toolchain is pinned (rust-toolchain.toml, the Docker RUST_VERSION), and the base images are pinned by digest.
  • The Dockerfile builds in a fixed directory and passes --remap-path-prefix so no build path ends up in the binary, and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH (the commit time of the release) is used for every timestamp, including the release archives (sorted, with fixed owner and modification time).
  • To compare a release with your own build: rebuild from the tag with the same Dockerfile, copy /usr/local/bin/autoxide out of your image, unpack the release archive (tar -xzf autoxide-X.Y.Z-<target>.tar.gz) and compare sha256sum of the two autoxide files. (SHA256SUMS lists the archives, not the binary inside.) A difference is not proof of tampering: a different base image digest or target architecture also changes the binary. docs/VERIFYING.md shows how to verify signatures and attestations, which is the supported check.

Software bill of materials (SBOM)

Every release carries two lists of what is inside:

  • Rust crates in the binary. The binary is built with cargo auditable, which embeds the exact dependency list in the executable. Tools such as cargo audit bin autoxide, Syft, Trivy or Grype read it, so a vulnerability scanner sees the Rust crates even in a stripped binary.
  • CycloneDX file. autoxide.cdx.json (CycloneDX 1.5, generated from Cargo.lock by cargo cyclonedx) is attached to the GitHub Release and attested; the image also carries an SPDX SBOM (sbom.spdx.json).

Support

From 1.0 each major version has long-term support:

  • The latest minor release gets every fix; the previous minor release gets security fixes for 3 months after the next minor release; when a new major version comes out, the last minor release of the previous major version gets security fixes for 6 months. Older releases are not patched. The table is in SECURITY.md.
  • Backporting. A fix is made on main first. For a supported older line, a maintainer cherry-picks it onto a release/X.Y branch cut from the latest vX.Y.Z tag, ships it as the next patch release (X.Y.Z+1) with only that fix, and runs the full gate on both databases first. A patch release never contains new features, new required settings or contract changes, so it is safe to install on its own.
  • Compatibility between versions of the database (which version you can upgrade from, manual steps) is stated in the changelog of each release. How releases are made is in docs/RELEASING.md (in Vietnamese).

Compliance (Vietnam)

Tiếng Việt

The compliance module helps a tenant run a commerce website in Vietnam without missing the basic legal duties. It is always on (it is not sold by plan). Every legal point that changes over time — lists of documents, deadlines, which logo domain is accepted — is data with an effective date (rules in modules/compliance/rules/vn.json, imported into the database), not code.

Not legal advice. The rules, checklists and templates shipped here were written from secondary sources. Every item says needs_legal_review: true: check it against the original legal text, with a legal professional, before you rely on it.

What the module covers:

PartEndpoints (under /api/v1/compliance)
Identity verification (KYC) of sellers, livestreamers, affiliates — profiles, checks and the gate KycGate; on a marketplace, catalog blocks listing goods of unverified sellers (see below)/kyc/…, /me/kyc…
Account verification for posting (phone / identity)/me/verification, /me/phone-verifications…
Versioned legal documents and proof of acceptance/documents…, /me/acceptances, /public/documents/{kind}
Consent ledger/me/consents
Personal data: purposes and legal bases, retention, processing register, data residency/purposes…, /retention, /processing-register, /residency, /public/purposes
Personal data breaches (72 hours) and data subject requests from other channels/incidents…, /subject-requests…
Tracking tags and cookie consent/tracking-tags…, /cookie-settings/{org_id}, /public/consent-config, /public/cookie-consents
Reports of infringements (intellectual property, counterfeit) and consumer complaints, disclosures to authorities/cases…, /respondent/cases, /disclosures, /public/reports, /public/complaints, /public/cases/{id}
Legal rules with effective dates, tenant policies/rules, /policies…
Website legal profile and the Ministry of Industry and Trade (MOIT)/legal-profiles…, /websites…, /public/badge, /public/owner

This guide explains the Ministry of Industry and Trade procedure with the mandatory page templates of content, then personal data (with the 72-hour breach runbook), reports of infringements with consumer complaints, and tracking tags with cookie consent.

The Ministry of Industry and Trade procedure

Vietnamese law (from 1 July 2026 the E-commerce Law 122/2025/QH15 and Decree 248/2026/ND-CP, which replaces Decrees 52/2013/ND-CP and 85/2021/ND-CP; before that, those two decrees — check the originals) requires the items below. The rules moit.checklist.* version 2 apply from 1 July 2026. A website notified or registered before then files again under the new decree within the transition period (one summary says 30 June 2027 — not confirmed); electronic identity checks of sellers and livestreamers apply from 1 January 2027. Which authority receives the files, whether online.gov.vn and the logos stay, is not confirmed yet — check.

  • a sales website (you sell your own goods) to be notified to the ministry — it then shows a blue “Đã thông báo Bộ Công Thương” logo;
  • a marketplace or other intermediary (others sell through you) to be registered — red “Đã đăng ký Bộ Công Thương” logo; the file includes a service project plan and operating regulations;
  • the website to show the owner’s information and its policies (general conditions, shipping, payment, returns, inspection, personal data protection, complaints).

A person submits on online.gov.vn; there is no public API. Autoxide keeps the data, tells you what is missing, drafts the dossier and shows the logo once you record the result.

1. Legal profile of the owner

One profile per organization unit. The tenant’s own profile belongs to the root unit (leave org_id out); a seller on a marketplace gets a profile on its unit. A website uses the profile of its own unit, or of the nearest unit above that has one.

POST /api/v1/compliance/legal-profiles
{
  "entity_type": "organization",
  "legal_name": "Cong ty TNHH Vi Du",
  "tax_code": "0101234567",
  "registration_number": "0101234567",
  "registration_issued_on": "2020-01-02",
  "registration_issued_by": "Phong Dang ky kinh doanh Ha Noi",
  "address": {"country": "VN", "province_code": "01", "commune_code": "00004", "line": "12 Trang Tien"},
  "representative_name": "Nguyen Van A",
  "phone": "024 1234 5678",
  "email": "lienhe@shop.example"
}
  • entity_type: individual, household_business or organization.
  • The address is checked against the administrative units of the address module (import them first: autoxide task address.import).
  • PATCH /legal-profiles/{id} changes some fields ("" clears a text, null clears address); send If-Match with the ETag you read.
  • kyc_profile_id links the owner’s identity verification; a marketplace checklist needs it verified.

Permissions: compliance.legal.read, compliance.legal.manage. Both have a scope: a seller’s staff see and change only their unit’s profile and websites.

2. Website

POST /api/v1/compliance/websites
{"domain": "shop.example", "kind": "sales"}
  • kind: sales (notification) or platform (registration). Changing kind later starts the procedure again.
  • channel: website (default) or mobile_app.
  • org_id: the unit of the website (e.g. a seller’s own store); left out, the whole tenant.

3. Mandatory pages

Write each page in content — the templates in the next section give a starting text — publish it, then link it to the website:

PUT /api/v1/compliance/websites/{id}/pages/return_policy
{"entry_id": "<id of the content entry>"}

Page kinds: owner_info, privacy_policy, return_policy, shipping_policy, payment_policy, inspection_policy, complaint_policy, terms_of_use, general_conditions, and for a marketplace platform_rules, seller_agreement. A linked page counts only once it is published.

4. Checklist

GET /api/v1/compliance/websites/{id}/checklist (MCP compliance.website_checklist) lists every item of the rule moit.checklist.sales or moit.checklist.platform in force, each with a status:

StatusMeaning
metDone.
missingTo do; hint says which endpoint to call.
unknownAutoxide cannot tell yet (e.g. no installed module answers “each product page shows its seller”) — check it yourself.
manualAlways checked by a person (e.g. your account on online.gov.vn).

Each item carries its legal_basis. When the rules change, platform staff import a new version (POST /api/v1/compliance/rules) and the checklist follows — no upgrade needed.

Selling before the procedure is done is shown as “required by law” (selling_before_done: "label"), not blocked: the sources found treat it as an administrative offence with fines, not as a ban on transactions. Check this with a legal professional (decision D-358).

5. Dossier

GET /api/v1/compliance/websites/{id}/dossier (MCP compliance.website_dossier) returns, filled from your data:

  • form: the declaration fields (owner, website, identity verification, linked pages with full URLs, complaints contact);
  • documents: Markdown drafts in Vietnamese — the declaration; for a marketplace also a draft service project plan and draft operating regulations;
  • checklist and a disclaimer.

Complete and review the drafts with a legal professional, then submit on online.gov.vn.

6. Status and logo

Record each step by hand:

POST /api/v1/compliance/websites/{id}/status
{"status": "submitted", "reference": "HS-001"}

Statuses: not_submitted, submitted, needs_supplement, notified (sales website), registered (marketplace), rejected, revoked. For notified / registered, paste the logo code the ministry gave in snippet (or send link_url and image_url). Only a link to online.gov.vn around an image from online.gov.vn is accepted — scripts, event handlers, styles or other domains give compliance.logo_snippet_invalid (422). The code is never stored or returned as sent: Autoxide keeps the two addresses and rebuilds a clean snippet.

7. For the interface (public, no sign-in)

EndpointReturns
GET /api/v1/compliance/public/badgeThe logo of the website being viewed: color (blue / red), link_url, image_url, alt, ready snippet. 404 while the website has no logo.
GET /api/v1/compliance/public/ownerThe owner’s information for the footer. 404 without a legal profile.

The website is found by ?domain=, then the request’s domain, then the website of the unit being viewed (?site=<unit id> or a domain bound to a unit). Both send an ETag; send it back in If-None-Match to get 304.

8. autoxide doctor

The check compliance.moit_readiness warns (never fails) when no website has a legal profile yet, or when a website not yet submitted still lacks checklist items — with the checklist address of each.

Mandatory page templates (content)

The content module ships starting texts for the mandatory pages, in English and Vietnamese:

GET  /api/v1/content/templates
POST /api/v1/content/templates/{key}/drafts
{"locale": "vi", "variables": {"policy": {"return_days": 7}}}
  • Keys: owner_info, privacy_policy, return_policy, shipping_policy, payment_policy, inspection_policy, complaint_policy, terms_of_use, general_conditions; for a marketplace platform_rules, seller_agreement, seller_info.
  • The draft is filled with the legal profile of the unit (owner.*, contact.*, read from compliance), then with the variables you send (they win). Every value goes into text only — it can never add markup. A required variable still missing gives content.template_variables_missing (422) listing them all.
  • The result is a draft page (content.write); review it, publish it, then link it to the website.
  • Every template starts with “Sample content — have a legal professional review it before use”.

Personal data

Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15 and Decree 356/2025/ND-CP (in force from 1 January 2026 — check the originals with a legal professional). Each tenant is the data controller of its own data.

Purposes and legal bases

GET /purposes (compliance.privacy.read) lists the purposes of processing: the defaults of the legal rule privacy.default_purposes (service, marketing, analytics, legal) merged with the tenant’s own. POST /purposes adds one, PATCH /purposes/{key} changes one (changing a default stores the tenant’s version) — both need compliance.privacy.manage. Each purpose has a category, a legal_basis (consent, contract, legal_obligation, vital_interest, public_interest), the kinds of data, the recipients (name, country) and a description by language. GET /public/purposes (no sign-in) lists the purposes in use for the privacy notice; active tracking providers appear there as recipients, with the country that receives the data.

Retention

Every module declares the personal data it keeps and for how long (Module::retention, read from its settings). GET /retention lists them, each compared with the legal rule privacy.retention_limits: ok, exceeds_limit or forever_not_allowed (only accounting — proof the law requires — may be kept forever). The limits shipped are cautious defaults, not numbers from the law. autoxide doctor warns (compliance.retention) when an item is not ok; lower the setting named in setting.

Processing register

GET /processing-register returns purposes, legal bases, kinds of data, recipients, retention and where the data is kept — the input of a data protection impact assessment, whose official form needs a legal professional.

Not covered yet (before 1.0)

Findings of the first legal review (AI-performed, not legal advice; docs/legal/review-2026-11-r1/) that core does not handle yet. Until they are done, the deployer covers them:

  • Seller identity before selling. The legal rule kyc.required_activities asks for verified sellers, livestreamers and affiliates (E-commerce Law 122/2025/QH15; Decree 248/2026/ND-CP Article 18, electronic identity of sellers from 1 January 2027 — check the originals). When the tenant is a marketplace (kernel.business_model = marketplace), catalog asks KycGate before a product of a seller (any branch other than the tenant’s root) goes active. The seller is the owning branch or a branch above it, below the root (marketplace → seller → store): one verified branch in that chain is enough. An unverified seller gets compliance.kyc_required (403); goods of the root and tenants that sell their own goods are not asked. If module compliance is turned off (for example AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,-compliance), identity cannot be checked, so goods of a seller cannot go on sale on a marketplace (catalog.seller_verification_unavailable, 403). Only the change to active is checked: goods already on sale stay on sale when the tenant becomes a marketplace, the rule starts to apply or a seller’s verification expires or is revoked — stop them yourself (POST /api/v1/catalog/products/{id}/status). A marketplace that gives each seller its own child tenant instead of a branch is not checked this way: each child tenant sells its own goods. Still open: livestream and affiliate flows (no module yet), and the profile does not record every item Article 18 lists — individuals: full name, date of birth, personal identification number (one source adds residential address); organisations and household businesses: name, head office, identification number, legal representative; foreign individuals: passport (or equivalent) number and issuing country, valid at least 6 more months at review. The profile keeps the verified name and a hash and last 4 digits of the document; the other items stay with the eKYC provider. Check the originals before relying on this.
  • Personal data of children. Law 91/2025/QH15 sets special rules for children and persons under guardianship (consent of a parent or guardian; from age 7 also the child’s — the article and ages need checking). Core has no birth date, age check or guardian consent: a service aimed at children must collect and keep the guardian’s consent itself. Planned after 1.0: a per-tenant setting, self-declared age at sign-up and consent given on someone’s behalf in the consent ledger.
  • Data sent abroad by providers. The AI providers of module ai, mail, SMS and file storage may process personal data outside Vietnam; they are not added to the processing register by themselves. Add each provider as a recipient (name, country) of the purposes that use it (POST /purposes, PATCH /purposes/{key}), and prepare the impact assessment for transfers abroad (Decree 356/2025/ND-CP — form and exemptions for small businesses need checking). Planned after 1.0: modules declare their processors (Module::processors) and autoxide doctor warns about recipients abroad.

Data residency

A tenant can be required to keep its data in one country (Cybersecurity Law 116/2025/QH15, in force 1 July 2026, replacing the Cybersecurity Law 2018 and the Network Information Security Law 2015 — secondary sources, to check; its implementing decree, reported as Decree 333/2026/ND-CP, replaces Decree 53/2022/ND-CP — not confirmed. Who must keep data in Vietnam needs a legal check):

autoxide placement country main VN          # record where a placement's servers are

PUT /api/v1/compliance/residency
{"tenant_id": "…", "data_residency": "VN"}

Only platform staff with compliance.privacy.manage set it. It is refused (tenant_residency_violation, 409) while the tenant’s placement is not in that country or its country is unknown; moving the tenant later to a placement elsewhere is refused with the same code, and so is changing the placement’s country. GET /residency shows the tenant’s state; autoxide doctor warns (compliance.data_residency) about any tenant not met.

Personal data breaches: the 72-hour runbook

The report to the authority is due 72 hours after detection (legal rule privacy.incident, data with an effective date). Do this as soon as a breach is suspected:

  1. Record it at once — POST /incidents with title, severity (low…critical) and detected_at (when it was detected, not when it started). The answer gives report_due_at. Needs compliance.incidents.manage.
  2. Set who is reminded — the tenant policy incident.alert_emails (PUT /policies/incident.alert_emails with a list of addresses). A job every 15 minutes sends a mail at 24, 48, 60 and 68 hours and at the deadline (each once), and emits compliance.incident_deadline_near.
  3. Contain and log — PATCH /incidents/{id} with status: "contained", the kinds of data and the number of people; add each finding and action with POST /incidents/{id}/entries (the log only grows).
  4. Draft the notifications — GET /incidents/{id}/draft?audience=authority&locale=vi (and audience=subjects for the people affected). These are drafts filled from the incident and the privacy.contact policy: complete the missing parts, have them reviewed, send them yourself.
  5. Record the report — PATCH /incidents/{id} with authority_notified_at and authority_reference (the breach becomes reported), then subjects_notified_at when people were told; closed at the end.

GET /incidents?overdue=true lists breaches past their deadline, and autoxide doctor (compliance.privacy_deadlines) warns about them. The deployment guide points here (DEPLOY.md).

Requests of data subjects received through other channels

A request a user makes in their account (export, delete) runs at once. A request received by email, post, phone or from an authority is recorded so it is not lost:

  • POST /subject-requests with kind (access, erasure, rectification, objection, restriction, withdrawal), channel (email, post, phone, authority, other), subject (a user id, an email address or a phone number) and received_at. due_at comes from the legal rule privacy.subject_requests in force when it was received: 72 hours, stricter than the 2 working days to answer of Decree 356/2025/ND-CP Article 5 (which replaced Decree 13/2023/ND-CP). Version 2 of the rule also lists the days to carry the request out by kind (fulfil_within_days, from secondary sources) for reference; Autoxide does not track that second deadline yet — check the original texts.
  • POST /subject-requests/{id}/fulfil: access of a user returns the personal data of every module (send it to the person; it is not stored); erasure / withdrawal of an email or phone number empties it from the consent ledger (the hashed key and the records stay as proof, so nothing is sent again). Erasing a whole account is DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/{id}.
  • PATCH /subject-requests/{id} sets in_progress or rejected (with a reason). GET /subject-requests?overdue=true lists late ones. All need compliance.privacy.manage.

When an account is deleted (auth.user_deleted), compliance deletes its verified phone number and pending codes and removes the user from cookie consent records; proof of consents, accepted documents and the identity verification result stay for the time the law requires. The personal data export of a user (GET /api/v1/auth/me/export) includes the compliance part.

Reports of infringements and consumer complaints

Intellectual property infringements, counterfeits and prohibited goods are reported as cases; so are consumer complaints. A case goes: intake → (hide the target) → answer of the reported party → decision, with deadlines and a log that only grows. Basis — check the original texts: E-commerce Law 122/2025/QH15 and Decree 248/2026/ND-CP (from 1 July 2026; take-down on request of an authority, Decree 85/2021/ND-CP before), Intellectual Property Law, Consumer Protection Law 19/2023/QH15 and Decree 55/2024/ND-CP (complaints).

WhoEndpoints (under /api/v1/compliance)
Anyone (public form, tenant from the domain)POST /public/reports, POST /public/complaints, GET /public/complaints, GET /public/cases/{id}?token=, GET /public/moderation-reasons
Staff (compliance.cases.read / .handle)GET|POST /cases, GET /cases/{id}, POST /cases/{id}/entries, …/restrict, …/restore, …/decision, …/close
The reported party (signed in)GET /respondent/cases, POST /cases/{id}/responses
Staff (compliance.disclosures.manage)GET|POST /disclosures

Intake. The public forms ask a form token first (GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=compliance:reports, or compliance:complaints) and are limited per network block and email per hour (AUTOXIDE_COMPLIANCE_PUBLIC_REPORTS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR, default 5). The target is the reported object as <module>.<type>:<id> (e.g. content.entry:…, comments.comment:…; a product once step 41 exists); it must exist. The sender gets tracking_token once — only its SHA-256 is kept — and a receipt mail when they gave an address (link: AUTOXIDE_COMPLIANCE_CASE_TRACKING_URL with {case} and {token}). Staff record cases received by letter (POST /cases, reporter_kind rights_holder or authority).

Deadlines come from the legal rule cases.deadlines: hours to acknowledge, working days to answer and to decide by kind (consumer complaints: 3 and 7), and 24 hours to decide a request of an authority. Working days skip Saturdays, Sundays and the holidays listed in the rule (Vietnam time); lunar new year and make-up days are entered each year. The hourly schedule compliance.case_deadlines sends the event compliance.case_overdue and a mail to the complaints.contact policy’s email, once per deadline.

Hiding the target. A request of an authority hides the target at once; so does an intellectual property or counterfeit report when the tenant sets the policy cases.auto_restrict to true. Staff hide or show it by hand (/restrict, /restore). compliance never touches the tables of other modules: it sends compliance.target_restricted / compliance.target_restored (kernel contract autoxide_kernel::moderation), and the owning module hides the object — content answers 451 content.restricted and leaves the page out of lists, sitemap, feed and search; comments hides the comment and restores its former status. The target is shown again only when no other case still hides it.

The reported party is the owner of the target (from the kernel’s resource directory, e.g. the author of the page) and anyone with compliance.cases.respond on the reported unit (respondent_org_id, a seller on a marketplace). They see their cases without the reporter’s contact details and answer before respond_by; later gives compliance.response_closed (409).

Decision. A signed-in person with compliance.cases.handle decides (upheld or partially_upheld keep the target hidden; rejected shows it again); API keys get compliance.session_required. The reason is shown to both sides and mailed to the reporter. There is no MCP tool for deciding.

Disclosures to authorities. POST /disclosures (signed-in person, compliance.disclosures.manage) records the authority, its request number, the legal basis and the names of the fields given, and returns the values once — from the seller’s legal profile and identity verification kept by compliance. The record and the event compliance.disclosure_recorded never hold the values.

MCP tools: compliance.list_cases, compliance.get_case (read), compliance.add_case_note, compliance.restrict_case_target.

Consumer protection

  • Hiding reviews. Content of consumers may be hidden only for the reasons of the legal rule moderation.hide_reasons (spam, illegal_content, personal_data, unrelated, offensive — to check). Modules that moderate reviews ask the trait ModerationPolicy (autoxide_kernel::moderation) before hiding — orders maps its own reasons (unlawful_content → illegal_content, abusive_language → offensive, spam_or_advertising → spam, not_about_product → unrelated), so a reason a tenant adds to its list cannot hide a review while compliance is installed (compliance.hide_reason_not_allowed, 422) and record the reason in their own event; the list is public at GET /public/moderation-reasons. A negative but lawful review stays visible.
  • General conditions of trade are a versioned legal document of kind general_conditions, public at GET /public/documents/general_conditions.
  • Complaint channel. GET /public/complaints gives the website’s complaint page the contact (policy complaints.contact) and the deadlines; complaints are cases of kind consumer_complaint.

AI labels

Content written or edited from AI suggestions carries ai_assisted (content) and image alt texts from suggestions carry alt_ai_assisted (media), returned by the public endpoints so the interface labels them (Law on Artificial Intelligence 134/2025/QH15, from 1 March 2026 — check the decree). See CONTENT.md and MEDIA.md.

Tracking tags and cookie consent

A tenant adds the measurement tags of advertising platforms without pasting scripts, and they run only after the visitor consents. (Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15, Decree 356/2025/ND-CP, Consumer Protection Law 19/2023/QH15 — whether analytics cookies need consent, and the impact assessment for transfers abroad, need a legal check; the design takes the strict reading: ask first.)

Providers and tags

GET /tracking-providers lists the built-in providers; the tenant only enters the ID:

providerNameCategoryID formData goes to
ga4Google Analytics 4analyticsG-XXXXXXXXXXUS
gtmGoogle Tag ManagermarketingGTM-XXXXXXXUS
google_adsGoogle AdsmarketingAW-123456789US
metaMeta PixelmarketingdigitsUS
tiktokTikTok Pixelmarketingletters and digitsSG
zaloZalo Ads PixelmarketingdigitsVN

POST /tracking-tags {org_id, provider, tracking_id}, PATCH /tracking-tags/{id} (status: active / paused), DELETE /tracking-tags/{id} — compliance.tracking.manage on the website’s unit. A wrong ID gives compliance.tracking_id_invalid with the expected form; an unknown provider compliance.tracking_provider_unknown.

Banner

PUT /cookie-settings/{org_id} sets enabled, the optional categories asked about (preferences, analytics, marketing; necessary is always on and carries no tag) and position. Categories of active tags are always asked. Changing the categories or the active providers raises policy_version: visitors are asked again. GET /cookie-consents/stats?org_id= gives totals of the last 30 days, never single records.

For the interface

GET  /api/v1/compliance/public/consent-config?granted=analytics&locale=vi
POST /api/v1/compliance/public/cookie-consents
{"consent_id": "<random, kept in a necessary cookie>", "categories": ["analytics"], "policy_version": 3}

The contract with the interface:

  • Nothing loads before consent. Without granted the config returns no tag; with it, only the active tags of those categories. Read the visitor’s choice from your necessary cookie and pass it.
  • Reject is as easy as accept. Show texts.reject_all as prominently as texts.accept_all, on the first layer; no category is preselected (preselected: false). texts.legal is not overridable.
  • Record the choice with POST /public/cookie-consents (no sign-in; limited per network block by AUTOXIDE_COMPLIANCE_COOKIE_CONSENTS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR). It stores the random id, the categories, the version and a hash of the network block — never the raw IP — for the days of privacy.consent_proof_days. A signed-in visitor’s choice also goes to the consent ledger (purposes analytics / marketing, scope website:<unit id>). An old policy_version gives compliance.cookie_policy_changed (409): show the banner again.
  • Do not slow the page. Load tags async, after the page has rendered (loading: after_consent_deferred); add csp_hosts to the Content-Security-Policy; never load tags on sign-in or account pages; on checkout pages send only the standard conversion events (view_item, add_to_cart, begin_checkout, purchase).
  • Sending conversions from the server to ad platforms is not built (it needs its own legal check on personal data transfers).

Content

Tiếng Việt: CONTENT.vi.md

The content module keeps the posts and pages of a website, in several languages, with drafts, history, scheduling, categories, tags, authors, menus and redirects. It is API only: the admin screens and the website itself are separate projects that call it. It lives under /api/v1/content. The full contract, with every parameter and error code, is in openapi.json (and at /api/docs when AUTOXIDE_HTTP_API_DOCS=true).

Images are items of the media library (MEDIA.md): an entry keeps only their ids, and they must be public before the entry can be published.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
content.readReading drafts, revisions and schedules
content.writeCreating and changing drafts, translations, restoring revisions, preview links, asking for a review
content.write_ownThe same as content.write, but only on entries the caller created (same user and same API key)
content.publishPublishing, taking down, archiving, moving pages, scheduling; the terms and authors of a published entry
content.publish_ownPublishing and taking down only entries the caller created; no archive, schedule or moving published pages
content.deleteDeleting entries for good
content.manageCategories, tags, authors, menus, redirects, display placements
content.bannersBanners of display placements, per organization unit

Give them to a role with PUT /api/v1/auth/roles/{id}. The admin role has them all. Readers of the website need none: everything under /api/v1/content/public/ is open.

The model

An entry is a post (kind: post) or a page (kind: page, can have a parent page). Each entry has a draft — always there, the version editors change — and, while it is published, a separate published version that readers see. Changing the draft never changes what readers see until it is published again (has_unpublished_changes tells).

  • status is draft, published or archived.
  • slug is the last part of the address: made from the title when not given ("Đường đến Đà Lạt" → duong-den-da-lat; -2, -3… when taken), lower-case letters and digits joined by -, unique among the entries of the same kind, language and parent.
  • body is a ProseMirror / Tiptap JSON document. The server checks it against an allowlist of nodes, marks and attributes (paragraphs, headings 2–4, lists, quotes, code, tables, images, embeds from AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_EMBED_HOSTS; bold, italic, underline, strike, code, links), refuses javascript: and other unsafe links, keeps images as media ids only, and reports every problem at once with its place (body.content[2].attrs.href). It stores no HTML: the website renders the JSON.
  • The server computes word_count, reading_time_minutes and a plain-text copy used by search (accents and case ignored: da lat finds Đà Lạt).
  • SEO fields: meta_title, meta_description, og_media_id (sharing image), canonical_url, noindex.

Write and publish

# Create a draft
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/content/entries \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"kind": "post", "locale": "en", "title": "Hello",
       "body": {"type": "doc", "content": [{"type": "paragraph",
                "content": [{"type": "text", "text": "First post."}]}]}}'

# Read it: note the ETag header
curl -i http://localhost:8080/api/v1/content/entries/$ID -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Change the draft: If-Match is required
curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8080/api/v1/content/entries/$ID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H 'If-Match: "1731400000000000"' -d '{"excerpt": "A short summary."}'

# Publish
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/content/entries/$ID/publish \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'If-Match: "1731400000000001"'
  • If-Match is required to change or delete an entry, to change its state (publish, unpublish, archive, move, restore, schedule), to change a term, author or redirect, and to replace a menu: send the ETag you read (* to change it whatever its version). Missing: 428 precondition_required; someone changed it since: 412 precondition_failed — read it again and reapply your change. This keeps two editors (or AI agents) from overwriting each other. Deleting a term, author or redirect and setting an entry’s terms or authors do not need it: nothing is overwritten.
  • POST …/unpublish takes an entry down (it is a draft again, its address answers 404); POST …/archive takes it down for good (its address answers 410); DELETE deletes it (published entries are taken down first, their address answers 410).
  • A page cannot be published before its parent page, nor taken down or deleted while it has published subpages.

History and scheduling

  • A revision is a full copy of the editable fields. One is kept on creation, on each publish and take-down, on restore, when asked ("save_revision": true), and automatically when the last one is more than 10 minutes old. GET …/revisions lists them, POST …/revisions/{revision_id}/restore copies one back into the draft (it does not publish). The newest AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_MAX_REVISIONS (default 50) are kept per entry, plus the published one and those of pending schedules; a daily job prunes the rest.
  • Scheduling: POST …/schedules with {"action": "publish" | "unpublish", "run_at": …}. A scheduled publish pins the current draft as a revision: later edits are not published by it. If the entry was published by hand after the schedule was made, the schedule fails (content.schedule_outdated) instead of overwriting it. A failed schedule keeps its error code (status: failed) and sends the event content.schedule_failed. Taking an entry down cancels its pending scheduled publish, and archiving cancels every pending schedule of the entry (each sends content.schedule_canceled): a schedule made earlier never brings back an entry that was taken down.

Pages and addresses

The server computes the address (path) of every published entry:

  • a post: /<AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_POST_PATH_PREFIX>/<slug> (default /blog/hello);
  • a page: the slugs of its parent pages, then its own (/about/team); at most 5 levels.

The website only adds its domain and, if it uses one, a language prefix (/vi/…).

  • POST …/move puts a page under another parent (or at the root). It takes effect at once, for the draft and the published version, and for every subpage. A page cannot move under itself or one of its subpages (content.tree_cycle).
  • When a published address changes (new slug, move), the server records a 301 redirect from the old address to the entry — for the entry and every subpage — so old links keep working. Archiving or deleting records a 410 Gone.
  • Redirects can also be made by hand (/api/v1/content/redirects, permission content.manage): 301, 302, 307, 308 to an entry or an address, or 410. Loops are refused (content.redirect_loop). An address in the site starts with a single /: //host (which browsers read as another site) is refused, here and in menus.

Languages

Languages are set by AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_LOCALES (default en,vi, BCP 47 codes) and AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_DEFAULT_LOCALE (default en).

With several tenants, these are the default of every tenant: a tenant can set its own content.locales and content.default_locale (its administrator with PUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}, permission kernel.settings.manage; platform staff with PUT /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/settings/{name}). Its languages then apply to everything of that tenant: what entries, terms, menus and redirects accept, the locale of public routes, and the content part of GET /api/v1/kernel/client-config for requests that name the tenant. When the tenant’s default language is not one of its languages, the server’s default is used if it is one of them, otherwise the first of them. Entries already written in a language a tenant drops stay as they are. Wrong codes are refused when they are set; DELETE a setting to go back to the server’s value.

  • Each translation is its own entry, with its own slug, status and history, linked to the others by translation_group_id. Create one with POST …/entries/{id}/translations ({"locale": "vi", "title": …}). A subpage can be translated only once its parent is.
  • Posts and pages never fall back to another language: a missing translation is 404, so canonical and hreflang stay right. Published entries list their translations (translations, for hreflang).
  • Names of categories, tags and menus fall back to the default language; the answer says which language it used (locale).

Categories, tags, authors, menus

Permission content.manage.

  • Terms (/api/v1/content/terms): category (can have a parent) or tag, with a name, slug, description and SEO texts per language. Attach them with PUT /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/terms ({"term_ids": [...]}, the first category is the main one). This takes effect at once, also on the published version — so for a published entry it needs content.publish as well as content.write (the same for its authors).
  • Authors (/api/v1/content/authors): profiles of the content module — display name, slug, bio, avatar (a media id), website — optionally linked to a user account (user_id). An entry can have several, in order: PUT /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/authors. Setting the terms or authors of an entry needs the right to edit it, not content.read.
  • Menus (/api/v1/content/menus/{key}?locale=): a tree of items (at most 4 levels, 200 items), each pointing to an entry, a term, or an address. PUT replaces the whole tree (If-Match: * to create one). Deprecated (sunset 14 May 2027): website menus moved to the menus module, whose items can point to objects of any module; copy yours with autoxide task menus.import_content_menus (MENUS.md).

Stores and websites

In a tenant with an organization tree (module organizations), each entry belongs to a unit: org_id when creating it (omitted: your only unit, or the root when your role covers the whole tenant). The permissions above follow the scope of the role: someone with content.write on a store (subtree) writes only entries of that store and the units below it; entries outside their scope answer 404. Filter the admin list with owner_org (one unit) or site (what a website shows).

Each unit can have a website: its domain bound to the unit (PATCH /api/v1/kernel/domains/{id} with org_id), or ?site=<unit id> on the public endpoints. A website shows the entries of its unit and of every unit above it — head-office posts appear on every store’s website, a store’s posts never on another store’s.

Each website has its own addresses and slugs: two stores can both have /about. When a unit and a unit above it both publish the same address, the website shows the one nearest to it (the store’s /about hides the head office’s on the store’s website; the sitemap lists it once). The languages a website offers are the setting organizations.languages of its unit (PUT /api/v1/organizations/units/{id}/settings/organizations.languages with ["vi", "en"]; the first is its default), kept to the tenant’s languages; unset, the tenant’s languages. Public reads, the sitemap, the feed and public search follow the website’s languages and show only what the website shows.

The website: public endpoints

No sign-in needed. Only published versions are ever returned — drafts never.

EndpointGives
GET /public/resolve?locale=&path=What lives at an address: entry, redirect or gone
GET /public/posts?locale=&term_id=&author_id=&q=Published posts, newest first, paged (q: at most 200 characters)
GET /public/menus/{key}?locale=A menu with computed hrefs; deprecated, use GET /api/v1/menus/public/{key}
GET /public/terms/{taxonomy}/{slug}?locale=A category or tag page
GET /public/authors/{slug}An author page
GET /public/sitemap?locale=Every published address, with hreflang alternates, paged
GET /public/feed?locale=&limit=The newest posts with body, for RSS, Atom or JSON Feed

(All under /api/v1/content.)

A category or tag is public only once an entry shown on the website carries it: the term page answers 404 content.term_not_found before that, and the term list leaves it out. This is on purpose — a term being prepared is not revealed — so a menu item pointing to an empty category leads to a 404 page until a post carries the category.

Several sites on one server. On a server with several tenants, each tenant is its own site: the public endpoints answer for the tenant of the request — its own domain, or the Autoxide-Tenant header (its short name). Two tenants may use the same slugs, addresses, author and term slugs, menus and redirects; one never sees the other’s entries. An ETag from one tenant never matches in another.

Rendering an address. For each request, the website calls resolve with the language and the path, and acts on type:

  • entry → render data.entry (title, body JSON, images with their URLs, SEO, terms, authors, translations);
  • redirect → answer data.status with Location: data.location;
  • gone → answer 410;
  • a 404 response → answer 404.

Caching. Public answers carry Cache-Control: public, no-cache and, where it makes sense, an ETag: a cache may keep them but must ask again; sending the ETag back in If-None-Match gets a cheap 304 Not Modified.

Refreshing the cache when content changes. Subscribe a webhook (POST /api/v1/webhooks, see the webhooks section of the README) to content.entry_published, content.entry_unpublished, content.entry_archived, content.entry_deleted and content.entry_moved. Their data.payload.published gives what to purge:

{
  "entry_id": "…", "kind": "page", "locale": "en", "translation_group_id": "…",
  "path": "/company/team",
  "stale_paths": ["/about/team", "/about/team/jobs"],
  "moved_subpages": [{"entry_id": "…", "old_path": "/about/team/jobs", "path": "/company/team/jobs"}]
}

path is the new address (null when no longer published), stale_paths every address that changed, subpages included. Menus, terms and authors send content.menu_changed, content.term_changed and content.author_changed; these carry no list of affected pages (a tag can be on thousands). Tag each cached page with its term and author ids (for example term:<id>, author:<id>) and revalidate those tags when such an event arrives — renaming or deleting a tag or an author, including when an account is deleted, then refreshes every page that shows it.

Sitemap and feed. Build sitemap.xml from /public/sitemap (follow next_cursor; skip items with noindex: true; content_modified_at is lastmod; translations gives the hreflang alternates). Build RSS, Atom or JSON Feed from /public/feed, using each post’s id (never changes) as the item id.

Hidden by a case (451)

When the compliance module handles a report of an infringement (counterfeit, intellectual property…) about an entry and hides it, content receives the event compliance.target_restricted: the published entry answers 451 content.restricted at GET /public/resolve (answer 451 to the reader), and is left out of /public/posts, the sitemap, the feed, search and other modules (resource directory). It stays hidden when published again. compliance.target_restored shows it as before. See COMPLIANCE.md.

Banners and display placements

A placement is a named spot of the website (home_hero, top_strip…) that tells the website how to draw what is in it and tells editors what picture fits, so changing a banner never breaks the layout. A banner is the content shown there, with a time window and an order. Changing banners is a data change (REST or MCP), not a change of the website’s code.

Placements (content.manage)

GET/POST /placements, GET/PUT/DELETE /placements/{key} (PUT needs If-Match; deleting a placement that still has banners answers 409 content.placement_in_use). Each has:

FieldMeaning
displaysingle, carousel, grid (2–4 cells), stack (vertical, for side columns), strip (a thin text bar), popup
display_settingscarousel: autoplay_seconds (0 = off, else ≥ 4); grid: columns (2–4); popup: frequency (once_per_session, once_per_day, once_per_week), delay_seconds (0–60)
acceptsimage, text or any; a strip takes only text
ratio, mobile_ratio, min_width, min_heightpicture rules, checked when a banner is saved (2% leeway on the ratio), from the size the media library stored
devicesall, desktop, mobile: call the placement only on these
page_kindskinds of pages it is used on: home, category, collection, product, search, cart, content_entry, content_type, landing, or any
max_itemsmost banners at once (1–50) per store and language

New tenants get a standard set: top_strip (strip, text), home_hero (carousel, 3:1, at least 1800×600; phones 4:5), home_middle (grid of 3, 1:1), category_top (4:1), sidebar_left and sidebar_right (stack, 1:2), inline (4:1, image or text), above_footer (4:1), popup (once a day, after 5 s, 4:5). Edit, switch off or delete them like your own. A tenant created before this feature adds the missing ones with POST /placements/presets (it never brings back one you deleted unless you call it).

Banners (content.banners)

GET/POST /banners, GET/PATCH/DELETE /banners/{id} (PATCH needs If-Match), and PUT /placements/{key}/order with {"banner_ids": [...]} and the placement’s ETag in If-Match to order a whole placement at once. content.banners is given per organization unit: the staff of a store manage only that store’s banners; org_id left out means every store of the tenant.

  • kind: image (needs media_id, a public picture; optional mobile_media_id) or text (title required, tone = primary, secondary, accent or neutral — never a colour code, so a new theme recolours it).
  • link: {"url": "https://…"} or a path /…, or {"kind": "catalog.product", "id": "…"} — any type of the object directory (GET /api/v1/kernel/resources). Saving checks the object exists; the public read leaves the banner out once the object is no longer public (product off sale, promotion over). A banner linking to a promotions.promotion is archived when the promotion ends or is cancelled: advertising must not promise an offer that is over (Vietnam’s Law on Consumer Protection 19/2023/QH15, Law on Advertising — check the original texts).
  • page_kinds (within the placement’s) and page_targets ([{"kind": "catalog.category", "id": "…"}], at most 50): show the banner only on those pages. Example: a left-column banner only on the “Phones” category.
  • starts_at / ends_at, status (draft, active, archived), ai_assisted.

Reading on the website (public)

One call for every placement of a page:

GET /api/v1/content/public/placements?keys=top_strip,home_hero,home_middle,popup&locale=vi&page_kind=home
GET /api/v1/content/public/placements?keys=category_top,sidebar_left&page_kind=category&page_ref=catalog.category:0190…

Each placement comes with display, display_settings, accepts, ratios, devices and its banners: active, inside their time window now, of the website (site, or the domain) and the units above it, in the page’s language, in a fixed order (position). Images come with variants and webp_url for srcset / <picture>; links come ready as href. Banners not limited to some pages always show; without page_kind only those show. Cache-Control: public, max-age=… lasts until the next banner starts or ends (at most 60 s), so a CDN never keeps an expired banner; ETag gives 304. GET /public/placements/{key} reads one placement.

Rules for the website (part of the contract):

  • Draw banners in the order given; never shuffle them (it breaks caching and the page jumps on reload).
  • A popup always has a visible close button, respects frequency, and never shows on cart, checkout, sign-in or account pages.
  • A carousel does not autoplay when the viewer asks for reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion), and has controls to pause and move.
  • Label banners with ai_assisted: true as written with AI help.

Example of a home page:

const res = await fetch(`/api/v1/content/public/placements?keys=top_strip,home_hero,home_middle,popup&page_kind=home&locale=${lang}`);
const { data } = await res.json();
for (const p of data.placements) render(p.key, p.display, p.display_settings, p.banners);

Store information (header and footer)

GET /api/v1/organizations/public/storefront (public; the website from site or the domain) gives the brand — name, logo and site icon (ids of public media items: /api/v1/media/{id}/content), phone, email, social profiles — inherited down the organization tree (a chain sets it, a store overrides what it wants), the location (address, opening hours, special days, pickup, cover picture of the unit’s public profile), the unit’s time zone and open_now. Manage the brand with the unit settings organizations.brand_name, organizations.brand_logo, organizations.brand_icon, organizations.contact_phone, organizations.contact_email, organizations.social_links (PUT /api/v1/organizations/units/{id}/settings/{key}). For the legal footer of a shop in Vietnam, also show GET /api/v1/compliance/public/owner and the badge of GET /api/v1/compliance/public/badge.

MCP tools

content.list_banners, content.save_banner (drafts only: a person sets a banner active; text from a tool is marked ai_assisted unless told otherwise), content.order_placement.

Draft preview

Editors can show a draft to someone without an account:

  1. Set AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_PREVIEW_SECRET (a random string of at least 32 characters). Without it, previews are off (503, code content.preview_disabled).
  2. POST /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/preview-token (permission content.write) returns a signed token and its expires_at (AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_PREVIEW_TTL_SECONDS, default 10 minutes).
  3. The website’s preview page calls GET /api/v1/content/public/preview?token=… and renders the draft. The answer is Cache-Control: no-store; it always shows the latest draft, and holds only its content — not who created it or asked for a review. An invalid or expired token is 404 (content.preview_token_invalid). Changing the secret revokes every token.

On a server with several tenants, a token only opens the draft of the tenant it was made in: it names its tenant, so the preview page works on the main domain without a tenant header, and the same token sent to another tenant (by domain or header) is 404 as an invalid token.

AI agents

AI helpers (guide: AI.md): GET /entries/{id}/seo-check (no AI), POST /entries/{id}/seo-suggestions, POST /entries/{id}/translate (into the draft of the translation, never published; follow GET /translation-requests/{id}), and GET /search / GET /public/search (by meaning and words). Entries made by the server’s translation carry translated_from_revision_id, and translation_outdated once the source changes.

MCP tools. content.list, content.get, content.create_draft, content.update, content.publish, content.unpublish, content.list_revisions, content.restore_revision, content.request_review, content.seo_check, content.suggest_seo, content.translate, content.get_translation_request, content.search and content.resolve, with the same permissions as the REST endpoints. Results that contain an entry include its version; the tools that change an entry require it back in their version argument, exactly like If-Match.

Give an agent its own API key (POST /api/v1/auth/api-keys) with a short expires_at and only the permissions it needs:

The agent may…Permissions
write drafts, a person publishescontent.read, content.write_own
write and publish its own postscontent.read, content.write_own, content.publish_own

With the _own permissions an agent only touches the entries it created with that same key: another key — even of the same user — gets 403 content.not_owner. It can never archive, schedule or delete (deleting needs content.delete), nor move a published page; it can move its own unpublished pages, under pages it created. More limits keep it from going around an editor:

  • content.write_own without content.write: a new page, a moved page or a translated subpage goes only under a parent page the agent created (403 content.not_owner), so it cannot block someone else’s page from being taken down or deleted; the entry is always marked ai_generated: true, whatever is sent; on PUT …/authors it may add only author profiles linked to its own account (user_id) — profiles already on the entry may stay.
  • content.publish_own without content.publish: it cannot publish an entry an editor archived (403 content.archived); it cannot set published_at (422, not_allowed; the server uses the current time, or keeps the date of an earlier publish); it cannot publish at an address where an editor made a redirect (409 content.path_has_redirect), since the published entry would hide it.

Every change is in the audit log with the API key that made it, and requests with an API key are rate limited per key (AUTOXIDE_HTTP_RATE_LIMIT_API_KEY_PER_MINUTE, default 120).

Review. When the agent is done, it calls POST /entries/{id}/request-review (tool content.request_review): the draft gets review_requested_at and the event content.review_requested goes out — subscribe a webhook to tell your editors. DELETE /entries/{id}/request-review withdraws it; publishing clears it.

AI-generated content. Send "ai_generated": true when creating or editing content written by AI (agents should always do so; with only content.write_own the server sets it anyway). When a person — signed in, not with an API key — publishes such an entry after reviewing it, they send {"ai_reviewed": true} to POST /entries/{id}/publish; the published version records who and when. Public endpoints return ai_generated and ai_reviewed, so the website can show readers a notice where the rules ask for one (for example Article 50 of the EU AI Act, which applies from 2 August 2026; its exception for human-reviewed text is read narrowly). Autoxide records the facts; it does not give legal advice. The admin API also tells how an entry was created: created_via is session or api_key.

AI-assisted content. When a person writes or edits content from AI suggestions (applies seo-suggestions, rewrites an AI draft), send "ai_assisted": true on POST /entries or PATCH /entries/{id} (MCP: create_draft, update_draft). The flag is copied to the published version on publish; the admin, preview and public endpoints return ai_assisted, so the website labels the content (Vietnam’s Law on Artificial Intelligence 134/2025/QH15, from 1 March 2026 — the form of the label and what counts as “edited” still need checking against the decree). Anyone who may write sets it; removing it (false while it is true) needs content.publish (else 403 content.ai_label_requires_publish), and restoring an older revision never removes it. ai_generated (the whole text written by AI) is unchanged. Images: the media library’s alt_ai_assisted (MEDIA.md) comes with each public image as alt_ai_assisted.

When an account is deleted

Posts and pages belong to the site, not to the person who wrote them: they stay. Author profiles linked to the account are deleted (and removed from entries), schedules the person made are canceled, and created_by becomes null, as do review_requested_by (who asked for a review) and the record of who confirmed an AI review — the time of that confirmation stays, so readers still see ai_reviewed. The personal data export lists the person’s author profiles and the entries they created.

Settings

SettingDefault
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_LOCALESen,vi
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_DEFAULT_LOCALEen
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_POST_PATH_PREFIXblog
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_MAX_REVISIONS50
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_MAX_BODY_BYTES524288
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_WORDS_PER_MINUTE238
AUTOXIDE_CONTENT_EMBED_HOSTSyoutube.com,youtu.be,youtube-nocookie.com,vimeo.com

All are described in .env.example.

Customer chat (module conversations)

The conversations module lets signed-in customers chat with a shop — or with a seller’s store on a marketplace — about a product, an order or anything else. Staff answer from a shared inbox. A conversation belongs to an organization unit, so chains and marketplaces split the work by branch like every other record.

Vietnamese: CONVERSATIONS.vi.md.

Calls (talking to the shop from the browser, “call me back”) go through a voice provider connector — a separate module that needs an account with the provider; none ships yet (tests use FakeVoiceProvider).

Permissions

PermissionAllows
conversations.readSeeing the conversations of the units in your scope and receiving their events in real time
conversations.replyAnswering, taking a conversation, closing it, AI drafts, handing it over as a support ticket
conversations.manageAssigning colleagues, blocking customers, reviewing reports of abuse
conversations.callCall-back requests, calling customers back, the calls of a conversation (numbers masked)
conversations.recordings.readListening to call recordings (every listen is recorded)
conversations.voice.manageThe phone line of a unit, recording on or off, deleting recordings on request

With scope own, staff see the conversations assigned to them. Customers need no permission: any signed-in account uses /api/v1/conversations/me/threads.

Conversations and messages

  • POST /me/threads starts a conversation with a unit (org_id, default: the shop) about a record (subject, <kind>:<id>, e.g. catalog.product:<id>). When the customer already has an open conversation with the same unit about the same record, the message goes there instead.
  • Every message carries a client_id the app makes up. Sending again with the same client_id (a retry after a lost connection) returns the first message with status 200 and never adds a second one.
  • Messages are plain text plus up to 5 images from the media library. They cannot be edited; the author may recall a message within 2 minutes (its text and images are removed, its place stays).
  • Staff list the inbox at GET /threads (filters status, assignee=me|none|<id>, unread, needs_agent, org_id, subject), mark a conversation read (POST /threads/{id}/read; read cursors are shown to the other side), take or assign it (POST /threads/{id}/assign) and close it. A closed conversation takes no more messages; the customer’s next message starts a new one.

Real time and notices

Open GET /api/v1/kernel/events/stream?names=conversations.* (the server must set AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM=true). Customers and assigned agents receive the events of their conversations without any permission; staff with conversations.read for the whole tenant receive all of them. Events never carry message text: on conversations.message_created, read the message over REST. POST …/typing sends conversations.typing.

A message still unread after AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_NOTIFY_AFTER_MINUTES (default 5) produces one notice for the customer, or for the assigned agent — one notice per conversation and window, however many messages came.

Help for agents

  • Automatic answers: each customer message is passed to the automatic answering of module support (same approved answers, same rules, switched on per unit there, off by default). Automatic messages have auto_reply: true; show a “Talk to a person” button that calls POST /me/threads/{id}/handoff.
  • POST /threads/{id}/suggest-reply asks the AI for a draft (draft_reply); nothing is sent by itself.
  • POST /threads/{id}/escalate opens a support ticket with the latest messages and a link back; calling again returns the same ticket.

Abuse and the law

  • AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_MESSAGES_PER_MINUTE (default 20) per person; more answer 429.
  • PUT /threads/{id}/block stops a customer writing to that unit; customers and staff report abuse with POST …/reports, reviewed at GET /reports.
  • Unit settings: conversations.require_verified_account (customers must have a verified phone number, Decree 147/2024), conversations.mask_contacts and conversations.mask_terms (hide phone numbers, emails, links and listed words — marketplaces use it to keep deals on the platform).
  • Personal data (Law 91/2025/QH15): conversations are deleted AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS (default 365) after the last message; deleting an account erases that customer’s messages and unlinks their conversations; the personal data export includes them.

Calls

  • PUT /voice/lines/{org_id} sets the unit’s line: provider, hotline, call-back hours (default 08:00–20:00 every day, UTC+7), recording (off by default). The first response carries webhook_path for the provider — keep it.
  • Customers read GET /me/threads/{id}/voice first (hide call buttons when available is false). POST /me/threads/{id}/calls starts a browser call and returns a token for the provider’s WebRTC SDK. POST /me/threads/{id}/callbacks asks to be called back at the account’s verified phone number, in a window within the call-back hours and the next AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_CALLBACK_DAYS_AHEAD (7) days; one open request per conversation; AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_CALLS_PER_DAY (5) calls and requests per day.
  • Agents see open requests in the work inbox and at GET /callbacks (numbers masked), and call with POST /callbacks/{id}/call (with an Idempotency-Key); the customer sees the shop’s hotline. When a call ends, one summary line is added to the conversation. Unanswered calls reopen the request; requests 2 hours past their window expire and the customer is told once.
  • Recording: switch it on only with a provider that plays a recording notice; customers must then send recording_ack: true. Recordings move from the provider to your file storage, are kept AUTOXIDE_CONVERSATIONS_RECORDING_RETENTION_DAYS (90) days, deleted with DELETE /calls/{id}/recording or with the customer’s account. Personal data law (Law 91/2025/QH15): tell customers before recording — check with a legal expert whether consent is also needed.

Customers

The customers module keeps a sales profile for every buyer of a shop, builds the purchase history from order events, and groups customers for price lists and promotions. It is registered after orders and works without it (no history, no groups in carts).

Profiles

  • One profile per buyer in a shop, keyed by the buyer account and/or the phone number. The phone is stored next to a keyed hash (HMAC with a per-shop key, the same buyer_key that orders writes), so the same number matches inside one shop and never across shops.
  • A profile is created on the buyer’s first order (orders.order_placed), when staff register a customer at the counter (POST /api/v1/customers), or on the buyer’s first GET /api/v1/customers/me.
  • A profile kept by phone joins a buyer account only when the account’s phone number is verified (one-time code, compliance). Registering a number at the counter does not give the history to whoever types that number later.
  • org_id is the unit where the customer registered or first bought. Staff with customers.read at unit / subtree scope see only the customers of their units; a tenant scope sees all.

Purchase history and totals

customers copies a summary of every order from the events of orders (it never reads the orders tables). GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/orders lists them.

  • Total spent = what the buyer paid for goods of completed orders, minus refunds: after all discounts (coupons and vouchers included), with tax, without shipping, without the part paid with points or gift cards. The definition is fixed (decision D-226).
  • Orders count = orders placed and not cancelled.
  • Events delivered twice never count twice.

Masked contact details

Every list and detail for staff (REST, MCP tools, exports) shows phone_masked (09•• ••• 412) and email_masked (n•••@gmail.com). To see them in full, call GET /api/v1/customers/{id}/contact?reason=… with permission customers.contact.reveal; every call emits customers.contact_revealed, which the audit log keeps (who, which customer, the reason). The buyer sees their own profile unmasked at GET /api/v1/customers/me.

Customer groups

  • Manual groups: staff add and remove members (POST / DELETE /api/v1/customers/groups/{id}/members/{profile_id}).

  • Rule groups: members follow a rule, all conditions must hold:

    {"total_spent_min": 5000000, "orders_count_min": 3, "last_order_within_days": 180,
 "tier_in": ["gold"], "tags_any": ["<tag id>"], "org_in": ["<unit id>"]}

    Members are updated shortly after a profile changes and again every night (rules about time, like “ordered in the last 180 days”, change without any event). GET /groups/{id}/preview counts the matching customers now.

  • A group of a unit only matches customers of that unit and below.

  • price_group (e.g. vip) is the customer group code that price lists of catalog use. When a buyer is in several groups with a code, the group first by name wins.

  • Carts of orders receive the buyer’s group ids (for promotions limited to groups), the membership tier and the price group.

Loyalty points and tiers

  • Rules (POST /api/v1/customers/loyalty/rules) are dated data: earning unit (earn_per_minor, e.g. 10,000 VND → points_per_unit), value of one point, validity in months, minimum to redeem, and the largest share of an order points may pay. A new version starts at effective_from (now or later) and never changes the past.
  • Points are earned when an order completes, on what the buyer paid for goods (definition above), times the tier multiplier. Each earning is a lot that expires at the end of the day (Vietnam time) points_valid_months later. Redeeming uses the lot that expires first.
  • Paying with points: send "tenders": [{"kind": "points", "input": {"points": 500}}] to POST /api/v1/orders/checkout. Points are held until the order is confirmed (then used) or cancelled / unpaid in time (then given back). The payment partner collects only the rest.
  • Tiers (POST /loyalty/tiers): the highest tier whose 12-month spending threshold is reached, checked when an order completes and every day. The tier code goes to carts (promotions by tier) and to group rules (tier_in).
  • Manual adjustments: POST /api/v1/customers/{id}/points/adjustments with customers.loyalty.adjust, a reference (never applied twice) and a reason.
  • Voucher rewards (POST /loyalty/voucher-rewards, kinds birthday, purchase, points) are granted through the promotions module; a birthday gives one voucher a year, an order one voucher, and an exchange for points takes the points first and gives them back if the voucher cannot be granted. Buyers see their points, the rules in force and the rewards at GET /me/points and GET /me/points/rewards, and exchange with POST /me/points/vouchers.
  • Ledger: unused points are a liability (loyalty.liability) at their value when earned; redeeming credits buyer.prepayments, expiry credits loyalty.breakage.

Wishlist, recently viewed, reminders, referrals

  • Wishlist (/me/wishlist): products or single variants, up to AUTOXIDE_CUSTOMERS_WISHLIST_MAX. Right after signing in, send the list kept in the browser to POST /me/wishlist/merge; duplicates are skipped.
  • Recently viewed (/me/recently-viewed): signed-in buyers only (guests keep it in the browser), newest first, old entries removed every day.
