  • Sign: alert AutoxideBackupTooOld or AutoxideBackupFailed; autoxide doctor warns about kernel.backup_age.
  • Check: the newest rows of kernel_backups for that database (status, error), the log line backup failed, free space on the server (a backup is first built in the temporary directory, as large as the database) and on the file storage.
  • Fix: what the error says (no files module, a full disk, storage credentials). A row stuck in running whose process died is marked failed by the next run after 15 minutes. Take a backup by hand with autoxide backup <directory> until the scheduled ones work again.

A key leaked

  • AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET: set a new value on every server and restart, WITHOUT putting the leaked one in AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET_PREVIOUS. Every access token stops working; clients get a new one with their refresh token, which stays valid. (Routine changes keep the old key there for a while so nobody notices — see “Get the code and set the secrets”.)
  • AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY: rotate it as described in “Get the code and set the secrets” (new value, old one in AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS, autoxide secrets reseal). Backups taken before still open with the old key: delete them or keep them as safe as the key. Counters by visitor address start again under the new key.
  • An API key or a webhook secret: revoke the key, rotate the webhook secret from the API.

The last administrator is gone

  • Sign: nobody can sign in with the admin role (the account was removed, locked out, or the person left). autoxide doctor warns when no active administrator exists.
  • Fix: on the server, autoxide user create --email … --name … --admin makes a new administrator and prints its password. For an administrator who only lost their second factor or passkeys: autoxide user reset-mfa / autoxide user remove-passkeys.

Migration locks

Only one process migrates at a time. There are two locks: one for the main database (migrate up, a server starting with AUTOXIDE_MIGRATE_ON_START) and one for the tenant databases (migrate up --all takes it after the first, the background migration runs and tenant moves take only it), so a long run over the tenant databases never holds up a server that starts. On PostgreSQL each lock is an advisory lock on its own connection; if a proxy or a failover cuts that connection the lock is gone, and the run stops before the next tenant database (run it again). Keep PgBouncer in session mode for the command, or point it straight at the database. On SQLite the locks are files next to the database (.migrate-lock, .placements-lock); an in-memory SQLite database has no lock (one process only). migrate up --all keeps the main lock while it waits (up to 15 minutes) for the tenant-database lock, so during that wait a server that starts with work to do on start (AUTOXIDE_MIGRATE_ON_START, the first administrator, start-up tasks) waits too. During a rolling update from a release older than this lock, servers of the old version may still run a migration run without it: let the update finish before starting runs from the API.

Updating while two versions run

During a rolling update, old and new servers run side by side on the same database, so a release changes the database in two steps (“expand, then contract”):

  1. Expand: the new version adds what it needs (a new column, nullable or with a default; a new table) and writes both the old and the new shape. The old version keeps working: it does not know the new column.
  2. Contract: a later release, once no server of the old version runs, stops writing the old shape and drops it.

autoxide serve refuses to start while migrations are missing, so run autoxide migrate up --all (the main database, then every tenant database; the same as migrate up in single-tenant mode) before starting the new servers, then replace the old ones as in “Updating without dropping requests”.

Rolling back to an earlier release

autoxide rollback --to X.Y.Z brings the main database and every tenant database back to the migrations of release X.Y.Z (0.14.0 or later), so the servers of that release start again. Run it with the binary of the release you are leaving: only it knows how to revert its own migrations.

  1. autoxide rollback --to X.Y.Z --dry-run lists, per database, the migrations it would revert, the tables and columns it would drop with how many rows or values they hold (a column that only holds its default value loses nothing), and the rows a revert deletes. It changes nothing. On SQLite it works on a copy of the database, in a private directory (.autoxide-rollback-…, readable by the server’s user only) next to the database file, deleted when it is done: keep free space the size of the database there. The real run, once the servers are stopped, measures without a copy. On PostgreSQL it runs the reverts inside a transaction that is rolled back, so for that time it holds locks on the tables it changes: it waits at most --lock-timeout-seconds (default 2) for a busy table, then stops and says so — run it when the load is low, or once the servers are stopped.
  2. Stop every server and worker of the current release. If the dry run shows data that would be dropped, take a backup first (autoxide backup).
  3. autoxide rollback --to X.Y.Z --yes, adding --accept-data-loss when data is dropped. Tenant databases go first, the main database last; if a tenant database fails, the main database is left as it is: fix the cause and run the same command again.
  4. Start the servers of X.Y.Z.

Modules your own binary adds (.module(…)) are not in the release table: the rollback leaves their migrations as they are and says so; --revert-untracked reverts them too. The rollback is recorded as a migration run of kind rollback; when the target release predates that record (0.19.0 and earlier), the run is closed before the main database is rolled back, and an error there is only printed.

A migration that cannot give an earlier release its data back (the contract step of an expand–contract change) refuses the rollback; the changelog lists such migrations under the upgrade notes, and the way back across them is the backup taken before the upgrade.

Checklist before going live

  • AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET and AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY set to long random values, kept secret (autoxide doctor warns when one is missing)
  • TLS in front (reverse proxy), port 8080 not reachable from the internet
  • AUTOXIDE_HTTP_CLIENT_IP_HEADER set to your proxy’s header
  • SMTP configured, so password reset and email verification work
  • Backups taken on a schedule and copied to another machine; a restore tried once
  • /health/ready watched by your monitoring
  • Placement countries recorded (autoxide placement country) when tenants must keep data in Vietnam, and incident.alert_emails set for the 72-hour breach reminders

Forms

Tiếng Việt: FORMS.vi.md

The forms module keeps form definitions, takes submissions from the public (contact forms, sign-ups for a consultation, simple surveys), checks every answer on the server, keeps them in an admin inbox, mails the people in charge, and exports or erases them. It is API only: the website shows the form and sends it; the admin screens are a separate project. It lives under /api/v1/forms. The full contract is in openapi.json.

No third-party account is needed: spam is stopped by the core’s shared anti-spam layer (a hidden trap field, a signed form token, rate limits, duplicate detection; an optional self-hosted proof-of-work challenge).

Permissions

PermissionAllows
forms.readReading forms and their submissions (personal data)
forms.manageCreating, changing, opening, closing and deleting forms
forms.reviewMarking submissions read, archived, spam or not spam; deleting one
forms.exportCSV export; exporting and erasing every submission of an email address
forms.submitSending submissions without the anti-spam checks for anonymous visitors (a website server’s own API key)

People who fill in a form need none: everything under /api/v1/forms/public/ is open.

  • Setting or changing notify_emails needs forms.read as well as forms.manage: the notification mails carry the answers, so someone who may not read submissions cannot send them to their own inbox.
  • Give forms.submit only to the API key of a website server; being signed in is not enough to skip the anti-spam checks (see The website).

Stores and sellers

With an organization tree (module organizations), a form may belong to a unit: org_id when creating it; omitted, it is a form of the whole tenant. forms.read, forms.manage, forms.review and forms.export follow the scope of the role: a store’s staff see and manage only their store’s forms and submissions, and forms of the whole tenant need a tenant-wide scope. Exporting or deleting every submission of an email touches every form, so it needs forms.export for the whole tenant. Filter the list with owner_org.

Define a form

curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/forms \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  -d '{"key": "contact", "name": "Contact us",
       "fields": [
         {"key": "name", "type": "text", "label": {"en": "Name", "vi": "Tên"}, "required": true},
         {"key": "email", "type": "email", "label": {"en": "Email"}, "required": true},
         {"key": "message", "type": "textarea", "label": {"en": "Message", "vi": "Lời nhắn"}},
         {"key": "agree", "type": "consent", "required": true,
          "label": {"en": "You may contact me about my request.", "vi": "Tôi đồng ý được liên hệ."}}
       ],
       "allowed_origins": ["https://www.example.com"],
       "notify_emails": ["sales@example.com"],
       "success_message": {"en": "Thank you!", "vi": "Cảm ơn bạn!"}}'
  • Field types (closed list): text, email, phone, textarea, number (min, max), select, radio, checkbox (several values), date (YYYY-MM-DD), hidden (filled by the page, e.g. a campaign tag), consent (a box that must not be ticked in advance; its label is the text shown). text, textarea and hidden take min_length / max_length. Labels, help texts, placeholders and option labels are {"en": …, "vi": …}.
  • Every problem of a definition is reported at once (fields[2].options…).
  • Versions. Changing fields makes a new version. Each submission keeps the version it was sent with and is always shown with that version’s labels (answers[], and for choice fields the chosen options with their labels in answers[].choices), so old submissions stay readable after the form changes.
  • PATCH and DELETE of a form need If-Match (the ETag you read). Closing a form ({"status": "closed"}) keeps its submissions; deleting it deletes them too.
  • notify_emails are mailed for each new submission, with Reply-To set to the sender’s address (left out if the mail service cannot use that address). They are never shown by the public endpoints, and recipients never come from what a visitor sends. Setting them needs forms.read too.
  • Email answers are checked the way the mail service counts them: at most 64 bytes before the @ and 254 bytes in all, measured in UTF-8 after lower-casing (é takes two bytes).

The website

  1. GET /api/v1/forms/public/contact?locale=vi — the fields with texts in one language, the token_scope and the success message. No admin settings are included.
  2. Each time the form is shown (never in cached HTML): GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=forms:contact — a form token. Show a hidden trap input that people leave empty.
  3. POST /api/v1/forms/public/contact/submissions:
{"data": {"name": "Ada", "email": "ada@example.com", "message": "Hello", "agree": true},
 "locale": "vi", "page_url": "https://www.example.com/contact",
 "form_token": "…", "trap": ""}
  • The answer is 201 {"data": {"id": …, "message": "Cảm ơn bạn!"}} — the same whether the submission was accepted, held as spam (sent too fast, duplicate) or dropped (trap filled, too many from one network or address): bots learn nothing.
  • Wrong answers: 422 with every problem in errors (data.email → email, unknown keys → unknown; past 50 unknown keys, the rest are counted in one data entry). A missing or expired token: 400 antispam.token_* — reload the form. A closed form: 409 forms.closed. A page whose Origin is not in allowed_origins: 403 forms.origin_not_allowed (an empty list allows any site).
  • Sending the same form_token again (double click, flaky network) returns the first id and stores nothing new.
  • A website server may send the form with its own API key instead, if that key has the permission forms.submit: no token needed, limited to AUTOXIDE_FORMS_SUBMISSIONS_PER_USER_PER_HOUR; use an Idempotency-Key header. Any other signed-in caller (for example a self-registered account) goes through the same checks as an anonymous visitor: without a form token it gets 400 antispam.token_missing.

The inbox

  • GET /api/v1/forms and GET /api/v1/forms/{id} give each form’s submissions: how many are new, read, archived and spam.
  • GET /api/v1/forms/{id}/submissions?status=&q= — newest first, spam left out unless asked; q searches the answers ignoring case and accents.
  • PATCH /api/v1/forms/submissions/{id} {"status": "read" | "archived" | "spam" | "new"} with If-Match. Moving a submission out of spam mails the people in charge as for a new one.
  • GET /api/v1/forms/{id}/submissions/export?format=csv — CSV for spreadsheets. Cells that start with =, +, -, @, tab or carriage return get a leading ' so they are never run as formulas.

Large exports

For a form with many submissions, export in the background instead of holding a request open:

  1. POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/submissions/exports (body optional: {"status": "new"} like the status of the export above) answers 201 at once, with the export’s address in Location. A form has one export running at a time; asking again meanwhile answers 409 forms.export_in_progress.
  2. GET /api/v1/forms/exports/{export_id} gives state: pending, running, then ready (or failed: ask for a new one). Once ready, download_url is a link to the file — the same content as the export above, byte for byte.
  3. The link needs no sign-in, so it can be opened in a browser; it works for AUTOXIDE_FORMS_EXPORT_LINK_MINUTES (default 60). Do not share it. Ask for the export again for a fresh link. It is an absolute URL when AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL is set.

Both need forms.export. The file is written to the shared file storage (module files, local disk or S3) under forms/exports/ and deleted after AUTOXIDE_FORMS_EXPORT_KEEP_HOURS (default 24) by the daily cleanup job.

Personal data

  • GET /api/v1/forms/data?email=… lists, and DELETE /api/v1/forms/data?email=… deletes for good, every submission of an address, in every form (permission forms.export) — for requests of the person the data is about. A submission counts when the address is its sender’s email, or when any answer is exactly that address (ignoring case), such as a second email field (“your friend’s email”). An address only mentioned inside a longer answer (a message) is not found: search the inbox with q for those.
  • Network addresses are never stored: only a keyed hash of the network block, cleared after AUTOXIDE_FORMS_IP_RETENTION_DAYS.
  • A ticked consent box stores the exact text shown, the form version, the time and the source.
  • Events (and so webhooks) carry ids and the form key only, never answers or addresses; other systems read details through the API with a permission.
  • When an account is deleted, forms it created stay; created_by becomes null.
  • Deleting a form deletes its submissions. A submission whose form no longer exists is deleted by the daily cleanup job.
  • Large exports hold personal data. Deleting the submissions of an address, or deleting a form, also deletes every export file of the forms concerned. Export files left are deleted after AUTOXIDE_FORMS_EXPORT_KEEP_HOURS. Backups of the file storage copy forms/exports/ too while the files exist. The event forms.submissions_exported records who exported which form (for the audit log), without the file.

Legal

Retention times are settings, not rules written in the code. Whether a contact form needs consent, how long submissions may be kept, and how fast data requests must be answered depend on the law that applies to you (for example Vietnam’s Personal Data Protection Law of 2025 and Decree 356/2025): check the original texts for your case and set AUTOXIDE_FORMS_RETENTION_DAYS (or the tenant’s forms.retention_days, or each form’s retention_days) accordingly.

AI agents (MCP)

Tools, with the same permissions and checks as REST:

  • forms.list, forms.get (forms.read); forms.create and forms.update (forms.manage; setting notify_emails also needs forms.read). forms.get returns the form with an etag; pass it back as etag to forms.update, like If-Match (it is not the form’s version, which counts changes to the fields). Close a form with forms.update and status: closed.
  • forms.list_submissions, forms.get_submission (forms.read) and forms.set_submission_status (forms.review; pass the submission’s version you read).

There is no tool to delete a form (that also deletes its submissions, and cannot be undone; use REST) and no tool to send a form.

Settings

SettingDefault
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_MAX_SUBMISSION_BYTES65536
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_MAX_FIELDS50
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_SUBMISSIONS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR10
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_SUBMISSIONS_PER_EMAIL_PER_HOUR5
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_SUBMISSIONS_PER_USER_PER_HOUR1000
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_RETENTION_DAYS0 (keep)
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_SPAM_RETENTION_DAYS30
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_IP_RETENTION_DAYS90
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_NOTIFY_LANGUAGEen
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_EXPORT_LINK_MINUTES60
AUTOXIDE_FORMS_EXPORT_KEEP_HOURS24

A form may set its own ip_limit_per_hour, email_limit_per_hour and retention_days. The anti-spam layer itself (AUTOXIDE_ANTISPAM_*) is shared by every module. All are described in .env.example.

With several tenants, a tenant can replace AUTOXIDE_FORMS_RETENTION_DAYS with its own forms.retention_days (0 to 36500; its administrator with PUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/forms.retention_days, permission kernel.settings.manage; platform staff with PUT /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/settings/forms.retention_days). The order is: the form’s retention_days, then the tenant’s setting, then the server’s. A wrong value is refused when it is set; DELETE the setting to go back to the server’s value.

Getting started

Three ways to try Autoxide, from least to most work. All three give you the same server: the REST API, the OpenAPI document, the MCP endpoint for AI agents, and an administrator account.

1. The demo (about two minutes)

autoxide demo is a throw-away server for looking around. It needs no settings. On first start it creates the folder autoxide-demo (change it with --dir) with a SQLite database, random secrets, an administrator admin@example.com and the reference data (addresses, taxes, promotion limits). It prints the password on screen. Run it again and it continues with the same data. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

With Docker:

docker run --rm -it -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:latest demo

The data is gone when the container stops. To keep it, add a volume and put the demo folder in it:

docker run --rm -it -p 127.0.0.1:8080:8080 -v autoxide-demo:/var/lib/autoxide/data \
  ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:latest demo --dir data

With a downloaded binary: take the file for your system from the release page, unpack it and run ./autoxide demo (autoxide.exe demo on Windows). The release files have a checksum and a build attestation: VERIFYING.md. The macOS and Windows files are not signed with an Apple or Microsoft certificate, so the system may warn the first time:

  • macOS: xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./autoxide, then run it again.
  • Windows: SmartScreen, “More info”, “Run anyway”.

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/docs for the API reference and sign in with the printed administrator account (POST /api/v1/auth/login).

The demo always uses its own SQLite file in the demo folder: it ignores DATABASE_URL from your environment and .env, so it cannot touch a real database. --database-url <url> points it at another database on purpose.

The demo also turns off outside services from your environment (SMTP mail, S3 file storage, OpenTelemetry, AI providers, provider modules): mail is written to files and uploads stay in the demo folder. --keep-external-services keeps them on purpose.

Not for production: the secrets sit in a plain file in the demo folder, and the API reference page loads its viewer script from a public CDN.

2. The quickstart (a real single-server install)

Docker Compose, a volume for the data, secrets of your own: see the Quickstart in the README. For PostgreSQL, several servers and HTTPS: DEPLOY.md.

3. Working on Autoxide itself

Open the repository in a Codespace or a dev container (.devcontainer/ is ready), or on your own machine check what is missing:

cargo xtask doctor      # read-only: lists the tools you need, with one install command each
./gate.sh --quick       # what "done" means before a commit

When cargo xtask check reports a violation it prints a how to fix: line under it. Rules for contributors and AI agents: AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md.

Inventory (inventory)

Tiếng Việt

Module inventory keeps the stock of every product variant in every warehouse or store of a tenant. Every change goes into an append-only movement ledger, and stock is never oversold, even when many requests arrive at the same time, on SQLite and on PostgreSQL. Other modules use it through autoxide_inventory::api; the HTTP API lives under /api/v1/inventory (see docs/openapi.json) and the MCP tools are named inventory.*.

Stock model

  • A warehouse is an organization unit of type warehouse or store (step 34), or the tenant’s root unit (a single shop keeps its stock there). A unit of another type answers inventory.not_a_warehouse.
  • A stock level is one variant in one warehouse. It holds two numbers:
    • on_hand: units physically in the warehouse — always the sum of the level’s movement ledger, never below 0;
    • available: units that can still be sold — on_hand minus the units reserved for orders. It may go below 0 when goods leave a warehouse whose stock is all reserved (e.g. damaged) or when a product may be sold out of stock. reserved (on_hand − available) is computed, not stored.
  • The movement ledger (GET /movements) only grows: receipt, sale, return, adjustment, count, transfer_out, transfer_in, expiry, supplier_return. A mistake is corrected with a new adjustment.
  • Stock numbers change only through single conditional UPDATE statements (rows::adjust), never read-then-write.

Adjusting stock

POST /adjustments (inventory.adjust) changes stock in one warehouse:

{
  "org_id": "…warehouse…",
  "reference": "ADJ-2026-0042",
  "lines": [
    {"variant_id": "…", "quantity": -2, "reason_code": "damaged", "note": "Dropped"},
    {"variant_id": "…", "quantity": 50, "reason_code": "found",
     "unit_cost": {"amount": "120000", "currency": "VND"}}
  ]
}
  • Every line needs a reason from the tenant’s reason list inventory.adjustment (GET /api/v1/kernel/reasons/inventory.adjustment); built-in codes: damaged, lost, found, data_entry_fix, sample_use, expired, count_variance. Tenants rename, reorder, turn off and add codes.
  • reference makes the call safe to retry: the same reference and content returns the adjustment already made (200); the same reference with other content is reference_reused.
  • on_hand never goes below 0 (inventory.insufficient_stock).
  • A positive line may carry a unit_cost (e.g. opening stock); it updates the average cost.

Average cost

Each stock level keeps a weighted average unit cost for gross-margin reports: when goods with a cost come in, (on hand × old cost + quantity × unit cost) / (on hand + quantity), rounded half away from zero to the currency’s minor unit. With nothing on hand the cost is the incoming cost. Goods without a cost (returns, found items) keep the cost. A change sends inventory.cost_changed (catalog uses it for price floors).

Reorder points and alerts

PATCH /levels/{id} (inventory.settings.manage) sets reorder_point. inventory.low_stock fires once when available falls from above the reorder point to it or below; inventory.out_of_stock when it falls from above 0 to 0 or below. GET /levels?below_reorder=true and the MCP tool inventory.list_low_stock list them.

Reservations (for orders)

Module orders holds stock through autoxide_inventory::api::Inventory:

  1. reserve — all lines of an order or nothing, until expires_at (at most AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_MAX_HOLD_HOURS). Calling again with the same order_id and content returns the same reservation; other content is reference_reused. Bundles take stock from each component; digital goods and services are skipped. Variants sold as backorder or preorder may take available below 0 (backordered).
  2. confirm — the order was placed: the reservation no longer expires.
  3. fulfil — ship some or all reserved units (fulfilment_key makes it safe to retry); writes sale lines. With module orders, stock leaves when the goods reach the buyer: inventory listens to orders.fulfillment_delivered (one shipment; key fulfillment:<id>) and orders.order_delivered (key order:<id>:delivered), so on_hand and reserved drop and the order becomes fulfilled. Units on the way stay reserved (already out of available). Each event line carries delivered_quantity, the units of the line that reached the buyer so far, and inventory issues the line up to that total, capped by what is still held: events arriving twice, late or in any order, or after units were already issued by hand with fulfil when the parcel left, never issue more. Because the goods are already gone, this path also:
    • takes units from an expired lot when the lots still in date are not enough (logged as a warning);
    • issues units whose reservation the system had released (the hold expired, or the payment failed, for example a bank transfer that arrived after the hold ran out): the sale line takes them straight from on_hand and available. A reservation released by staff (POST /reservations/{id}/release) or by a cancelled order is never issued again;
    • issues serial-tracked goods with the serial numbers recorded on the order line (POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/lines/{line_id}/serials), each serial from the warehouse that holds it. Units without a usable serial (not recorded yet, or not in stock in a warehouse holding the line) stay reserved (logged as a warning) while the other lines are issued; recording the serials later (orders.line_serials_recorded) issues them. A manual fulfil does none of these three. One event is issued in one transaction: if one of its lines is rejected (for example stock already gone), none of its lines is issued. When a delivered order cannot be issued (no reservation for goods that track stock, or rejected), inventory logs a warning with the error code and counts inventory_delivery_unissued_total{reason="no_reservation"|"rejected"}. Reconcile by hand: release the hold (POST /api/v1/inventory/reservations/{id}/release; a reservation released by staff is never issued again, so later events for the order, such as serials recorded afterwards, do not take the stock a second time), then record the units sold with an adjustment (POST /api/v1/inventory/adjustments, negative quantity, reason data_entry_fix). Upgrading from an earlier version: orders delivered before this version keep their reservation confirmed (their units stay reserved). List them with GET /api/v1/inventory/reservations?status=confirmed and reconcile each order already delivered the same way (release, then adjustment).
  4. release — give back what was not shipped (cancelled, payment failed…). Releasing twice adds back once.
  5. restock — returned goods come back in (reference such as return:<id>); unsellable lines are only recorded.

Unconfirmed reservations past expires_at are released by the job inventory.expire_reservations (every minute). Each reservation takes stock with one conditional UPDATE per line, in a fixed order, so 100 buyers of the last unit get exactly one success.

Pre-orders

A variant sold as preorder may be reserved before stock exists. When the variant has a preorder_limit (set in catalog), held and confirmed pre-orders never exceed it, even when many buyers order at the same moment: the extra ones get 409 inventory.preorder_sold_out. Cancelling or expiring a pre-order gives its places back.

When stock arrives at a warehouse that has waiting pre-orders (receipt, transfer, return, positive adjustment), the job inventory.allocate_preorders gives the free units to pre-order lines in the order they were placed and publishes inventory.preorder_allocated for each line (quantity this time, allocated_quantity in total), so orders can move the order on. Running the job again never allocates twice.

Admins see reservations with GET /reservations (inventory.reservations.read) and release a stuck one with POST /reservations/{id}/release (inventory.adjust; recorded with their user id).

Module inventory also listens to orders.order_confirmed, orders.order_cancelled and orders.return_received (when module orders is installed) and runs the same functions, so an event arriving before or after the direct call, or twice, changes stock once. It also listens to orders.preorder_cancelled: only the cancelled pre-order lines of an order that stays open are released (their stock and pre-order places come back; the rest of the order keeps its reservation), once per event even when it is delivered again.

Choosing warehouses

PUT /sources/{store} lists the warehouses serving a store or channel, by priority; without rows the store sells its own stock. PUT /settings/{store}:

  • prefer_nearby — warehouses in the buyer’s province first (the province comes from the units’ public profile in module organizations);
  • allow_split — split an order over several warehouses when none has every line (default off: one order, one warehouse).

A reservation tries one warehouse that has every line first; with no candidate at all it answers inventory.no_source, with not enough stock inventory.insufficient_stock naming each line.

Transfers

POST /transfers (inventory.transfer at the source) creates a draft with a number such as CK-2026-000001. POST /transfers/{id}/ship takes the units from the source (only stock not reserved for orders) and adds them to incoming at the destination; POST /transfers/{id}/receive (at the destination) receives all or part — the destination’s average cost uses the source’s cost at shipping. close writes off what never arrived; cancel works on drafts. MCP tools inventory.create_transfer, inventory.receive_transfer.

Stock counts

POST /counts (inventory.count) opens a count (KK-…) for one warehouse; PUT /counts/{id}/lines or POST /counts/{id}/import (CSV with sku, counted, optional reason_code) records counted quantities. Each line keeps the on-hand quantity at the moment it was counted, so selling goes on while counting. POST /counts/{id}/apply (inventory.adjust) writes each difference counted − expected_at_count as a count ledger line with its reason (default count_variance).

Lots, expiry dates and serial numbers

Turned on per product in catalog (lot_tracked, serial_tracked).

  • Adding units of a lot-tracked variant needs lot_code (and expires_on). Reservations hold stock at the level; the lot is chosen when goods leave: the named lot, or else the lots that expire first, then units without a lot — never an expired lot (inventory.lot_unavailable).
  • GET /lots?expiry_state=ok|expiring|expired: expiring means within the unit setting inventory.expiring_days (default 30). A daily job writes expired lots off the stock (expiry ledger lines, event inventory.lot_expired).
  • Serial-tracked variants need exactly one serial number per unit when added, shipped (FulfilLine::serials), adjusted down or transferred; a serial number can be sold only once, even by two shipments at the same time.
  • Transfers carry lots and serial numbers: the destination gets the same lot codes and expiry dates.

Purchasing

  • POST /suppliers (inventory.purchasing.manage): suppliers belong to a purchasing unit; GET /suppliers shows payable — what that unit owes each supplier, from module ledger (absent without it).
  • Purchase orders (PO-…): draft → POST /purchase-orders/{id}/order (units count as incoming) → goods receipts, in parts → close (what never arrived leaves incoming) or cancel.
  • POST /receipts (inventory.receive, PN-…): against a purchase order (never more than ordered) or directly; each line updates the average cost and may carry a lot and serial numbers. With a supplier and module ledger, a job posts Debit inventory.stock / Credit payable.supplier once (ledger_status: pending, posted, failed — retry with POST /receipts/{id}/retry-ledger — or not_applicable). MCP tool inventory.create_receipt.
  • POST /supplier-returns (TH-…): goods back to the supplier at the current average cost (or a given price); the posting is reversed.

Public availability

GET /api/v1/inventory/public/availability?variant_ids=<id>,<id>&store_id=<unit> needs no sign-in. For each variant (1 to 100 per call) and store it answers a level:

LevelMeaning
in_stockEnough to sell; the number is never shown
lowFewer than AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_PUBLIC_LOW_THRESHOLD (5) left; quantity says how many
outNone to sell now
preorderNot in stock yet, sold as preorder

A store sells from its warehouse sources (or its own stock): with allow_split the sources add up, otherwise the fullest one counts, as for a reservation. Bundles count the sets their components make; variants not tracking stock are always in_stock. Unknown or hidden variants are left out. Without store_id every store offering pickup is listed. The answer changes as soon as stock is reserved; it carries an ETag (send it in If-None-Match for 304) and Cache-Control: public, max-age=5. Module catalog filters “available at store X” with the same rule (Inventory::in_stock_at).

Back-in-stock alerts

Shoppers ask to be told when an item is back at a store (needs module notifications):

  1. POST /api/v1/inventory/public/restock-alerts with variant_id, store_id (omit for the online shop), email or phone, and consent: true (plus the consent_text shown, kept as proof). Visitors who are not signed in send a form_token from GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=inventory:restock_alerts. A signed-in buyer may give no contact: alerts go to their account at once. The answer is always the same 202.
  2. Visitors get a message with a link to your page AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_CONFIRM_URL ({token} is replaced); the page sends the token to POST /api/v1/inventory/public/restock-alerts/confirm.
  3. When the store can sell the item again, each confirmed alert gets one message (inventory.back_in_stock) per time the item comes back, never twice for the same wave. Every message links to the page again; sending its token to POST /api/v1/inventory/public/restock-alerts/stop stops the alerts.

The messages are transactional (asked for and confirmed by the person, no advertising). Module customers asks Inventory::restock_alerts_of so a buyer is not told twice about the same item.

Checking the numbers

autoxide task inventory.verify_levels [tenant=<slug>] [org_id=<unit>] compares every level with its ledger and its reservations and only reports. autoxide doctor runs the same check on a sample of 1,000 levels per tenant.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
inventory.readStock levels, ledger, lots, valuation
inventory.adjustAdjustments, applying counts, releasing stuck reservations
inventory.receiveGoods receipts
inventory.transferShipping and receiving transfers
inventory.countStock counts
inventory.reservations.readReservations of orders
inventory.settings.manageReorder points, warehouse sources, store settings
inventory.purchasing.read / .manageSuppliers, purchase orders, supplier returns

All of them are scoped by organization unit: a person with a unit grant on warehouse A sees and changes only warehouse A.

Plans

Limit inventory.warehouses (units holding stock); features inventory.multi_warehouse, inventory.transfers, inventory.lots, inventory.serials, inventory.purchasing.

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_MAX_HOLD_HOURS72Longest reservation of an unpaid order
AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_EXPIRE_BATCH200Expired reservations released per job run
AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_MAX_LINES_PER_RESERVATION200Lines per reservation
AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_PUBLIC_LOW_THRESHOLD5Below it the public availability says low
AUTOXIDE_INVENTORY_RESTOCK_CONFIRM_URL—Website page for back-in-stock alert links, with {token}

Media library

Tiếng Việt: MEDIA.vi.md

The media module keeps the images, videos, audio files and documents of a website or app in nested folders, and serves them, publicly or to signed-in users. It lives under /api/v1/media. The full contract, with every parameter and error code, is in openapi.json (and at /api/docs when AUTOXIDE_HTTP_API_DOCS=true).

Content is stored where the files module stores files (AUTOXIDE_FILES_DIR on disk, or an S3 bucket), under keys starting with media/. Details (name, type, size, image size, texts, folder) are in the database. autoxide backup and autoxide restore carry both.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
media.readListing and reading items (private ones too), folders and the trash
media.writeUploading, editing, replacing, moving, publishing, trashing; folders
media.purgeDeleting items in the trash for good

Give them to a role with PUT /api/v1/auth/roles/{id}. The admin role has them all.

Stores and sellers

With an organization tree (module organizations), each item belongs to a unit: org_id when uploading (omitted: your only unit, or the root when your role covers the whole tenant). The permissions follow the scope of the role — a seller with media.write on their shop (subtree) sees and changes only that shop’s items; own means the items you uploaded. Items outside your scope answer 404, also for the private download link. Filter the list with owner_org. Folders and tags are shared by the whole tenant.

Upload

Send the raw file as the body (not a multipart form), its type as Content-Type and its name as name:

curl -X POST "http://localhost:8080/api/v1/media?name=team.jpg" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: image/jpeg" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \
  --data-binary @team.jpg
  • The server checks the content really is of the declared type, from its first bytes. An HTML page sent as image/png is refused (415, code media.content_mismatch). Without Content-Type (or with application/octet-stream) the server detects the type.
  • Accepted types are set by AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_ALLOWED_TYPES (default: JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF, SVG, MP4, WebM, every audio type, PDF); the largest size by AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_MAX_BYTES (default 100 MiB).
  • Raster images (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP, AVIF) get width and height. JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP images also get smaller copies (see below).
  • The answer (201, with Location) lists duplicates: items already in the library with exactly the same content (same SHA-256). The upload is kept either way.
  • folder_id=<id> puts the item in a folder, tags=brand,logo gives it tags. New items are private.

Read, list, search

  • GET /api/v1/media/{id} — one item, with an ETag.
  • GET /api/v1/media — a page of items. Filters: folder_id (root or an id; only that folder, not its subfolders), type (image/png or image/*), visibility (public / private), trashed=true (the trash), q (name contains, ignoring case), tag (has this tag, ignoring case), alt_missing=true (images with no alt text that are not marked decorative). Order: sort=created_at|name|size with order=asc|desc. Follow pagination.next_cursor with the same filters. include=uploader adds uploaded_by_name, the name of who uploaded each item.
  • GET /api/v1/media/summary — totals of the library: items, bytes, images_missing_alt, trashed_items.

Change

Changes need the ETag you read, in If-Match (* to change whatever the version). Without it the answer is 428 (code precondition_required); if someone changed the item in between, 412 (code precondition_failed) — read it again and retry.

  • PATCH /api/v1/media/{id} — name, alt, title, caption, decorative (true for an image that only decorates: its empty alt text is on purpose), folder_id (null for the root), visibility, tags (replaces them all; [] removes them).
  • PUT /api/v1/media/{id}/content — replace the content, keeping the id (and every place that uses the item). Same checks as an upload. The url, version_id and ETag change; the old content is deleted.
  • PUT /api/v1/media/{id}/alts/{locale} with {"alt": "…"} — the alt text in one language (e.g. vi on a bilingual site); DELETE /api/v1/media/{id}/alts/{locale} removes it. The item’s own alt stays the default for every language without a translation; the item answers all translations in alts. Languages allowed: AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_ALT_LOCALES (default en,vi), or the tenant’s own media.alt_locales setting when it set one (its administrator with PUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/media.alt_locales, platform staff with PUT /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/settings/media.alt_locales; media.alt_locales in GET /api/v1/kernel/client-config shows the tenant’s list); others are refused with media.unsupported_locale. Deleting an item for good deletes its translations.

Serve the content

Every item has a url: /api/v1/media/{id}/content?v=<version_id>.

  • Who: items with visibility: public (and not in the trash) load without signing in — use the url directly in <img src> or <video src>. Other items need media.read; without it the answer is 404, as if the item did not exist.
  • Caching: with the current v the answer may be cached for a year (immutable): replacing the content changes v, hence the address. Without v, or with an old one, it is cached for a minute (public) or revalidated each time (private). Making an item private does not remove copies already in caches (browsers, CDN); replace its content if that matters.
  • Safety: only raster images open in the browser (Content-Disposition: inline); everything else, SVG and PDF included, is downloaded (attachment). Every answer carries X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox, so content cannot run scripts on your domain. On top of that, an SVG containing anything that can run (<script>, on…= attributes, javascript: links, embedded HTML), anywhere in the file, is refused at upload (415 media.svg_active_content).
  • Metadata: the original is served exactly as uploaded, metadata included — a photo’s EXIF may hold where it was taken and the camera’s serial number. Remove it before uploading when that matters; the smaller copies below carry none.
  • Video and large files: one Range: bytes=… is answered with 206 (seeking in a video works); a range outside the content with 416. HEAD gives the headers only. If-None-Match with the ETag gives 304.

Smaller copies of images

A few seconds after an upload (or a content change), a background job makes smaller copies of every JPEG, PNG, GIF and WebP image, at the widths in AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_IMAGE_WIDTHS (default 320,640,1280,1920; only widths smaller than the image; off to turn this off). They are turned the right way up (EXIF orientation), keep the proportions, and are JPEG — or PNG when the image has transparency. The item lists them in variants, each with its url (the item’s url plus &w=<width>), ready for srcset:

<img src="/api/v1/media/…/content?v=…&w=640"
     srcset="…&w=320 320w, …&w=640 640w, …&w=1280 1280w" sizes="100vw" alt="…">

Until a copy is made, asking for it returns the original, briefly cached. Images over 40 million pixels, AVIF and SVG get no copies. Replacing the content makes new copies and deletes the old ones. Copies follow the item’s visibility and trash.

Changing AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_IMAGE_WIDTHS applies to new uploads. To give images uploaded before the same widths, run this once after restarting with the new setting; the worker makes the copies in the background (dry_run=true only counts):

autoxide task media.refresh_variants

WebP copies

Next to each JPEG or PNG copy the job also makes a WebP copy of the same size, usually far lighter: on a test photo about 55–60% smaller than the JPEG, and for an image with transparency over 90% smaller than the PNG (3.3 MB down to 80 KB at 1920 px). Each entry of variants gives its address in webp_url (the copy’s url plus &format=webp) and its size in webp_size. Let the browser pick: browsers that read WebP take the <source>, the others the <img>:

<picture>
  <source type="image/webp"
          srcset="…&w=320&format=webp 320w, …&w=640&format=webp 640w" sizes="100vw">
  <img src="…&w=640" srcset="…&w=320 320w, …&w=640 640w" sizes="100vw" alt="…">
</picture>

The public views of the content module (featured_media, body_media) carry the same webp_url. webp_url is null while the WebP copy is not made; an address with &format=webp asked for before then returns the JPEG or PNG copy, briefly cached. Images whose copies were made before WebP copies existed get them from the same command: autoxide task media.refresh_variants (it also queues images that only lack WebP). Making the WebP copies takes the background job about three times as long as the JPEG ones (about a quarter of a second more per photo for the default widths); requests are not slowed.

AVIF copies

With AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AVIF=true (off by default) the server also makes an AVIF copy of every smaller copy, in a separate background job after the smaller copies are saved — never while uploading. At the same visual quality an AVIF copy is about a third lighter than the WebP one (28–44% on the test images, docs/BENCHMARKS.md), but making it takes seconds of CPU per image (up to about 8 s for the four default widths of a 4000 × 2250 photo), so turn it on only when the server has CPU to spare. The AVIF encoder is not in the default build (it pulls in an unmaintained build-time library): build the server with cargo build --release --features avif first; a default build refuses to start with AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AVIF=true and says so. Each entry of variants then gives avif_url (url plus &format=avif) and avif_size; put it first:

<picture>
  <source type="image/avif" srcset="…&w=320&format=avif 320w, …&w=640&format=avif 640w" sizes="100vw">
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="…&w=320&format=webp 320w, …&w=640&format=webp 640w" sizes="100vw">
  <img src="…&w=640" srcset="…&w=320 320w, …&w=640 640w" sizes="100vw" alt="…">
</picture>

avif_url is null until the copy is made (or when the server does not make them); an address with &format=avif asked for before then returns the WebP copy (or the JPEG or PNG one), briefly cached. After turning it on, autoxide task media.refresh_variants queues AVIF copies for the images uploaded before. Turning it off stops making new ones; those already made are still served.

Tags

Besides its one folder, an item may carry up to 20 tags (each 1 to 50 characters, without ,). Tags are created when first given to an item. /api/v1/media/tags lists them, with the number of items (not in the trash) carrying each, renames one (PATCH, with If-Match) or deletes one (DELETE, removing it from every item). Names are unique, ignoring case.

Folders

/api/v1/media/folders: create (POST, name and parent_id), list (GET, filter parent_id=root|<id>, sort=created_at|name), read, rename or move (PATCH, with If-Match), delete (DELETE). Each folder gives item_count: the items directly in it, not counting the trash. Folders nest. Names are unique in a parent, ignoring case. A folder cannot move into itself or its subfolders (409, media.folder_cycle). Only empty folders can be deleted — items in the trash count (409, media.folder_not_empty).

Trash

  • DELETE /api/v1/media/{id} moves an item to the trash: its public link stops working, media.read still sees it (GET /api/v1/media?trashed=true).
  • POST /api/v1/media/{id}/restore takes it out.
  • POST /api/v1/media/{id}/purge (permission media.purge) deletes it for good.
  • Items stay in the trash AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_TRASH_DAYS days (default 30), then a daily job deletes them. Another daily job deletes stored content no item points to any more (left by an interrupted upload, say), only when it is older than a day.

Alt text suggestions

POST /api/v1/media/{id}/alt-suggestions with {"locale": "vi", "context": "…"} (permission media.write) asks the server’s AI model for the alt text of a JPEG, PNG, GIF or WebP image in that language. It sends a small copy (at most 1280 px), re-encoded without metadata even when the original is small, never the original file; private images only when AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AI_SEND_PRIVATE=true. Nothing is saved: store what a person accepts with PATCH (default language) or PUT /api/v1/media/{id}/alts/{locale} (other languages). decorative: true means the image adds no information — leave its alt text empty. A post body may also set an alt text on its own image nodes, which wins over the item’s. Turning AI on: AI.md.

When the stored default alt text comes from a suggestion, send "alt_ai_assisted": true with it (PATCH /api/v1/media/{id}, MCP media.update); send false once a person rewrote it. Items return alt_ai_assisted, and so do the images of public content entries (only when the image uses the library’s alt), so the interface can label it (Vietnam’s Law on Artificial Intelligence 134/2025/QH15, from 1 March 2026 — the form of the label still needs checking against the decree).

AI agents (MCP)

Tools media.list, media.get, media.update, media.set_alt, media.trash, media.list_tags, media.upload and media.suggest_alt, with the same permissions as the REST endpoints. media.update and media.set_alt take the updated_at you read instead of If-Match. media.upload takes the content as base64, up to 1 MiB once decoded — but the whole tool call must also fit AUTOXIDE_HTTP_BODY_LIMIT_BYTES (1 MiB by default), and base64 is a third larger, so with the default limit files of up to about 750 KiB fit; upload larger files through REST.

media.write lets its holder see every item it changes — for example by making a private item public — so give it only to people who may also read the library.

For module authors

Other modules read media through the autoxide_media::api::Media trait (register after media): find_many(&ids) returns, in two queries for any number of ids, the id, visibility, type, image size, alt, url and smaller copies of each item not in the trash. find_many_in(&ids, locale) does the same with alt in that language when the item has a translation (one more query), else the default. Keep only the item id in your own tables.

When an account is deleted

Items belong to the library, not to the person who uploaded them: they stay, and their uploaded_by becomes null. The personal data export lists the items the person uploaded.

Website menus (module menus)

The menus module keeps the menus of your website: the main bar, mega menus with columns, the footer, and any other menu. An item links to an address, to an object of any module (a post, a category, a product category, a promotion, a seller’s shop), or to nothing (a heading that groups sub-items). The website reads one public endpoint that returns the menu ready to show.

Vietnamese: MENUS.vi.md.

This module is the menu on your website. The menu of an admin interface is a different thing and is not stored here.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
menus.readSeeing menus as they are saved
menus.manageCreating menus, replacing their items, deleting

Reading a menu on the website (/api/v1/menus/public/…) needs no sign-in.

Menus and items

A menu has a key (main, footer…: lower-case letters, digits, -, _) and a language. There is one menu per key and language. The website asks for main in Vietnamese; when there is no Vietnamese main, it gets the one in the default language.

Each item has:

FieldMeaning
labelUp to 200 characters. With ref it may be empty: the item then shows the object’s title in the menu’s language, and follows renames by itself
urlhttps://, http://, mailto: or a path starting with a single / (//other.site and \ are refused)
ref{"kind": "content.term", "id": "…"}: an object of any module, by resource type and id
auto_children, auto_children_limitAlso list the object’s own sub-items (e.g. the sub-categories of a category), 1 to 50, default 12
iconA name from a fixed set: bag, bolt, book, calendar, cart, category, chat, fire, gift, grid, heart, help, home, info, mail, map_pin, news, percent, phone, search, shop, sparkles, star, store, tag, truck, user
highlightSets an entry apart (e.g. a promotions link pushed to the right in its own colour): accent, brand, sale, muted
badgeA small label: {"text": "-50%", "tone": "sale", "from": …, "until": …}; tones sale, brand, new, neutral. Outside its dates it hides by itself
featureAn object to feature in the item’s drop-down panel (title, summary, link, picture)
childrenSub-items, same shape

An item has at most one of url and ref; with neither it is a heading. A menu nests at most 4 levels and holds at most 200 items (sub-items from auto_children count as a level).

Object types available now: content.entry (posts and pages) and content.term (categories and tags; categories have sub-items). Product categories, promotions, sellers and shops come with their modules.

Admin API

RequestDoes
GET /api/v1/menusLists menus (paged with limit, cursor, order)
POST /api/v1/menusCreates a menu: {"key", "locale", "items"}. 201 with Location; 409 menus.menu_exists if the key and language are taken
GET /api/v1/menus/{id}The menu as saved, with an ETag
PUT /api/v1/menus/{id}Replaces the whole item tree: {"items": […]}. Send the ETag you read in If-Match (* to overwrite). 428 without it, 412 if someone changed the menu since
DELETE /api/v1/menus/{id}Deletes the menu and its items

All problems with the items are reported at once, each with its place (items[0].children[1].ref.id). When all problems are of one kind the error has its own code: menus.ref_unknown_kind (no module provides that type), menus.ref_not_found (no such object), menus.children_unsupported (auto_children on a type without sub-items).

AI agents use the same operations through MCP: menus.list_menus, menus.get_menu (returns version), menus.create_menu, menus.replace_menu_items (needs version), menus.delete_menu.

Menus of each website

With an organization tree (module organizations), a menu belongs to a website: org_id when creating it (omitted: the website of the whole tenant). menus.read and menus.manage follow the scope of the role, so a store manages only its own menus. The public endpoint picks the website from the domain (a domain bound to a unit) or ?site=<unit id>, and returns that website’s menu — or, when it has none with this key, the menu of the nearest website above (the whole tenant’s menu is the default for every store). The languages of a website’s menus are the setting organizations.languages of its unit (the first is its default), kept to the server’s AUTOXIDE_MENUS_LOCALES; unset, the server’s.

On the website

GET /api/v1/menus/public/main?locale=vi

{
  "data": {
    "key": "main",
    "locale": "vi",
    "items": [
      {
        "label": "Đồ gia dụng",
        "href": "/blog/category/do-gia-dung",
        "ref": {"kind": "content.term", "id": "…"},
        "icon": "category",
        "highlight": null,
        "badge": null,
        "feature": null,
        "children": [{"label": "Nhà bếp", "href": "/blog/category/nha-bep", "ref": {…}, "children": []}]
      },
      {"label": "Khuyến mại", "href": "/sale", "ref": null, "highlight": "sale",
       "badge": {"text": "-50%", "tone": "sale"}, "children": []}
    ]
  }
}
  • Items pointing to objects that are not public (a draft, an archived post, a hidden category) are left out with their sub-items; a heading with nothing left under it is left out too.
  • locale in the answer is the language actually returned.
  • Best sellers in a drop-down panel are not part of the menu: when the panel opens, call the product list of the catalog with the item’s ref.
  • The answer has an ETag (send it back in If-None-Match to get 304) and Cache-Control: public, max-age=….

How fresh is it?

The server keeps each worked-out menu in memory for AUTOXIDE_MENUS_PUBLIC_CACHE_SECONDS (default 60), and browsers may reuse it as long. Saving a menu clears this at once on the server that saved it. A badge starting or ending cuts the time short, so it shows and hides on time. A renamed category or a moved page shows within that time. With several servers, each server keeps its own copy, for the same time at most.

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_MENUS_LOCALESen,viLanguages a menu may be written in
AUTOXIDE_MENUS_DEFAULT_LOCALEenLanguage served when a menu is missing in the language asked for
AUTOXIDE_MENUS_PUBLIC_CACHE_SECONDS60How long a public menu is kept ready and may be cached (0 to 3600; 0 turns it off)

Moving from the menus of content

The menu endpoints of the content module (/api/v1/content/menus…, /api/v1/content/public/menus/{key}) still work but are deprecated: their answers carry Deprecation, Sunset: 14 May 2027 and a Link to the replacement. Copy your menus once:

autoxide task menus.import_content_menus

Menus that already exist here (same key and language) are left alone, so running it again is safe. Items pointing to posts become ref content.entry; items pointing to categories or tags become content.term. Then switch the website to GET /api/v1/menus/public/{key}.

It copies the menus of the default tenant. On a server with several tenants, run it once per tenant that has old menus, naming the tenant by its short name: autoxide task menus.import_content_menus tenant=shop-a. Each tenant’s menus stay its own: the public menu main of one tenant is never served to another.

Modules: what runs, and how to choose

Tiếng Việt

The Autoxide binary contains every module, but an installation only runs the modules it needs. One setting chooses them: AUTOXIDE_MODULES.

Three tiers

  • core — the server does not run without them (sign-in, idempotent writes, and what those need). Always on; they cannot be turned off.
  • official — on by default. Its API has no breaking change within one release line: a change that would break clients is made as a new endpoint, and the old one is declared deprecated with a removal date. A new release always reads the data of an older one (migrations run on their own). Security fixes reach every release line that is under long-term support.
  • experimental — off by default; turn one on by naming it. It works and is tested on SQLite and PostgreSQL like the rest, but its API may change between releases, breaking changes included; each change is listed in the changelog. The system never deletes its data on its own, but moving that data to a new release may need a manual step, described in the upgrade notes. An experimental module can be removed if nobody uses it, or become official.

A module is in one tier as a whole; tiers do not split a module. An official module never depends on an experimental one.

Becoming official: no open items left in the roadmap; real users; an API that did not have to change over several releases in a row; and, for a connector to an outside provider, a test run with a real account.

The modules

Needs lists the modules a module cannot start without; they are turned on with it. A module also uses other modules when they are on (for example orders takes shipping rates from shipping and stock holds from inventory), and simply offers less when they are off.

ModuleTierNeedsWhat it does
mailcore—Outgoing mail for every module, queued and retried, over SMTP or to files in development.
authcoremailUser accounts, sign-in with passwords, passkeys and TOTP, access and refresh tokens, API keys, roles and permissions.
idempotencycore—Storage of Idempotency-Key results, so retried writes run once.
aiofficial—Connection to AI models (text generation and embeddings) for every module; off by default.
filesofficial—File storage for every module, on disk or on S3-compatible storage.
addressofficial—Administrative units of Vietnam (provinces and communes after the 2025 merger) and address checks, shared by every tenant.
organizationsofficial—The organization tree inside each tenant (head office, regions, stores, sellers…), its unit types, life cycle and settings.
auditofficial—Append-only audit log: who changed what, on which record, when, before and after.
webhooksofficial—Signed webhooks (Standard Webhooks) that send module events to other systems, with retries and delivery history.
taxofficial—Tax engine: tax groups and rates as dated data, tax profiles per organization unit, withholding and invoice requirements.
ledgerofficial—Double-entry ledger per organization unit: accounts, append-only entries, balances, holds, payouts and payments through licensed partners.
invoicesofficialtax, ledgerAccounting documents and e-invoices: drafts, numbered issue, adjustment, replacement and cancellation.
complianceofficial—Vietnamese compliance basics: identity checks, legal documents and acceptances, website registration, personal data requests and incidents.
notificationsofficial—Notifications to users by email, SMS, Zalo ZNS, web push, mobile push and an in-app inbox, with templates and preferences.
plansofficial—Plans that sell modules, features and limits per tenant, with add-ons, overrides, subscriptions and usage.
mediaofficialai, filesMedia library: images, video, audio and documents in nested folders, with tags, alt text and resized copies.
contentofficialai, mediaPosts and pages of a website in several languages: drafts, revisions, scheduling, categories, tags, authors and redirects.
formsofficialmail, filesForms with typed fields, public submissions behind spam protection, an inbox, CSV export and retention.
menusofficialmediaWebsite menus (top bar, mega menu, footer) whose items point to addresses or to records of any module.
catalogofficial—Products, variants, category tree, price lists with history and price floors: the product catalog every commerce module reads.
inventoryofficialcatalogStock per variant and warehouse with an append-only movement ledger, reservations that never oversell, transfers, stock counts, lots, serials and purchasing.
shippingofficial—Shipping: buyer address books, shipping rates set by each shop (zones by province, weight tiers, free shipping, store pickup), carriers plugged in as connectors, shipments with parcels and tracking, and cash-on-delivery reconciliation.
promotionsofficialcatalogPromotions as rules: automatic discounts, coupons and vouchers, flash sales, tiers, bundles and gifts, stacking in three classes, usage holds for orders and legal limits as dated data.
ordersofficialcatalogOrders: carts for buyers and guests, checkout with time-limited holds of stock and promotions, orders with sequential numbers and a lifecycle, payments through licensed partners, returns and refunds, electronic invoices, point of sale, product reviews.
customersofficial—Customer profiles keyed by buyer account or phone number, purchase history from orders, masked contact details with audited reveal, and manual or rule-based customer groups for price lists and promotions.
sepayexperimental—Confirms VietQR bank transfers from SePay’s bank transaction notifications, with one SePay account per tenant (experimental: written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service).
momoexperimental—MoMo payment gateway (Vietnam) with one MoMo account per tenant: payment links, payment notifications, status checks and refunds. Written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service. See the MoMo guide.
einvoice_sepayexperimental—Sends e-invoices to the Vietnamese tax authority through SePay eInvoice, with one SePay eInvoice account per tenant (experimental: written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service).
esmsexperimental—SMS through eSMS (Vietnam): one-time codes and customer-care messages under each tenant’s own eSMS account and brandname. Written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service.
ghnexperimentalshippingGiao Hang Nhanh (GHN) carrier connector for shipping: quotes, shipments, labels, cancellation, tracking and status webhooks, with each tenant’s own GHN account. Written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service.
bookingsexperimental—Bookable services with staff, rooms and equipment, weekly schedules, public availability, bookings that never overlap, deposits through a licensed partner, cancellation policies and reminders.
newsletterexperimentalmailNewsletter lists, double opt-in subscribers, one-click unsubscribe and campaigns sent in rate-limited batches.
commentsexperimentalmailComments and questions on any record (posts, products…), with threads, moderation, reports, bans and answers.
supportexperimental—Customer support tickets: messages, internal notes, guest access by ticket token, staff scope by organization unit, and hand-over to consumer complaints.
conversationsexperimental—Customer chat with a shop or a marketplace store: shared inbox, assignment, read cursors, real-time events, notices for people offline, hand-over to support tickets and automatic answers from approved replies.
analyticsexperimental—Cookieless website analytics kept in your own database: pages, sources, UTM campaigns, most viewed objects and funnels; per-person tracking only with consent.
reportingexperimental—Reports across a customer tree: figures from every tenant (also on other databases), summed per day, tenant, unit and currency.
automationsexperimental—Automation rules: when an event, a schedule, a manual call or an unusual figure happens and the conditions hold, run MCP tools with the permissions of the rule’s author.

GET /api/v1/kernel/modules lists the modules that run on a server, with stability for each. In the OpenAPI document every operation of an experimental module carries "x-stability": "experimental" (an operation without it belongs to an official module), and docs/mcp-tools.json has stability for every tool; both also say so in the description.

Choosing: AUTOXIDE_MODULES

A comma-separated list. Each entry adds to the set; core modules are always in it.

EntryMeaning
coreOnly the core modules.
officialEvery core and official module. The default.
allEvery module, experimental ones included.
nameThat module, and the modules it needs.
-nameLeave that module out of the set chosen by the other entries.

Examples:

# The default, written out.
AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official

# Official modules plus two experimental ones.
AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,bookings,support

# A website backend: sign-in, pages and posts, media, forms, menus. `media`, `files`, `ai`
# and `mail` come along because `content`, `forms` and `menus` need them.
AUTOXIDE_MODULES=content,forms,menus

# Everything official except plans and the commerce modules that are not needed here.
AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,-plans,-customers,-orders

Mistakes are reported at startup, by every command, with what to write instead:

  • a name that is not a module lists the valid names;
  • -name for a module that an enabled module needs names the modules to leave out too (official,-catalog answers: leave out -inventory,-orders,-promotions as well, or remove -catalog);
  • -auth or another core module is refused.

autoxide doctor prints the modules that run and those that are turned off (the first line of autoxide serve’s log says the same), and autoxide config shows the value in use. autoxide modules lists every module of the program — also modules a binary of your own added — with its tier, whether it is on, what it depends on and, for a module that is off, whether the database still holds its data; autoxide modules --json prints the same for programs and agents.

Settings of a module that is turned off are not read: a leftover AUTOXIDE_NEWSLETTER_… line in .env is ignored. A task in AUTOXIDE_STARTUP_TASKS whose module is off is skipped with a warning in the log; a task name that does not exist in a module that is on is still an error.

What “turned off” means

A module that is turned off:

  • serves no routes: its paths answer 404;
  • is absent from the OpenAPI document served at /api/v1/openapi.json, from /llms.txt and from GET /api/v1/kernel/modules;
  • offers no MCP tools, resources or prompts;
  • runs no jobs and no schedules, and receives no events;
  • has no migrations applied: on a new database its tables are never created.

The files docs/openapi.json and docs/mcp-tools.json in the repository, and the SDKs built from them, always describe every module. autoxide openapi and autoxide mcp-manifest print that full contract whatever AUTOXIDE_MODULES says. A client can ask a server which modules it runs through GET /api/v1/kernel/modules.

Data of a module that is turned off

Turning a module off never deletes anything. If the database already has its tables, they stay, autoxide migrate up keeps applying the module’s new migrations to them, and turning the module on again continues from there.

While it is off, the module still takes part in personal data and in the tenant lifecycle (“dormant mode”) — it serves no routes, MCP tools, jobs or other events, but:

  • a person’s data export (GET /api/v1/auth/me/export, subject access requests) includes its part, and deleting an account deletes or anonymizes that person’s data in it, as when it is on;
  • deleting a tenant for good deletes its rows of the tenant (except tables kept by law), a tenant data export includes them, and moving, splitting or merging a tenant takes them along (the module’s own migrations are applied to its tables on both databases first, and only where it already has tables);
  • files still reads its own configuration while off and opens its storage, so deleting an account deletes the stored content too, and conversations deletes call recordings through that storage and the enabled voice connector; when the storage cannot be opened, the deletion is retried (nothing is reported done while content remains).

This is an obligation of personal data protection law (Vietnam: Law 91/2025/QH15, Decree 356/2025/ND-CP), so it does not depend on whether you use the module any more. What it still does not do while off:

  • retention clean-up of its data does not run (the module’s jobs do not run);
  • tenants created in the meantime do not get the module’s starting data;
  • events other modules publish in the meantime are not delivered to it later.

So that data is not lost by accident:

  • autoxide serve logs a warning at startup, and autoxide doctor reports modules_turned_off, when the database holds rows of a module that is off — with the exact AUTOXIDE_MODULES=… line that turns it back on. (When you set AUTOXIDE_MODULES yourself the message is informational: you chose.)
  • autoxide copy, autoxide backup and autoxide restore refuse to run while such data exists, because they only handle the modules that are on. Run them with the module turned on, or with AUTOXIDE_MODULES=all.

The check for such data looks at the main database and at the database of every placement.

To remove the data of a module for good, run autoxide migrate down <module> --steps 1000 — it works while the module is off (this drops its tables — back up first). autoxide migrate up keeps the tables of a turned-off module up to date where they exist, and never creates them elsewhere. migrate down has no --all: it acts on the main database only, so the module’s tables in the database of a placement stay (and migrate up --all keeps updating them) until you run it against that database too.

Upgrading from 0.17 or earlier

Up to 0.17 every module ran. From this release, with AUTOXIDE_MODULES not set, the eight experimental modules (bookings, newsletter, comments, support, conversations, analytics, reporting, automations) are off.

  1. Before updating, decide which of them you use. If unsure, update and run autoxide doctor: modules_turned_off lists the ones whose tables hold rows, and gives the line to add.
  2. Add that line to .env (or the environment of the container), for example AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,newsletter,comments, and restart. To keep exactly the behavior of 0.17, use AUTOXIDE_MODULES=all.
  3. Roles keep the permissions of modules that are off, plans keep their features, and stored data stays; they take effect again when the module is turned on.

Nothing is deleted in either case, and the choice can be changed at any time.

For module authors

A module declares its tier and what it needs in its Module implementation; all three have defaults, so a module that declares nothing is official, optional and independent:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn stability(&self) -> Stability { Stability::Experimental }
fn essential(&self) -> bool { false }
fn depends_on(&self) -> Vec<&'static str> { vec!["mail", "files"] }
}

List in depends_on every module whose contract you take with context.require::<…>()? in start. Contracts you take with .ok() are optional and stay out of it. A test in the binary starts each module with only the modules it declares, so a missing name fails the gate, not an installation. See MODULE_GUIDE.md for the rest of the contract.

The module ecosystem

English · Tiếng Việt

Autoxide’s core is small and neutral; business features live in modules. Modules can live in this repository (the official ones) or in your own repository, built against the stable contract (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md). This page says how to name, describe, publish and list a module so that others can find it and know it will work. How to write one: docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md and docs/guides/writing-a-module.md.

Naming

  • The crate is named autoxide-<name> (lowercase, hyphen-separated), for example autoxide-bookmarks. Tables start with <name>_ (the ownership rule), permissions with <name>., error codes with <name>..
  • Names of the official modules in this repository are reserved. For your own, check https://crates.io and the community list first: pick a name that says what the module does (autoxide-shipping-ghn, not autoxide-best). If a name is already taken by a module with the same job, consider contributing to it.
  • A name with the autoxide- prefix says “this module plugs into Autoxide”. It does not say “made or endorsed by the Autoxide project”: see TRADEMARK.md.

Discoverability

  • Add the GitHub topic autoxide-module to the repository (Settings → About → Topics). The list of repositories with that topic is the always-fresh catalogue: https://github.com/topics/autoxide-module.
  • Add the crates.io keywords autoxide and autoxide-module (keywords in Cargo.toml; crates.io allows five).
  • Put autoxide-module.toml (below) at the root of the repository, and one line in the README: which Autoxide versions it works with.

The module manifest (autoxide-module.toml)

A proposed file that describes a module for people and tools. It is declarative metadata: the Rust code stays the source of truth, and a check in the CLI (autoxide check, planned in step 71 G6) will compare the file with the code. Until then the file is read by humans and by the community list.

# autoxide-module.toml — at the root of the module repository
manifest_version = 1

[module]
name = "bookmarks"                      # the module name; the crate is autoxide-<name>
crate = "autoxide-bookmarks"
summary = "Save and tag links."        # one line, English
license = "MIT OR Apache-2.0"
repository = "https://github.com/example/autoxide-bookmarks"
tier = "community"                      # official | community  (stable/experimental is the contract tier of the core)

[compatibility]
autoxide = ">=0.19, <0.21"              # core versions this release was tested with (SemVer range)
rust-version = "1.99"                   # minimum Rust version
databases = ["sqlite", "postgres"]      # both are required for the list below

[provides]
permissions = ["bookmarks.read", "bookmarks.write"]
tables_prefix = "bookmarks_"
mcp_tools = ["bookmarks.list", "bookmarks.create"]
events = ["bookmarks.created"]

[requires]
# traits of other modules this one needs (context.require::<dyn …>())
modules = []

Rules: databases must list both sqlite and postgres to be accepted in the community list (the core’s first rule); autoxide is a range of released versions that you have tested, not “any”.

Version compatibility

A module depends on a released Autoxide (autoxide-kernel, autoxide-testkit, autoxide pinned to a tag or version).

Autoxide coreModule contractWhat a module author should do
0.xMay change in a minor release (with #[deprecated] first)Pin an exact minor (=0.19) and test on each new minor
1.xStable: breaks only in a major releaseDepend on 1 (caret); declare >=1.0, <2.0
2.0New majorPort, release a new major of the module

A module release that works with several core versions lists the range in [compatibility] and in CI (test against the lowest and the newest version in the range). Raise the range only after the test suite passes on the new version.

Listing your module

The community list has no gatekeeper beyond these checks, so that anyone can publish:

  1. The module is in a public repository under an OSI-approved open-source license.
  2. cargo xtask check-module <dir> from an Autoxide checkout passes on it (the module rules of the core: ownership of tables, error codes, translations, OpenAPI documentation).
  3. Its tests pass on both SQLite and PostgreSQL, using autoxide-testkit.
  4. It has a README in English (a Vietnamese one is welcome), a SECURITY.md or a link to how to report problems, and autoxide-module.toml.
  5. The repository carries the topic autoxide-module.

To appear on the curated list below, open a pull request that adds one row (alphabetical by name) to this file. A maintainer checks the five points above, not the quality of the code, and may remove a row that stops meeting them. The list is not an endorsement.

The community list

ModuleSummaryAutoxide versionsRepository
none yetThe reference example is examples/external-module0.19in this repository

Official and community modules

Official modules are in modules/ of this repository, maintained by the Autoxide maintainers, held to the full gate and labelled by contract tier (stable or experimental). Community modules are maintained by their authors and carry no promise from the Autoxide project. A community module that becomes widely used can be proposed to be adopted as an official module with an RFC.

Writing a module

Tiếng Việt

Business features live in modules, not in the core. A module is one crate under modules/<name> that owns its tables, declares what it needs from the core through the Module trait, and is registered in exactly one place. The sample module modules/notes uses every part of the contract; cargo xtask new-module starts a new module from it.

Rules that the gate enforces

  • One crate, two public items. A module exposes only pub mod api; (types and traits other modules may use) and pub fn module() (for the binary). Everything else is private. Other modules write autoxide_<name>::api::… and nothing else.
  • Own tables only. Every table of module notes is named notes_…, including the migration history notes_migrations. Never read, write or join another module’s tables, and never add a foreign key to them: keep the id only.
