Notifications

Tiếng Việt

The notifications module sends notifications to people over email, SMS, Zalo ZNS, web push, mobile push and an in-app inbox. Modules declare the kinds of notification they send; people choose which ones they get; advertising follows the consent ledger and the legal rules of the compliance module. Platform staff can send a notice to the admins of every tenant.

The legal notes below (consent, allowed hours, advertising labels) come from Decree 91/2020/ND-CP and the Law on Personal Data Protection 91/2025/QH15 and need checking against the original documents by someone qualified before use in production.

Kinds and categories

Every notification has a kind declared by a module, e.g. orders.order_shipped. A kind has:

FieldMeaning
categorysecurity (sign-in, password: always sent, cannot be turned off), transactional (caused by something the person did: on unless they turn it off), marketing (advertising: needs a consent)
channelswhere it may go: email, sms, zns, web_push, in_app, mobile_push
default textstitle, body and a short text (SMS, ZNS, push) in English, with {name} places; the Vietnamese translation lives in the declaring module’s locales/vi.json
purposeadvertising only: the consent purpose to check (default marketing)
invitationadvertising only: an invitation to sign up, sent at most once per address and channel

GET /api/v1/notifications/kinds lists every kind (any signed-in user), so an interface can build a preferences page.

How a notification is sent

  1. A module calls Notifier::notify (from an event handler or a job, never inside its own write transaction) with the kind, the recipient (a user, an email, a phone number, or every admin of the tenant), the values for the text, an optional link and a required dedupe_key.
  2. The module picks the channels: the kind’s channels, minus those the person turned off (security ignores preferences), minus those without an address (email of the account, phone number, push subscriptions), minus those without a provider on this server. Advertising also needs a consent in the ledger of compliance. Each recipient gets at most AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_PER_RECIPIENT_PER_HOUR (20) transactional and advertising notifications per hour.
  3. One message per channel is written to the send log with a delivery job, in one transaction. The same dedupe_key again returns the same messages and sends nothing new — retry safely.
  4. The delivery job reads the message again. For advertising it checks the consent again right before sending (withdrawn → skipped / consent_withdrawn) and the allowed hours: outside them the message is deferred to the next opening, and dropped (quiet_hours_expired) if it could not go out within 24 hours. It then renders the text (tenant text, else translation, else English) and hands it to the provider. Temporary errors are retried; permanent ones mark the message failed with an error_code.

Skipped channels are listed in the result (skipped) and in the send log with a reason: no_consent, consent_withdrawn, preference_off, no_address, channel_disabled, quiet_hours_expired, invitation_used, throttled.

Advertising

  • Only to people with a consent for the purpose and channel (PUT /api/v1/compliance/me/consents, or a module recording one through ConsentLedger).
  • Allowed hours and labels are legal rules with effective dates in compliance, not code: notifications.send_windows (SMS and ZNS 07:00–22:00 Vietnam time, utc_offset_minutes: 420) and notifications.marketing_labels (QC before SMS, [QC] before email subjects and push titles). Platform staff import new versions with POST /api/v1/compliance/rules.
  • Every advertising email carries a List-Unsubscribe header and a footer with a link to your website’s page AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL (with {token}). That page sends the token to POST /api/v1/notifications/public/unsubscribe (no sign-in): the consent is withdrawn and waiting advertising is canceled. Without the setting, advertising emails are not sent (failed / unsubscribe_url_missing). The link works while the send log keeps the address (AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS, 90 days).
  • When a consent is withdrawn anywhere (event compliance.consent_withdrawn), queued and deferred advertising of that person is canceled.

Channels and providers

ChannelProvider (kernel trait)Address
emailMailer (module mail)the account’s email, or the email given
smsSmsSenderthe phone number given
znsZnsSenderthe phone number given; the approved Zalo template id is set per tenant with PUT /templates/{kind}/zns/{locale} (zns_template_id)
web_pushWebPushSenderthe browsers the user registered (POST /me/push-subscriptions)
mobile_pushMobilePushSenderthe devices the user registered (POST /me/device-tokens)
in_appbuilt inthe user’s inbox (GET /me/inbox)

SMS, ZNS, web push and mobile push providers are separate modules that need the provider’s keys; this release ships none (tests use fakes). Without a provider the channel is skipped (channel_disabled). Push secrets (the browser’s auth key, device tokens) are stored encrypted. When a push service says a subscription or token is gone, it is removed.

Mobile push: the app registers its FCM / APNs token with POST /me/device-tokens ({"platform": "android", "token": "…", "app_id": "com.example.shop"}; registering the same token again updates it), lists the person’s devices with GET /me/device-tokens (the token is never returned) and removes one with DELETE /me/device-tokens/{id}. Mobile push follows the same rules as web push: preferences per kind, advertising only with a consent (channel push in the consent ledger) and inside the allowed hours of notifications.send_windows (key push). A token the provider reports as gone or rejects is removed at once; a token that fails 10 times in a row is removed too. A provider module implements the kernel trait MobilePushSender; Firebase Cloud Messaging and Apple Push Notification service connectors need the provider’s keys and are not part of this release.

For people: inbox and preferences

  • GET /me/inbox (page, unread=true for unread only), GET /me/inbox/unread-count, POST /me/inbox/{id}/read, POST /me/inbox/read-all.
  • GET /me/preferences lists every kind with each channel on or off; PUT /me/preferences takes {"items": [{"target": "category:marketing", "channel": "email", "enabled": false}]}. A target is kind:<key> or category:<name>; a kind setting wins over its category. Turning a security notification off answers notifications.preference_locked.
  • GET /public/web-push-key gives the key for PushManager.subscribe.

For admins

EndpointPermission
GET /templates, PUT / DELETE /templates/{kind}/{channel}/{locale} — replace a default text (only the {name} places of the default text and {link})notifications.templates.manage
POST /messages — send a notificationnotifications.send (advertising also notifications.send_marketing)
GET /messages, GET /messages/{id} — the send lognotifications.messages.read
POST /platform-notices — a notice to the admins of every tenant (platform staff)notifications.platform_notices.send

A platform notice goes in the background, 50 tenants at a time, to the inbox and email of every active admin; running it again never sends twice. category is transactional (admins may turn it off) or security. The plans module uses the same path to tell tenant admins when their subscription is suspended or past due, and once a month when they use 80% of a limit.

MCP tools: notifications.list_kinds, notifications.send_notification, notifications.list_messages, notifications.list_my_inbox, notifications.mark_inbox_read, notifications.list_my_devices, notifications.get_template_schema, notifications.preview_template, notifications.update_template_draft.

Templates written by the tenant

A tenant can write its own template for each kind, channel and language, in the syntax of the shared template engine: {{ code }}, {% if link %}…{% endif %}, {% for line in lines %}…{% endfor %}, filters money, number, date. Templates are untrusted data: no files, no network, limits on size, steps and output (template.limit_exceeded), and every value put into HTML is escaped.

Endpoint (under /templates/{kind}/{channel}/{locale})Permission
GET /kinds/{kind}/schema — the variables a template may use (required ones marked) and sample datasigned in
GET / PUT / DELETE …/draft — the draft; saving checks syntax, unknown variables and required variables, every problem at once with line and columnread: notifications.templates.read; write: notifications.templates.manage
POST …/publish — the draft becomes a new version (never changed afterwards) and is used from the next notification onnotifications.templates.manage
GET …/versions — the last 20 versions, live marks the one in use; POST …/rollback {"version": 1} uses an older one again; DELETE …/published stops using the templateread / notifications.templates.manage
POST …/preview {"source": "draft", "data": {…}} — render with the sample data or your values (only variables of the kind); nothing is sentnotifications.templates.read
POST …/test-send — send to yourself only: your verified email (email) or your inbox (in_app); 10 per hournotifications.templates.manage
GET / PUT /branding — name, logo (https), colors, footer of HTML emailsread / notifications.branding.manage

Fields: subject (email subject, push and inbox title), body_text (plain text: email text part, inbox), body_html (email only; omitted → made from body_text), short (SMS, ZNS, push), zns_template_id.

Every email has an HTML part in a branded MJML layout (rendered with mrml, made for Outlook, Gmail and phones) and a plain-text part. The footer shows the branding footer and the owner’s legal name and address (legal profile of compliance). Advertising always gets the label and the unsubscribe footer; a template cannot remove them. Text used when sending: the published template in use, else a replaced text (PUT /templates/{kind}/{channel}/{locale}), else the default text in the person’s language. A published template that fails with real data falls back to the default text; the message is still sent and marked error_code = template_fallback.

A module declares the variables of a kind with .variables(&[Variable::required("link", "…")]) and sample data with .sample(r#"{"link": "https://…"}"#); without them, the {name} places of the default text and link are allowed.

Declaring a kind in a module

Register the module after notifications in crates/app/src/modules.rs, then:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_notifications::api::{Category, Channel, Notification, NotificationKind, NotificationTemplate, Notifier, Recipient};

const SHIPPED: NotificationKind = NotificationKind::new(
    Category::Transactional,
    &[Channel::Email, Channel::InApp],
    NotificationTemplate::new(
        "orders.order_shipped",
        "Order {code} is on its way",
        "Your order {code} was handed to the carrier.",
        "Order {code} shipped",
    ),
);

// In Module::start:
let notifier = context.require::<dyn Notifier>().ok();
if let Some(notifier) = &notifier {
    notifier.declare(SHIPPED)?;
}

// In an event handler or a job:
let notification = Notification::new(SHIPPED.key(), Recipient::User(user_id), json!({"code": code}), event.id.to_string())
    .link(format!("/orders/{id}"));
notifier.notify(tenant_id, notification).await?;
}

Add orders.order_shipped.title, .body and .short to the module’s locales/vi.json (cargo xtask check asks for them). Advertising: Category::Marketing, optionally .purpose("…"); an invitation to sign up: .invitation().

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS90days the address and values of a message are kept in the send log
AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_INBOX_RETENTION_DAYS180days a notification stays in the inbox
AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_UNSUBSCRIBE_URL—your page that withdraws a consent, with {token}
AUTOXIDE_NOTIFICATIONS_PER_RECIPIENT_PER_HOUR20transactional and advertising notifications per recipient per hour

A daily job (notifications.purge) applies the retention times. A person’s inbox, preferences, devices and send log are part of their personal data export; when their account is deleted they are removed (the send log keeps the rows without address or values).

OpenSSF badges: Scorecard and Best Practices

English · Tiếng Việt

Two independent OpenSSF programs measure how safely an open-source project is run. Autoxide uses both.

OpenSSF Scorecard (automatic)

Scorecard scores the repository on checks such as pinned dependencies, token permissions, code review, branch protection, signed releases and fuzzing. The workflow .github/workflows/scorecard.yml runs it weekly and on every push to main, publishes the result and uploads it to the Security tab. Nothing to do per release.

Add the badge to the README once the first run has published:

[![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/OWNER/REPO/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/OWNER/REPO)

Some checks depend on repository settings that a workflow cannot change. The maintainers must set them in Settings → Branches (branch protection or a ruleset on main): require pull requests, require the gate (…) status checks, require at least one approving review, require review from code owners (so changes under .github/ and scripts/ need the owners), block force pushes. Turning these on is the largest single improvement of the score.

OpenSSF Best Practices badge (answered on the web)

The Best Practices badge is a questionnaire the maintainers answer, with evidence links. It has three levels: passing, silver and gold. Steps:

  1. Sign in at bestpractices.dev with the GitHub account of a maintainer and add the repository.

  2. Answer the questions. Most can be answered with a link from this repository:

    CriterionEvidence in this repository
    Project website, descriptionREADME.md
    How to contributeCONTRIBUTING.md, GOVERNANCE.md
    FLOSS licenseLICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE (dual-licensed)
    Documentationdocs/, the OpenAPI contract docs/openapi.json
    HTTPS for the project siteGitHub Pages and github.com
    Public version-controlled sourceGitHub
    Unique version numbers, release notesSemVer tags, CHANGELOG.md
    Bug-reporting process.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/, SUPPORT.md
    Vulnerability reporting processSECURITY.md (private reporting, response times)
    Working build systemcargo build; reproducible build in docs/COMPATIBILITY.md
    Automated test suite./gate.sh, .github/workflows/ci.yml
    New functionality has testsRule in CONTRIBUTING.md, checked in review
    Warning flags / lintersClippy, cargo xtask check, zizmor, actionlint
    Static analysisCodeQL (codeql.yml), Clippy
    Dynamic analysis, fuzzingfuzz/ and .github/workflows/fuzz.yml
    Known vulnerabilities fixedcargo deny in CI, nightly audit.yml, Dependabot
    Secrets are not stored in gitgitleaks in CI
    Signed releases / provenanceRelease workflow (see docs/RELEASING.md)
    Reproducible builds (gold)docs/COMPATIBILITY.md, “Reproducible builds”
    Two-person review (gold)Branch protection; needs a second maintainer

  3. Copy the badge snippet bestpractices.dev gives you (it contains the numeric project id) into the README.

Be honest in the answers: a criterion marked “met” must be true and the evidence link must show it. Criteria that are not yet true (for example the second reviewer for gold) stay “unmet” until they are.

Who does what

StepWho
Scorecard and CodeQL workflowsDone in the repository
Branch protection on mainProject owner (repo settings)
Enable private vulnerability reportingProject owner (repo settings)
Create the Best Practices entry, answer itProject owner (web)
Add both badges to the READMEAny contributor, after the above

Plans, subscriptions and limits

Tiếng Việt

The plans module lets you sell Autoxide by plan without changing code. A plan is data: which modules a tenant may use, which features are on, how much it may use (limits), and its prices. Tenants get a plan through a subscription; the kernel enforces it on every request, MCP tool, job and event.

Nothing changes until you create a plan: a tenant with no subscription gets the default plan, and with no default plan it is not limited at all. The platform tenant (the operator) is never limited.

Everything below is done by platform staff — users of the platform tenant holding plans.plans.manage / plans.subscriptions.manage — over REST (/api/v1/plans/...) or MCP (plans.* tools).

Create a plan

See which modules, features and limits exist in GET /api/v1/kernel/modules (features, limits, always_enabled, requires). Modules marked always_enabled (sign-in, files, audit…) are on for everyone.

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/plans/plans \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"code": "pro", "name": "Pro", "status": "active", "trial_days": 14,
       "modules": ["content", "media", "forms"],
       "features": ["content.ai_suggestions", "auth.api_keys"],
       "limits": {"organizations.units": 10, "auth.members": 25,
                  "files.storage_bytes": 10737418240, "kernel.api_requests": null}}'
  • A limit set to null is unlimited; a limit left out is 0.
  • A limit that has parts (parts in GET /api/v1/kernel/modules) also takes a cap per part: "organizations.units.store": 2 allows at most 2 units of type store, within the overall organizations.units. A part left out has no cap of its own.
  • A base plan that turns on a module must turn on the modules it needs (requires), or the request answers plans.module_dependency_missing.
  • "is_default": true makes it the plan of tenants without a subscription (only one plan is the default).
  • "kind": "addon" makes an add-on: its limits are added on top of the base plan, times the quantity bought.
  • Lifecycle settings per plan: grace_days (7), suspend_days (30), retention_days (90), renewal_lead_days (7).

Add a price with POST /api/v1/plans/plans/{id}/prices ({"kind": "recurring", "interval": "month", "amount": {"amount": "199000", "currency": "VND"}}). Prices never change: add a new one and deactivate the old one (POST /prices/{id}/deactivate); subscriptions keep their price until they change plan. A plan is never deleted, only retired (POST /plans/{id}/retire).

Create a tenant on a plan

Platform staff with plans.provision create a tenant ready to use in one call: the tenant, its subscription, the sample data of the modules the plan turns on (when the plan or the request asks), and an email invitation of its administrator with the role admin.

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/plans/provisionings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"slug": "acme", "name": "Acme Ltd", "plan_id": "...", "admin_email": "owner@acme.example"}'

It runs in the background: follow it with GET /api/v1/plans/provisionings/{id} (steps, and error when it failed); fix the cause, then POST …/retry goes on from the last step done. From the server: autoxide tenant create --slug acme --name "Acme Ltd" --plan <plan id> --admin-email owner@acme.example does the same at once. A dedicated plan needs placement: a placement of kind dedicated added first with autoxide placement add. A plan that requires_kyc cannot be provisioned by staff: the tenant signs up by itself and passes the identity checks (next section).

Tenants sign up by themselves

Turn it on with AUTOXIDE_PLANS_SIGNUP=true and mark the plans people may pick with "self_signup": true (active base plans). The sign-up page of your website talks to the API on the platform host (or sends Autoxide-Tenant: <platform slug>), without signing in:

  1. GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=plans:signup for a form token, then POST /api/v1/plans/signups with email, tenant_name, slug, plan_code, "accept_terms": true (the person accepts the platform’s current terms of use and privacy policy) and the form_token. The answer is always 202; invalid values answer 422 with every problem at once (plan_code not open to sign-up, slug taken…).
  2. A mail goes to the address with a link valid 24 hours (AUTOXIDE_PLANS_SIGNUP_URL, with {token}; without it the mail carries the token). The page sends the token to POST /api/v1/plans/signups/confirm: the acceptance of the terms is recorded (module compliance), and
    • for a plan that requires_kyc, the sign-up becomes awaiting_kyc and kyc.url is where the person passes the identity checks (calling confirm again starts new checks; after them the provider sends the person to AUTOXIDE_PLANS_SIGNUP_RETURN_URL). Passed → the tenant is created; failed → rejected (kyc_rejected);
    • otherwise the tenant is created at once.
  3. Creating the tenant is the same provisioning staff run (provisioning_id); the person is invited by mail as the administrator (role admin). Follow it with GET /api/v1/plans/signups/{id}?token=…: pending_email → (awaiting_kyc) → provisioning → completed (tenant_id), or rejected (reason) / expired.

Sending the same email and slug again while waiting sends a new mail (the old link stops working). Two people waiting for the same slug: the first to reach the provisioning keeps it, the other is rejected (tenant_slug_taken). Unconfirmed sign-ups expire after 24 hours, unfinished identity checks after 30 days; ended sign-ups are deleted 30 days later. Staff list them with GET /api/v1/plans/signups (plans.subscriptions.read, MCP plans.list_signups).

Put a tenant on a plan

curl -X PUT https://api.example.com/api/v1/plans/tenants/$TENANT/subscription \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"plan_id": "...", "price_id": "...", "addons": [{"plan_id": "...", "quantity": 2}]}'

The first time this starts the plan’s trial (unless "trial": false, or the tenant already had one). For one tenant you can also turn a module or feature on or off, or replace a limit, with a reason and an optional end: POST /api/v1/plans/tenants/{id}/overrides.

Changes take effect at once on the server that made them and within AUTOXIDE_PLANS_CACHE_SECONDS (default 30) on the others.

What tenants see

  • GET /api/v1/plans/entitlements (any signed-in user): modules, features, each limit with its use, and access (full or read_only) — user interfaces hide what the plan does not include.
  • An endpoint of a module the plan does not include answers 403 module_not_enabled; a feature 403 feature_not_enabled; a full limit 403 limit_exceeded; the monthly request quota 429 quota_exhausted (only when the plan sets a maximum).
  • With plans.billing.read / plans.billing.manage: GET /subscription, GET /usage, GET /billing-periods, POST /subscription/change (an upgrade applies at once and bills the rest of the period; a downgrade applies when the period ends), POST /subscription/cancel, POST /subscription/resume.

Lifecycle

StatusAccessNext
trialingfulltrial ends: free plan → active; priced → paid next period → active, else past_due
activefullperiod ends: next period paid (or free) → new period; unpaid → past_due
past_duefull (grace)paid → active; grace_days pass → suspended
suspendedread-onlypaid → active; suspend_days pass → canceled
canceledread-onlyresumed before delete_after → active; retention_days pass → deleted
deletednonethe tenant and its data are deleted for good (accounting records modules must keep stay)

A job moves subscriptions every 5 minutes. renewal_lead_days before a period ends, the next billing period is opened and a reminder is mailed to the subscription’s billing email (AUTOXIDE_PLANS_REMINDER_DAYS, default 7,1), again when overdue and every 3 days of the grace period.

Payments (manual for now)

Until a payment provider is connected (step 36), billing periods are paid outside the system: check the bank transfer, then POST /api/v1/plans/billing-periods/{id}/mark-paid ({"provider_reference": "..."}); a past-due or suspended subscription becomes active again. POST /billing-periods/{id}/void cancels a period opened by mistake.

Platform staff see a tenant’s billing periods with GET /api/v1/plans/tenants/{id}/billing-periods and its billing profile (legal name, tax code, invoice email, address — the tenant sets it with PUT /api/v1/plans/billing-profile) with GET /api/v1/plans/tenants/{id}/billing-profile.

To block a tenant completely (reads too), use POST /api/v1/plans/tenants/{id}/subscription/suspend with a reason; undo it with PATCH /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id} ("status": "active"). GET /api/v1/kernel/tenants?subscription_status=past_due and ?near_limit=true list tenants to follow up.

Exporting a tenant’s data

Platform staff (kernel.tenants.operate) and administrators of the tenant itself (kernel.data.export) can export all of a tenant’s data as one JSON Lines file: POST /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/exports, then GET …/exports/{export_id} until it is ready, then GET …/exports/{export_id}/content (or POST …/link for a 24-hour link that works without signing in). The first line describes the export; every other line is {"table": "...", "row": {...}}. Password hashes and secrets are left out, and so are the contents of uploaded files (their records are included; download them through the files API). When a subscription is canceled an export is started automatically. Exports are deleted after AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_EXPORT_RETENTION_DAYS (30).

Deleting a tenant

POST /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/erase (kernel.tenants.delete, with {"confirm": "<slug>", "reason": "..."}) deletes a suspended tenant and its data for good; it cannot be undone. A subscription that passes its retention period does this by itself.

Settings

SettingDefault
AUTOXIDE_PLANS_CACHE_SECONDS30How long each server keeps a tenant’s entitlements in memory

Promotions

Tiếng Việt

The promotions module runs discounts as rules. A promotion reaches buyers in one of three ways: automatically, by coupon (a code anyone holding it can use) or as a voucher (a one-time right in one account’s wallet). Orders compute a cart, hold the usage of the promotions when the order is placed, confirm it when paid and release it when cancelled, through autoxide_promotions::api::Promotions. Everything is under /api/v1/promotions; every endpoint is described in docs/openapi.json, and the main operations are MCP tools (promotions.*).

Promotions

  • POST /promotions creates a draft. Every promotion has a start and a required end (ends_at). trigger is automatic, code or voucher; scope is items, order or shipping, which gives the stacking class product, order or shipping.
  • Kinds: percent_off, amount_off (per item for items, per order for order), fixed_price, buy_x_get_y (reward_selection: cheapest, same_item, specified; reward_value_bp 10000 = free), free_shipping, flash_sale (prices per variant with real units left), tiered (the highest tier reached), bundle_price (“3 items for 199,000”), add_on (a deal price for an extra item when a qualifying item is bought), gift_choice (the buyer picks gifts; free items come back as separate lines at price 0).
  • Conditions: targets (products, variants, categories with their subcategories), customer groups, channels, first order only, minimum order or quantity, and extra conditions on payment method, carrier, province, membership tier, client (web, app, pos), seller, new / returning customers, items already discounted, excluded targets; time windows per weekday in the store’s time zone.
  • Targets, flash-sale prices and translations have their own endpoints (PUT /promotions/{id}/targets, /flash-items, /translations/{locale}).
  • After a promotion is turned on, only a later end, more uses / budget / vouchers and its texts can change (promotions.locked_after_start); every change is kept in GET /promotions/{id}/versions.

Turning on and the law

POST /promotions/{id}/activation-check lists the checks without changing anything; POST /promotions/{id}/activate runs the same checks and fails with every failed check in errors:

  • the discount limit in force (50% of the price just before the promotion in Viet Nam, unlimited for a national promotion programme), using the catalog’s price history. Decree 239/2026/ND-CP (26 June 2026) repealed the limits of Decree 81/2018/ND-CP Articles 6 and 7 and left them to the Ministry of Industry and Trade; the circular is not found yet, so pack vn version 2 keeps 50% as a cautious default with the new basis, and keeps the 120 discount days a year that one summary says the decree dropped — check the original texts;
  • discount days per programme and per year;
  • the promotion notice recorded for each authority (PATCH /promotions/{id}/notices/{authority}; the province comes from the unit setting promotions.notice_province);
  • targets, and the catalog’s price floors (block stops, warn warns); conflicts are warnings.

Limits and notice rules are data with effective dates, not code: load them with autoxide task promotions.load_legal_data (the pack vn ships with the server, with its legal basis and “to be checked” notes) and read them at GET /legal-limits?at= and GET /notice-rules?at=. Without data in force a promotion cannot be turned on (promotions.no_legal_data). The pack was compiled from secondary sources: have it checked by a legal professional before real use.

To prepare the notices, GET /promotions/{id}/notice-export?format=json|csv (permission promotions.compliance and promotions.read; MCP tool promotions.export_notice) gives one entry per authority: whether a notice is required under the rules in force on the start day, the last day to submit, the legal basis and what was recorded. People submit the notice to the authority; Autoxide only prepares the data and records it.

A coupon, step by step

With API, TOKEN and ORG (your unit) as in the shop guide. The paths in this page are under /api/v1/promotions, so a promotion is at /api/v1/promotions/promotions/{id}.

P="$API/api/v1/promotions/promotions"
# 1. The province that receives your notices: a setting of your unit (units below it inherit it).
curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/organizations/units/$ORG/settings/promotions.notice_province" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"value": "01"}'

# 2. A draft: 10% off with a code, from now for 30 days.
PROMO=$(curl -sS "$P" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"trigger\": \"code\", \"kind\": \"percent_off\", \"value_bp\": 1000,
       \"currency\": \"VND\", \"locale\": \"vi\", \"title\": \"Giảm 10%\", \"terms\": \"Nhập mã GIAM10\",
       \"starts_at\": \"$(jq -rn 'now | todate')\", \"ends_at\": \"$(jq -rn 'now + 30 * 86400 | todate')\"}" \
  | jq -r .data.id)

# 3. The code buyers type (`"count": 100` instead of `code` generates codes).
curl -sS "$P/$PROMO/codes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"purpose": "redeem", "code": "GIAM10"}'

# 4. What is still missing: a `promotions.notice_required` check names its authority, e.g. `province:01`.
curl -sS -X POST "$P/$PROMO/activation-check" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.data.checks'

# 5. Record the notice you submitted to that authority, then turn the promotion on.
curl -sS -X PATCH "$P/$PROMO/notices/province:01" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status": "submitted", "reference": "123/TB-SCT"}'
curl -sS -X POST "$P/$PROMO/activate" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
  • purpose is redeem for the coupon of a code promotion and claim for the claim code of a voucher promotion. A code taken by another promotion is refused (promotions.code_taken).
  • The setting holds the province code (GET /api/v1/address/provinces); without it the authority is province:unknown. {"status": "not_required"} records that no notice is needed.
  • Prices must exist before the promotion starts. The legal limit is computed from the price just before starts_at, and a price counts only from its valid_from (now, when you leave it out). A promotion that starts before the product’s first price gives that product no discount (withheld, reason promotions.reason.no_reference_price). Start the promotion after the price was set, or give the price an earlier valid_from when you add it (POST /api/v1/catalog/price-lists/{id}/prices).

Computing a cart

POST /evaluate (and Promotions::evaluate) computes a cart without holding anything:

  1. candidates: running, in their window, of the store or its parents (a seller’s promotions only on the seller’s items), conditions met; coupons and vouchers open their promotions — a wrong code or voucher comes back in rejected_codes with a reason, the cart still works;
  2. the product class, then order on what is left, then shipping. Two promotions stack only when both allow it (exclusivity, combines_with); stop_after stops lower priorities in the class. The unit setting promotions.stacking_mode picks priority (default, predictable) or best_for_buyer;
  3. the legal limit per line adds every discount (all classes, platform and seller vouchers together); the later discount is cut first (capped_by_law), then the price floor (capped_by_floor). A product with no price before the promotion gets no discount (withheld);
  4. each discount is shared among its payers (funding: platform, seller, brand, payment partner) to the cent; reasons are translated to the cart’s locale.

Percentages are rounded half up on the line total; order discounts are shared to lines in proportion to their amounts. The same cart always gives the same result and fingerprint.

A website menu can point to a promotion: the type promotions.promotion in the resource directory is public only while a public promotion runs, with its title, conditions and the standard path /promotions/<id>.

Sellers in platform promotions

On a marketplace, a seller joins a platform flash sale that has not started: POST /promotions/{id}/participations (permission promotions.participate on the seller’s unit, below the unit running the promotion) with the seller’s own products, each with a sale price or a discount and the units offered. The platform approves or rejects it (POST …/participations/{participation_id}/approve or /reject, permission promotions.publish); approved products join the flash sale and their discount is paid by the seller (funding). GET …/participations shows every application to the platform and their own to sellers.

Planning

All read-only, permission promotions.read:

  • POST /promotions/{id}/simulate {"carts": [...]} (1 to 20 carts, MCP tool promotions.simulate): each cart computed with the promotion (a draft works too) and without it, and difference_minor;
  • GET /promotions/{id}/conflicts: other promotions of the unit at the same time, on shared targets and in the same class, where one side is exclusive (only one of them applies to a line);
  • GET /promotions/calendar?from=&to=&org_id=: promotions running on those days (Vietnam dates, up to 366);
  • GET /promotions/{id}/stats?from=&to=: confirmed uses, discount, order value and who paid, per day.

Holding usage

Promotions::reserve recomputes the cart and holds, in one transaction, every counter: uses of the promotion and of the code, uses per buyer key (account, hashed phone, hashed address — a new account with the same phone gets no extra use), uses per day, budget, flash-sale units, gifts and vouchers. All or nothing; the same order and cart again returns the same hold. A different result from the one the buyer saw fails with promotions.changed. confirm makes it final; release gives the usage back (after confirmation only for promotions with return_usage_on_cancel; vouchers return to the wallet while valid). Holds not confirmed expire (promotions.expire_holds, every minute).

Vouchers

Buyers save the voucher of a claimable promotion (POST /public/promotions/{id}/claim), enter a claim code (POST /me/vouchers/claim-code, tries are limited) or receive one through grant_voucher (loyalty, birthday, compensation…; the same source + source_ref never gives twice) or by hand with a reason (POST /promotions/{id}/vouchers). GET /me/vouchers lists the wallet. The wallet is in the personal data export; deleting an account revokes unused vouchers.

On the website

GET /public/promotions?locale=&site= (no sign-in) lists the promotions marked public running now on a website: those of its unit and of the units above it, with their full conditions, the notices recorded with the Departments of Industry and Trade (authority and reference) and the largest discount the law in force today allows (legal_limit, from the law data). Pages with limit / cursor; send the ETag back in If-None-Match to get 304.

GET /public/promotions/for-product/{product_id}?variant_id=&site= lists the public coupons that lower the price of one variant, cheapest first: the price of one unit with the coupon, its conditions and the uses left (only when there is a real limit). The listed price stays the price without a coupon — show “X with code …”, not a discounted price. For a cart, Promotions::eligible (served by orders) gives the coupons and vouchers that work, those that do not yet with a reason (“add X to use”), and the best selection, so a picker can replace the code box.

GET /public/promotions/flash-sales?site= lists the public flash sales running now or starting within a day, with their products, sale prices and the units left at the sale price (a real count: held and sold units are taken off). A signed-in buyer can ask to be reminded before one starts (POST /public/promotions/{id}/reminders, permission promotions.use; DELETE cancels): one reminder is sent through notifications ten minutes before the start. Asking is recorded in the consent ledger as consent to that one reminder, not to advertising.

Returns

api::returns has the rules for orders: the refund of a line is the amount paid × returned / bought, the last unit taking the remainder; order discounts are taken back only when the unit setting promotions.clawback_on_return is proportional; gifts follow the promotion’s gift_return_policy.
