Public roadmap

A short English overview of where Autoxide is going. It deliberately does not list individual tasks: the single source of truth is docs/ROADMAP.md, the working plan of the maintainers and their AI agents, written in Vietnamese (translate it with any tool; item titles are plain technical text). Changes of direction go through GOVERNANCE.md (RFCs in docs/rfcs/).

Where we are

The latest release is in the 0.x series. Feature freeze until 1.0: no new business modules; the work is the stable contract, upgrades, AI-agent standards, onboarding and community standards. It is tracked as “step 71” of the roadmap, in groups G1 to G14.

What 1.0 means

The first release with a stability promise (docs/COMPATIBILITY.md):

  • A stable tier (REST API and OpenAPI, error codes, configuration, migrations, MCP tools, events and webhooks, the CLI, the Rust API for modules, the TypeScript SDK) that breaks only in a major release, and an experimental tier that is labelled and may change in a minor one.
  • One-step upgrades and rollback, with library major versions isolated behind kernel layers.
  • Both SQLite and PostgreSQL, always.
  • Standard sign-in for AI agents (MCP with OAuth 2.1), extension without writing Rust, and the community and supply-chain standards of an open-source project.
  • Exit criteria: every roadmap item of step 71 done, the full gate green on both databases, an external security test with no high-severity finding, legal review of personal data, e-invoicing and tax, and measured quality goals.

After 1.0

Business modules wait until after 1.0. New modules are best written outside this repository against the stable contract: see docs/MODULE_ECOSYSTEM.md.

Rules every change follows

The same rules apply to people and AI agents; the short list is in CONTRIBUTING.md and the full text in CLAUDE.md.

How to take part

  • Pick a good first issue or help wanted.
  • Propose bigger changes as an RFC.
  • Build and share a module: docs/MODULE_ECOSYSTEM.md.
  • Ask questions in Discussions (SUPPORT.md).

Runbook

English · Tiếng Việt

What to do when something goes wrong in production, in the order to do it. Every command and endpoint here exists in this version (the CLI help, docs/openapi.json and the metric names were checked against the code). The per-alert cases (server errors, slow requests, connections, backups, the last administrator) are in the runbook of DEPLOY.md; this page covers the incidents that need a decision and a sequence of steps.

How to use this page

  1. Contain first, explain later. Stop the damage (suspend a tenant, revoke a key, take a server out of rotation), then find the cause.
  2. Write down what you do and when (a plain text log in your incident channel). You will need it for the review, and for a data breach notice if personal data was exposed (DEPLOY.md).
  3. Never paste secrets, tokens or personal data into tickets or chat. Refer to a request_id instead; every error response carries one.
  4. First command for almost everything: autoxide doctor (add --json for scripts and AI agents). It changes nothing and says what is wrong and how to fix it.

In the commands below, API is the address of the API, TOKEN is an access token of a user with the permission the step names, and jq is installed.

Before an incident

  • Prometheus scrapes /metrics (AUTOXIDE_HTTP_METRICS=true, own port) and loads deploy/prometheus/autoxide-alerts.yml; the Grafana dashboard deploy/grafana/autoxide-dashboard.json is imported.
  • Scheduled backups run (autoxide doctor warns when not), are copied off the storage they sit on, and a restore was practised on a spare machine (DEPLOY.md).
  • At least two people can sign in as platform staff, and at least one can run autoxide on the server (autoxide user create … --admin makes a new administrator if every one is locked out).
  • The secrets (AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY, AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET) are stored outside the repository and outside the database backups, and you know where.

Database full or slow

Full (writes fail with “no space left on device”): free or add disk space first, then see DEPLOY.md, “Database full”. SQLite: look at the size of the database file and its -wal file (a long read such as a backup keeps -wal growing). PostgreSQL: the largest tables with SELECT relname, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) FROM pg_statio_user_tables ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC LIMIT 10;. Finished jobs and delivered events are removed after 7 days by themselves.

Slow (alert AutoxideSlowP95, requests waiting): check database_connections{state="in_use"} against database_connections_max (alert AutoxideDbPoolExhausted); on PostgreSQL look at pg_stat_activity for long queries, on SQLite remember there is one write connection by design. A query without an index belongs in a new migration of the module that owns the table (EXPLAIN ANALYZE on PostgreSQL, EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN on SQLite). Raise AUTOXIDE_DATABASE_READ_CONNECTIONS / AUTOXIDE_DATABASE_WRITE_CONNECTIONS only after ending what holds connections, and keep the total of all processes under PostgreSQL’s max_connections.

Background queue backlog

Signs: alerts AutoxideJobsStuck, AutoxideEventsBacklog, AutoxideDeadLetterGrowing; mail, webhooks, exports arrive late.

  1. Is a worker running? At least one process must have AUTOXIDE_PROCESS_ROLE set to all or worker; check its /health/ready and logs.
  2. Which module is behind? jobs_pending and jobs_oldest_pending_seconds by module and database, or, as platform staff with kernel.ops.read: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/v1/kernel/ops/backlog".
  3. Multi-tenant: a database being migrated answers 503 tenant_maintenance and its work waits; let autoxide migrate up --all finish.
  4. Jobs that gave up: autoxide jobs failed [--module <module>] [--limit <n>] lists them with the last error. Fix the cause (a wrong SMTP password, a partner down) before autoxide jobs retry <module> <id>; a job retried too early only fails again.
  5. Still behind with a healthy worker: raise AUTOXIDE_JOBS_CONCURRENCY or start more worker processes.

A key leaked

Decide which key, then rotate it. Do not wait to be sure.

The access token signing key (AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET). An attacker who has it can forge access tokens.

  1. Generate a new value: openssl rand -base64 48.
  2. Set it on every server and restart them. Do not put the leaked value in AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET_PREVIOUS (that variable keeps an old key accepted for a smooth routine change).
  3. Every access token stops working at once; clients get a new one with their refresh token, which stays valid. If the refresh tokens may be stolen too, also sign users out: see mass revocation.

The encryption key (AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY). It encrypts stored secrets (two-step sign-in secrets, webhook signing secrets, provider credentials) and keys the hashes of visitors’ IP addresses.

  1. Set the new value, and the old one in AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS, on every server; restart.
  2. Run autoxide migrate up once if you upgraded, then autoxide secrets reseal: it encrypts every stored secret again with the new key.
  3. Remove AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY_PREVIOUS from every server and restart.
  4. Backups made before the rotation still open with the old key: delete them or keep them as safe as the key was. If the database (or a backup) leaked together with the key, the secrets inside must be treated as exposed: ask the tenants to rotate their provider credentials and webhook secrets.

An API key or a provider credential. Revoke the key (DELETE /api/v1/auth/all-api-keys/{id} for any user’s key, with auth.users.manage; users revoke their own with DELETE /api/v1/auth/api-keys/{id}); POST /api/v1/auth/api-keys/{id}/rotate replaces one with a new key. A provider credential (payment, SMS, shipping) is changed in the provider’s console first, then in the tenant’s settings.

Mass revocation of API keys and sessions

Use it when accounts or devices may be compromised and you cannot tell which. Containment first:

  • Stop one tenant completely: autoxide tenant suspend <id-or-slug> (every request to it answers 403) or PATCH /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id} with {"status": "suspended", "reason": "…"} (permission kernel.tenants.manage, platform staff). Undo with autoxide tenant resume <id-or-slug> or "status": "active". For “readable but not changeable” use autoxide tenant read-only <id-or-slug> or {"read_only": true}, undone by autoxide tenant writable.

  • Sign one user out everywhere: DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/sessions (permission auth.users.manage). An access token already issued keeps working until it expires (15 minutes by default, AUTOXIDE_AUTH_ACCESS_TOKEN_SECONDS). Disabling the account (PATCH /api/v1/auth/users/{id}) stops new sign-ins.

  • Sign every user of a tenant out: there is no single call; loop over the users (the list is paged: limit up to 200, cursor from pagination.next_cursor):

    cursor=""
while :; do
  page="$(curl -sf -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/v1/auth/users?limit=200${cursor:+&cursor=$cursor}")"
  jq -r '.data[].id' <<<"$page" | while read -r id; do
    curl -sf -X DELETE -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/v1/auth/users/$id/sessions" >/dev/null
  done
  cursor="$(jq -r '.pagination.next_cursor // empty' <<<"$page")"
  [ -n "$cursor" ] || break
done

    Then change AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET (see “A key leaked”) so access tokens die at once instead of within 15 minutes.

  • Revoke every API key of a tenant: list them with GET /api/v1/auth/all-api-keys (same paging) and call DELETE /api/v1/auth/all-api-keys/{id} for each; build the loop like the one above. Re-issue the keys that are legitimate afterwards (POST /api/v1/auth/api-keys).

  • A user who lost a device or a second factor: autoxide user reset-mfa and autoxide user remove-passkeys on the server, or DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/mfa and DELETE /api/v1/auth/users/{id}/passkeys through the API.

Afterwards read the audit log for what the compromised credentials did (see a customer reports lost data).

Restoring one tenant from a backup

There is no command that restores one tenant into a live shared database: it would overwrite newer data of that tenant with old data and cannot be undone. Choose by how the tenant is stored.

  • The tenant has its own database (its own placement). Restore that placement’s database from its backup as in DEPLOY.md, or from a PostgreSQL point-in-time recovery to the second before the mistake. Suspend the tenant first (autoxide tenant suspend <id-or-slug>), restore, run autoxide doctor and autoxide migrate up --all, then autoxide tenant resume <id-or-slug>.

  • The tenant shares the main database. Restore the backup into a temporary installation (a spare database and storage, the same AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY):

    # on the spare machine, DATABASE_URL and the storage settings point at EMPTY targets
autoxide restore ./restore-dir        # applies the migrations, copies every table and file
autoxide doctor
autoxide serve

    There, read the tenant’s data (the API, or POST /api/v1/kernel/tenants/{id}/exports, permission kernel.data.export, then GET …/exports/{export_id}/content), and put back what was lost through the live API: single records (POST/PATCH of the module), a revision (POST /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/revisions/{revision_id}/restore), an item in the trash (POST /api/v1/media/{id}/restore), CSV imports where the module has one (for example POST /api/v1/catalog/imports). For a large loss, moving the tenant to its own placement (autoxide tenant move … --dry-run first) gives it a database that can be restored alone next time.

  • Afterwards run the module’s own checks where they exist (autoxide task inventory.verify_levels, autoxide task catalog.rebuild_storefront tenant=<slug>) and tell the tenant what was restored and what is lost (everything changed after the backup).

A customer reports lost data

  1. Do not change anything yet. Note the tenant, the record, the time the customer last saw it, and who can act in the tenant.
  2. Look for what happened. The audit log (permission audit.read): curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "$API/api/v1/audit?subject=<record id>&limit=50"; narrow with module, action, actor_user_id, actor_kind (a person, an API key or an AI agent). The request log of the tenant (GET /api/v1/kernel/devtools/requests, permission kernel.devtools.read) shows recent signed-in calls for AUTOXIDE_REQUEST_LOG_DAYS days (default 14). Search the server logs with the request_id and with tenant_id (see “Monitoring”).
  3. It was deleted or changed by someone legitimate: most deletions can be undone from the module — a content revision (POST /api/v1/content/entries/{id}/revisions/{revision_id}/restore), a media item in the trash (POST /api/v1/media/{id}/restore). Otherwise take the old value from the audit entry and write it back through the API.
  4. It was done by a credential that should not have acted: treat it as a compromise: revoke (mass revocation), then restore as above.
  5. No trace of a change and the data is simply gone: suspect the platform: check autoxide doctor, the migration history (autoxide migrate status), recent deployments and manual database access. Restore from a backup or point-in-time recovery (above).
  6. Tell the customer what you found, what was restored and what could not be. If personal data was exposed or lost, follow DEPLOY.md, “Personal data breaches” (deadlines apply).

Monitoring: what to watch and when to alert

Enable AUTOXIDE_HTTP_METRICS=true and give /metrics its own port (AUTOXIDE_HTTP_METRICS_ADDRESS); never expose it to the internet. With OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT set, traces are exported too, carrying tenant_id (metrics have no tenant label by design; look a tenant up in logs and traces).

Watch (metric)HealthyAlert (file autoxide-alerts.yml)Then
http_requests_total{status=~"5.."} over all requestsunder 1%AutoxideHigh5xxRate above 2% for 10 minDEPLOY.md “Server errors”
http_request_duration_seconds p95 by routeunder 0.5 sAutoxideSlowP95 for 10 min“Database full or slow”
database_connections{state="in_use"} / …_maxunder 70%AutoxideDbPoolExhausted at 90%“Database full or slow”
jobs_oldest_pending_seconds, events_oldest_pending_secondssecondsAutoxideJobsStuck, AutoxideEventsBacklog“Background queue backlog”
jobs_dead, events_dead0AutoxideDeadLetterGrowingautoxide jobs failed
backup_last_success_timestamp_seconds, backup_runs_total{outcome="failed"}within one intervalAutoxideBackupTooOld, AutoxideBackupFailedDEPLOY.md “Backups”
http_rate_limited_total, http_api_key_rate_limited_total, http_tenant_rate_limited_totalnear 0AutoxideRateLimitedClients above 1/s for 15 min“Mass revocation”
webhooks_failed_total vs webhooks_delivered_totalunder 5% failingAutoxideWebhooksFailing above 20% for 30 minthe receivers’ owners
mail_bounces_total{kind="hard"}fewAutoxideMailHardBounces above 20 per hourDEPLOY.md “Mail that bounces”

Other series worth a panel (no alert by default): database_write_retries_total (write contention), kernel_request_log_dropped_total (request log overloaded), entitlement_denials_total (plan limits hit), mcp_tool_calls_total (agent traffic), jobs_retried_total, backup_size_bytes and backup_duration_seconds (growth).

Thresholds are starting points: watch for a few weeks, then tighten them to what is normal for your deployment. Every alert has an action annotation that says what to do; add routing (severity page wakes someone, warn goes to a channel) in Alertmanager.

After the incident

Within a week write a short review: what happened and when, how it was found, what was done, what it cost, and what changes so it does not happen again (an alert, a check, a step added to this page). Fix the runbook where reality differed from it. A vulnerability in Autoxide itself goes through SECURITY.md, not a public issue.

Shipping (shipping module)

Tiếng Việt

The shipping module keeps buyers’ address books, computes shipping rates set by each shop, plugs in shipping carriers as connector modules, follows shipments and reconciles cash on delivery (COD). It does not depend on orders or catalog: orders quote through autoxide_shipping::api and send shipment requests as events.

Address book

Signed-in buyers keep up to AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_MAX_ADDRESSES_PER_BUYER (default 20) addresses:

MethodPathWho
GET, POST/api/v1/shipping/me/addressesany signed-in account, own addresses only
GET, PATCH, DELETE/api/v1/shipping/me/addresses/{id}same
POST/api/v1/shipping/me/addresses/{id}/defaultsame
GET/api/v1/shipping/buyers/{buyer_id}/addressesshipping.addresses.read (customer care)
  • Vietnam: province_code and commune_code come from the official list of administrative units of the address module (two levels since 2025-07-01). The commune must belong to the province and be in force; the names are saved with the address, so a later change of the list does not change saved addresses.
  • Other countries: a generic form — province_code is the region (state, province…), city the city, postal_code optional. In responses the city is address.commune_name and address.commune_code is empty.
  • Exactly one address is the default (the first one automatically). Deleting the default makes the most recently changed other address the default.
  • An address book is personal data: it is part of the account’s data export and is erased when the account is deleted. Shipments keep their own copy of the recipient.

Other modules read it through dyn AddressBook (get, default_for).

Shipping rates

Each shop sets its own rates under /api/v1/shipping (permission shipping.settings.manage at the unit):

MethodPathWhat
GET, POST/zoneszones: groups of provinces (or whole countries)
GET, PATCH, DELETE/zones/{id}one zone (deleting it removes its tiers)
PUT/zones/{id}/regionsreplace the provinces of a zone
GET, POST/methodsshipping methods: table_rate, carrier, pickup
GET, PATCH, DELETE/methods/{id}one method with its tiers and pickup points
PUT/methods/{id}/ratesreplace the weight tiers of a method
PUT/methods/{id}/pickup-pointsreplace the stores of a pickup method
POST/quotequote a cart (shipping.read at the store) — the same computation orders use
  • Inheritance: a store uses the active methods of its own unit and of every unit above it; a method of a nearer unit replaces one with the same code higher up (a store can override the chain’s standard).
  • Zones: a zone listing the destination province wins over a zone for the whole country.
  • Weight: chargeable weight = max(actual weight, volumetric weight); volumetric weight of an item = length × width × height (mm³) / volumetric_divisor (default 6000) grams, rounded up. Items that do not need shipping (digital goods, services) weigh nothing; a cart with none to ship gets no options. An item without weight uses the method’s default_item_weight_grams; without one, the method is listed in unavailable with shipping.weight_missing.
  • Tiers: min_weight_grams ≤ weight < max_weight_grams (no maximum = no limit) and longest side ≤ max_side_mm; each step_grams (or part) above the minimum adds step_amount. Overlapping tiers are refused.
  • Free shipping: free_over compared with the order value after discounts; the option shows free_over so a cart can say how much more to buy.
  • VAT: fees are VAT-inclusive; each option carries the method’s tax_category so the order puts the VAT line of the shipping fee on the invoice.
  • Store pickup: one option per store, fee = the method’s handling_fee, no destination or weight needed.
  • Every option has an option_key. Send it back when placing the order: ShippingRates::confirm_option answers shipping.option_changed when the fee or destination changed.

Carrier accounts

/api/v1/shipping/carrier-accounts (permission shipping.carriers.manage, plan feature shipping.carriers): GET, POST, PATCH /{id}, POST /{id}/test. Credentials are stored encrypted per tenant and never shown again (only credential_fields). The create answer holds webhook_path once — give it to the carrier. check_status (never, ok, failed) is set by the test call and whenever the carrier refuses the credentials. A carrier method quotes through its account; a carrier that does not answer within AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_CARRIER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS is listed in unavailable (shipping.carrier_unavailable) without breaking the quote.

Shipments

MethodPathPermission
GET/shipments?order_id&status&org_id&tracking, /shipments/{id}shipping.shipments.read
POST/shipments (by hand), /shipments/{id}/book, /cancel, /split, /statusshipping.shipments.manage
PUT/shipments/{id}/parcelsshipping.shipments.manage
GET/shipments/{id}/labelshipping.shipments.read
  • Orders ask for a shipment with the event orders.fulfillment_requested (returns: orders.return_pickup_requested), payload {"after": {"shipment": ShipmentRequest}}. The same order_id + request_key never creates a second shipment; the same key with other content is refused and logged. orders.order_cancelled cancels the shipments not picked up yet.
  • Statuses: pending, booking, ready_to_ship, picked_up, in_transit, out_for_delivery, delivered, delivery_failed, returning, returned, ready_for_pickup, picked_up_by_buyer, cancelled, lost. They only move forward along a fixed table (a new attempt after delivery_failed is allowed). Carrier updates that arrive late or out of order are kept in the tracking history but do not move the status back.
  • Booking calls the carrier outside any database transaction: pending → booking is saved first, then the carrier is called with the shipment id as client_reference. A shipment stuck in booking asks the carrier (find_by_reference) before ever booking again (every 5 minutes for shipments stuck over 10 minutes).
  • A method with auto_book books as soon as the order asks; otherwise staff check the goods and press book.
  • Parcels: one parcel at first; PUT /parcels splits the items into several parcels before booking. split moves some lines to a new shipment (partial delivery); cash on delivery stays with the original.
  • Events (after is a ShipmentEvent, without personal data): shipping.shipment_created, …_booked, …_status_changed, …_delivered, …_delivery_failed, …_returned, …_cancelled, shipping.booking_failed, shipping.cod_collected.

Carrier webhooks

POST /api/v1/shipping/webhooks/{carrier_code}/{hook}/{token} is public: hook names the tenant and token the carrier account, so the carrier sends no tenant header. This is the webhook_path of a new carrier account. The older address …/webhooks/{carrier_code}/{token} still works; there the tenant comes from the autoxide-tenant header or the domain. The connector checks the signature on the raw body; a wrong signature answers 401 and nothing is stored. A valid body is stored as received (secret headers removed) and answered 202; a job applies it. Repeated updates are applied once (event_key); bodies above AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_WEBHOOK_MAX_BYTES answer 413. Carriers without webhooks are polled every 30 minutes.

Cash on delivery (COD)

The carrier collects the cash and pays it to the seller under its contract; Autoxide only records who owes what and reconciles (it never holds the money). With the ledger module installed:

  • a delivered COD shipment records “the carrier owes the amount” (clearing.carrier_cod) against the buyer’s receivable;
  • POST /api/v1/shipping/cod/statements (permission shipping.cod.manage) imports a carrier statement: CSV with the columns tracking_number, cod_amount, fee (minor units) or fetch: true for carriers with a statement API. Matching lines settle the shipment (money in transit + carrier fee against what the carrier owed; event shipping.cod_settled with seller_org_id). The same reference with the same content is not imported twice.
  • Lines that differ (amount, unknown tracking number, not delivered) and COD still missing from statements after AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_COD_SETTLEMENT_DAYS become discrepancies (GET /cod/discrepancies, event shipping.cod_mismatch). Resolve one with a code of the reason list shipping.cod_resolution and a note; written_off writes the missing amount off. refresh-tracking asks the carrier for the latest tracking first. Statements and discrepancies can be read with shipping.cod.read (accounting, audit) or shipping.cod.manage.

Contract for other modules

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
let rates = context.require::<dyn autoxide_shipping::api::ShippingRates>()?;   // quote, confirm_option
let book = context.require::<dyn autoxide_shipping::api::AddressBook>()?;
let carriers = context.require::<dyn autoxide_shipping::api::CarrierRegistry>()?;
}

Register your module after shipping in crates/app/src/modules.rs. Build requests with the constructors (QuoteRequest::new, QuoteItem::new(…).weight(…), ShipmentRequest::new): the types are #[non_exhaustive] so new fields never break callers.

orders asks for a shipment by publishing orders.fulfillment_requested (or orders.return_pickup_requested) with {"after": {"shipment": <ShipmentRequest>}}; shipping answers with shipping.shipment_* events whose after is a ShipmentEvent (no personal data).

Writing a carrier connector

A connector is its own module (shipping-<carrier>) registered after shipping. It implements ShippingCarrier and registers it in Module::start:

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn start(&mut self, context: &mut StartContext<'_>) -> Result<(), Error> {
    let registry = context.require::<dyn autoxide_shipping::api::CarrierRegistry>()?;
    registry.register(Arc::new(MyCarrier::new()))
}
}

Rules every connector follows (see autoxide_shipping::api::fake::FakeCarrier for a complete example):

  • create_shipment must not create a second shipment for the same client_reference (the Autoxide shipment id); find_by_reference finds one created by a call whose answer was lost.
  • parse_webhook checks the signature on the raw body (constant-time comparison) before reading it, and returns shipping.webhook_signature when it is wrong.
  • Convert carrier times to UTC (Vietnamese carriers often send local time without a zone).
  • Map carrier statuses to the common ShipmentStatus; keep the carrier’s own text in carrier_status.
  • Never log credentials: CarrierCredentials hides its values from Debug.

AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_FAKE_CARRIER=true registers the fake carrier fake for trying everything on a development machine. autoxide doctor warns while it is on; never turn it on in production.

Delivery dates

Delivery calendars live under /api/v1/shipping/calendars (shipping.settings.manage): a time zone (default Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh), working days of the week, and special days set with PUT /calendars/{id}/days/{YYYY-MM-DD} — closed (holiday, entered when it is announced; nothing is hard-coded) or special_hours with its own cut-off. A method links a calendar (calendar_id), a daily cut-off (cutoff_minute, 660 = 11:00) and same_day.

Every option of a quote carries eta: earliest_date and latest_date as calendar dates in the calendar’s time zone (working days after the dispatch day), and order_by, today’s cut-off when it is still ahead. Methods without a calendar use Monday to Saturday, Vietnam time. Store pickup options carry ready_at (order time + the pickup point’s prep_hours, moved to the next opening time of the store from its public profile, 08:00–21:00 when the store has none) and hold_days.

Public estimate for product pages

GET /api/v1/shipping/public/estimate?variant_id=…&quantity=1&province_code=79 needs no sign-in. It runs the same quote as checkout for a one-line cart to a province (fees, free-shipping threshold, eta with today’s cut-off) and answers estimate: true — the real fee is always computed again for the cart. The variant’s weight, size, selling unit and price come from the catalog module. Answers are cacheable for 60 seconds.

Automatic answers in support

When the support module is installed, shipping answers the question “where is my parcel?” (intent shipping.tracking, by tracking number or order number) with the real status of the shipment, in the buyer’s language. Only the owner gets an answer: the buyer account of the shipment, or a verified phone number equal to the recipient’s. When the shipment is not found, an order has several shipments, or the asker cannot be shown to be the owner, there is no automatic answer and staff reply.

MCP tools

shipping.quote (read only), shipping.list_shipments, shipping.get_shipment, shipping.book_shipment, shipping.cancel_shipment (destructive), shipping.update_status, shipping.list_cod_discrepancies — with the same permissions as the matching REST endpoints.

Configuration

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_FAKE_CARRIERfalseRegister the in-memory fake carrier (development only)
AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_CARRIER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS10Longest wait for one carrier call
AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_MAX_ADDRESSES_PER_BUYER20Addresses one buyer may keep
AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_WEBHOOK_MAX_BYTES262144Largest carrier webhook body
AUTOXIDE_SHIPPING_COD_SETTLEMENT_DAYS14Days before an unsettled COD amount is overdue

Carrier credentials, delivery calendars and holidays are data of each tenant, not environment variables.

Customer support (module support)

The support module takes support requests from customers — questions about an order, a product, an account or a payment — and lets the shop’s staff answer them until they are done. Each request is a ticket with messages back and forth. Tickets belong to an organization unit (a shop, a branch, a seller’s store on a marketplace), so chains and marketplaces split the work by branch like every other record.

Vietnamese: SUPPORT.vi.md.

What it does not do: consumer complaints with legal deadlines live in module compliance (a ticket is handed over there, never copied), disputes between buyers and sellers in marketplace, returns in orders. Live chat is a later module.

Permissions

PermissionAllows
support.tickets.readSeeing the tickets of the units in your scope, with messages and internal notes
support.tickets.replyAnswering, internal notes, opening tickets for customers, status, priority, assignee, links
support.tickets.manageHiding messages, handing tickets over as consumer complaints or to the platform
support.settings.manageSupport policy, teams, routing rules and saved replies of the units in your scope
support.auto_reply.manageApproving saved replies for automatic answers

Every permission works per organization unit: staff of a branch see the tickets of that branch and the branches below it; a marketplace seller with a grant at their store sees only that store’s tickets. With scope own, staff see the tickets assigned to them.

Customers need no permission: any signed-in account sees its own tickets at /api/v1/support/me/tickets.

Tickets

  • From the website — POST /api/v1/support/public/tickets. Signed in: the ticket belongs to the account. Guest: give email or phone and the anti-spam fields of the form (GET /api/v1/antispam/token?scope=support:tickets). The answer carries access_token once — the guest keeps it to see (GET /public/tickets/{id}?token=) and answer (POST /public/tickets/{id}/messages) this one ticket. A 6-digit code goes to the email or phone; the guest confirms it (POST /public/tickets/{id}/verify) before writing a second message.
  • By staff — POST /api/v1/support/tickets with the customer’s account, email or phone (a phone call, a visit).
  • From another module — through the trait SupportIntake (e.g. the order page); the same reference never makes two tickets.
  • After sign-up — POST /api/v1/support/me/claim attaches the verified guest tickets with the account’s verified phone number, or with the email / phone of a verified guest ticket whose token the customer sends.

Statuses: open → pending_agent (the customer wrote) ⇄ pending_customer (staff answered) → solved → closed. A customer writing on a solved ticket opens it again; closed is final (open a new ticket with follow_up_of). Only allowed steps are taken (support.invalid_transition).

Messages are never edited. A mistaken message is hidden with a reason (POST /tickets/{id}/messages/{message_id}/hide, support.tickets.manage); the customer sees that a message was hidden. Internal notes (internal: true) are for staff only and notify the colleagues listed in mentions. Signed-in customers attach media items they uploaded themselves (at most 5 per message).

Settings per unit

All settings are data of an organization unit and apply to the units below it unless they have their own.

  • Policy — PUT /api/v1/support/policies/{org_id}: ticket categories, minutes to the first answer and to solve per priority (low, normal, high, urgent, counted in business time), business hours and days off, UTC offset, days before a solved ticket closes, whether guests may open tickets, email replies, automatic answers. Defaults: Monday–Friday 08:00–17:00 (UTC+7), first answer within 8 business hours and solved within 3 business days for normal.
  • Teams — POST /api/v1/support/teams, members with PUT /teams/{id}/members/{user_id} (accepting new tickets; members switch it themselves). A member must be able to answer tickets of the unit.
  • Routing rules — POST /api/v1/support/routing-rules (category, channel → team). A new ticket goes to the team of the first matching rule (nearest unit first) and round-robin to the member waiting longest who still has support.tickets.reply at the ticket’s unit.
  • Saved replies — POST /api/v1/support/macros with text per language and the variables {customer_name}, {ticket_number}, {subject}; fill one in for a ticket with POST /tickets/{id}/macros/{macro_id}/render.

Deadlines and work

The first-answer and solve deadlines are computed when a ticket opens and when its priority changes. While the ticket waits for the customer, the clock stops; when the customer writes, the solve deadline moves by the business time waited. The job support.sla_check (every minute) marks late tickets once (breached, event support.ticket_breached); support.auto_close closes solved tickets after the policy’s days. Tickets waiting for staff show in the work inbox (GET /api/v1/kernel/work, source support.tickets). GET /api/v1/support/reports/summary?from=&to= counts tickets, solved and late ones, median times and the average rating.

Links, hand-over, ratings

  • POST /tickets/{id}/links {"target": "orders.order:<id>"} links a record of any module (it must exist); the order page lists related tickets with GET /tickets?link=orders.order:<id>.
  • POST /tickets/{id}/escalate {"to": "consumer_complaint"} hands the ticket to compliance as a consumer complaint with legal deadlines: the ticket keeps case_id and closes as escalated; calling again never opens a second case. Customers who want to complain send it directly to POST /api/v1/compliance/public/complaints. {"to": "platform"} hands a seller’s ticket to the marketplace’s staff.
  • Once solved, customers rate the support from 1 to 5 (POST /me/tickets/{id}/satisfaction, or the public endpoint with the token).

AI and email

  • POST /tickets/{id}/reply-suggestions drafts an answer with module ai from the ticket’s messages (emails and phone numbers removed) and the unit’s saved replies. It is only a draft: staff edit it and send it with ai_assisted: true, and the customer sees the label.
  • Email replies (off by default; turn on inbound_email in the policy): an inbound mail module gives replies to support+<key>@your-domain to the trait InboundMail; the key of a ticket comes from InboundMail::reply_address_key. Mail from anyone but the customer, to an unknown key or a closed ticket is dropped; mail never opens a new ticket. Quoted earlier mail is cut.

Automatic answers (off by default)

Turn on auto_reply in a unit’s policy. When a customer writes, the AI only classifies the question; rules in the server decide, and only two kinds of text ever reach the customer:

  1. An approved saved reply, word for word with its variables filled in. Approve one with PUT /api/v1/support/macros/{id}/auto-reply {"enabled": true, "questions": {...}, "review_due_on": "YYYY-MM-DD"} (support.auto_reply.manage); after the review day it is no longer used, and editing its text withdraws the approval.
  2. A sentence built from exact data by a module that attached a FactSource (e.g. the status of the customer’s own order); it answers nothing when it is not sure the customer owns the data.

An answer is sent only when the classification is confident enough (auto_reply_min_confidence_bp, default 9000), carries no risk flag, the question has no blocked word (built-in: complaints, refunds, returns, cancellations, payment problems, personal data, legal words, asking for a person — plus the unit’s auto_reply_blocked_terms), and fewer than auto_reply_max_per_thread (default 2) automatic answers came in a row. Otherwise staff answer as usual, with an AI draft prepared. Automatic messages have auto_reply: true: label them “Automatic answer” and show a “Talk to a person” button (POST /me/tickets/{id}/handoff, or the public one with the token), which stops automatic answers on that ticket. Customers rate an answer (…/auto-replies/{reply_id}/feedback); a saved reply reported wrong AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_AUTO_REPLY_FLAG_LIMIT (3) times in 7 days stops being used. Try a question with POST /api/v1/support/auto-reply/preview (nothing is sent) and read the log at GET /api/v1/support/auto-replies.

For AI agents (MCP)

Tools, with the same permissions as REST: support.list_tickets, support.get_ticket, support.reply_ticket, support.add_internal_note, support.update_ticket, support.link_ticket, support.suggest_reply (a draft only), support.preview_auto_reply.

Settings

VariableDefaultMeaning
AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_GUEST_PER_HOUR5Guest tickets per hour per network address, email, phone
AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_MAX_BODY_CHARS10000Longest message
AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_TOKEN_DAYS_AFTER_CLOSE30Days a guest’s ticket token works after the ticket closes
AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_GUEST_URL—Page showing a ticket to a guest ({id}, {token})
AUTOXIDE_SUPPORT_AUTO_REPLY_FLAG_LIMIT3Wrong reports in 7 days that retire an automatic answer

Personal data

Deleting an account anonymizes its tickets (name, contact and the customer’s text are removed) and keeps them for statistics. The customer’s tickets and messages are part of the personal data export. Legal basis to check with a qualified person: Law 91/2025/QH15 on personal data protection, Law 19/2023/QH15 on consumer protection, Law 134/2025/QH15 on artificial intelligence (labelling AI-written answers).

Taxes

Tiếng Việt

The tax module computes taxes from data: tax categories and rates with their effective dates, withholding rates for platforms, and rules (such as when cash register invoices are required) come in a tax data pack, not in the code. The server ships with a pack for Vietnam. Other modules (sales, invoices, the ledger) compute taxes through autoxide_tax::api::TaxEngine.

Every rate in the shipped pack carries its legal basis and the note “needs checking against the original document”. Check them with someone qualified before using them in production.

The Vietnam pack

CategoryRateNotes
vat.standard10%Law on VAT 48/2024/QH15
vat.standard_reducible8% until 2026-12-31, then 10%the 2% reduction; goods excluded from it use vat.standard
vat.reduced_55%
vat.zero0%exports
vat.exemptnot subjectshown as “not subject to VAT”, not as 0%
excise.beer65% special consumption tax, then 10% VAT on the price including itsample

Withholding by marketplaces with payment (Decree 117/2025/ND-CP) for household businesses: goods 1% VAT

  • 0.5% PIT, services 5% + 2%, production and transport 3% + 1.5%. Businesses declare themselves: nothing is withheld. What core does today: computes the amount (POST /api/v1/tax/withholding) and books it when a settlement asks for it (ledger, entry TaxWithheld). What it does not do yet (with the marketplace module, after 1.0): withhold by itself on every payout to a household seller, issue the withholding certificate (withholding_certificate exists as a document kind, nothing creates it), and prepare the data of the declaration on the seller’s behalf — a marketplace does these itself until then.

The pack is imported by itself within an hour after the server starts (and whenever an update ships a newer one). To import it at once, or another pack:

autoxide task tax.import_pack
autoxide task tax.import_pack path=/path/to/pack.json

or POST /api/v1/tax/packs (platform staff with tax.packs_manage). Only a higher version than the imported one is accepted; the same pack again changes nothing. autoxide doctor warns when a rate ends within AUTOXIDE_TAX_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS (60) days with no rate after it — for example if the 8% rate is extended past 2026, import a pack that says so.

Compute taxes

curl -X POST https://api.example.com/api/v1/tax/quote \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jurisdiction": "VN", "tax_point": "2026-11-17", "price_mode": "inclusive", "currency": "VND",
       "lines": [{"line_id": "1", "category": "vat.standard_reducible", "amount": {"amount": "108000", "currency": "VND"}}]}'
  • price_mode: exclusive (amounts before taxes) or inclusive (taxes are split out).
  • Taxes are rounded once per rate on the whole document, then shared between the lines: the lines always add up to the totals. A later stage (VAT) is computed on the price plus earlier stages (special consumption tax).
  • tax_point is a calendar day, not an instant. Orders and invoices compute it with TaxEngine::tax_date: the day in the time zone of the seller’s tax jurisdiction (pack rule tax_date.time_zone; Vietnam: Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh), else in the unit’s organizations.timezone, else in UTC. So an order placed at 00:30 on 1 January 2027 Vietnam time (17:30 UTC on 31 December) is taxed at the rate of 1 January. No rate on that day: 422 tax.rate_missing — the engine never guesses.
  • The order’s tax is an estimate; the invoice decides. The law ties the VAT tax point to the transfer of ownership of goods (delivery) or the completion of a service. An order taxes at the day it is placed; its invoice taxes at its own issue date (orders.invoice_timing, on_delivered by default). When a rate changes in between, the invoice uses the new rate and the order’s documents (GET …/orders/me/orders/{id}/documents) show differs_from_order: true — settle the difference with the buyer. The flag compares the tax of each line and the total, ignoring one minor unit per line of rounding (two for a line partly cancelled, which the invoice rounds again): an order priced without tax carries its tax-inclusive shipping fee on the invoice at the pre-tax amount, so the invoice total can differ from the order by one minor unit. An order mixing tax-inclusive and tax-exclusive prices is always flagged — one invoice has a single price mode and cannot carry it exactly. When the flag is true, correct the invoice with an adjustment (POST /api/v1/invoices/documents/{id}/adjust) or a replacement (POST /api/v1/invoices/documents/{id}/replace). A draft invoice is re-taxed at issue when it was computed on another day. Adjustments and replacements keep the tax date (rate) of the invoice they correct. Ledger entries of orders and invoices are dated with the same tax date. autoxide doctor warns when an imported tax jurisdiction declares no tax_date.time_zone.
  • The answer has a snapshot (rates and their ids, pack version, rounding): keep it with the document.

POST /api/v1/tax/withholding computes what a platform withholds from a payment to a seller. MCP tools: tax.quote, tax.rates.

Tax profiles

Each organization unit can have a tax profile — tax code (10 or 13 digits, 0101234567-001 for a branch, or a 12-digit personal id), regime, business lines, estimated yearly revenue, legal name and address: PUT /api/v1/tax/profiles/{org_id} (tax.profiles_manage on the unit). A unit without its own profile uses the nearest one above it. The regime decides the invoice: vat_credit → VAT invoice; vat_direct, household → sales invoice without VAT per line; exempt → no tax. A household business with revenue from 1 billion VND a year must issue cash register invoices (TaxEngine::invoice_requirements, Decree 70/2025/ND-CP — check the latest schedule).

Read the data

GET /api/v1/tax/jurisdictions, /categories, /rates?on=YYYY-MM-DD, /withholding-rates, /rules, /packs (tax.read).

Threat model of the core

Tiếng Việt: THREAT_MODEL.vi.md

What this is: the maintainers’ model of what an attacker could aim at in an Autoxide server, which controls exist today and what is still open. It was written with AI assistance from the code and the decision log, as input for a round of penetration testing by people outside the project. It is not an audit and does not claim that Autoxide is free of vulnerabilities. To report a problem, follow SECURITY.md.

  • Date: 2026-11-26, main of the 0.x series before 1.0
  • Roadmap item: step 71, G13 (docs/ROADMAP.md)
  • Builds on: the November 2026 review (code review and black-box test) and the November 2026 security and performance test (29,566 cases on both databases)
  • Method: STRIDE per trust boundary — Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege

How to read this document

Each of the eight boundaries below has the same parts:

  • Assets — what an attacker wants at that boundary.
  • Entry points — where data crosses it.
  • Trust assumptions — what the design takes for granted. A test that breaks an assumption is a finding.
  • STRIDE table — threat → existing control → residual risk or open item. A control names where it lives: a code path (relative to the repository root), a decision ID (D-… in docs/DECISIONS.md or docs/decisions/D-….md) or a gate rule of cargo xtask check. A control marked (to verify) is described by the design or the documentation but was not traced end to end in the code for this document; the list is at the end, in Controls to verify.

Findings of the earlier rounds keep their IDs: H-, M-, L-, I-, P- (review) and PT- (test).

System overview

               browsers, apps, AI agents, partner servers, payment / carrier / bank callbacks
                                         │  HTTPS (TLS ends at a reverse proxy)
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────▼───────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ (1) HTTP layer: request id → security headers → log → limits → CORS → tenant → auth  │
  │     REST /api/v1/…  ·  OpenAPI  ·  SSE / WebSocket  ·  public routes  ·  webhooks in │
  │ (2) MCP endpoint /mcp, /mcp/<module>                                                 │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ (3) kernel: Principal and permissions, tenancy, throttle, idempotency, outbox, jobs, │
  │     config and secrets, seal, outbound address filter, storage and AI traits         │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ (4) modules (one crate each, own tables, talk through traits and events)             │
  ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
  │ (5) databases: control database + placements (SQLite or PostgreSQL), file storage    │
  └───────────────┬───────────────────────────────────────────────────┬──────────────────┘
                  │ (6) placement: tenants on shared or own databases │
                  ▼                                                   ▼
  (7) external providers: payments, bank feed, carrier, SMS,   (8) AI providers chosen by the
      e-invoice, mail, outbound webhooks, web push                 installer (TextModel / Embedder)

Modes. AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_MODE=single serves one default tenant and ignores Host and the tenant header. multi serves many tenants from one process; this is the mode with the most boundaries and the one to test.

Actors

ActorCredentialWhat they are trusted with

Global assumptions

  • TLS is terminated by a reverse proxy or load balancer in front of the server; the server itself speaks HTTP (docs/DEPLOY.md). AUTOXIDE_HTTP_CLIENT_IP_HEADER / AUTOXIDE_HTTP_TRUSTED_PROXIES are set only when such a proxy exists (crates/kernel/src/config/http.rs).
  • AUTOXIDE_SECRET_KEY and AUTOXIDE_AUTH_TOKEN_SECRET are set to random values in production; the example values of .env.example are refused at startup (H-3; crates/kernel/src/security/secret.rs, modules/auth/src/config.rs).
  • The database and the file store are reachable only by the server and the operator.
  • The code is memory-safe Rust: unsafe_code = "forbid" for every workspace crate (Cargo.toml); release builds keep overflow checks (an overflow is a 500, not a wrap — PT-5).

1. Client ↔ HTTP layer

Assets: availability of the API; the mapping request → tenant; credentials in transit; tenant data in responses; browser sessions of tenants’ websites.

Entry points: every REST route under /api/v1/ (docs/openapi.json, about 1,300 operations); public routes (security((), ("bearer" = []))); /api/v1/openapi.json, /api/docs (opt-in), /llms.txt; /health/*; /metrics (opt-in); GET /api/v1/kernel/events/stream (SSE) and /events/ws (WebSocket); inbound provider webhooks (boundary 7); headers Host, Origin, Autoxide-Tenant, Authorization, Idempotency-Key, If-Match, the client-address header.

Trust assumptions:

  • The tenant of an authenticated request comes from the credential, never from Host or a header alone (crates/kernel/src/data/tenancy/request.rs).
  • A Host maps to a tenant only when that tenant has verified the domain by DNS TXT (crates/kernel/src/data/tenancy/domains.rs).
  • Public routes only return data the tenant has published; choosing another tenant for a public request (by host, header or ?site=) is allowed and exposes only that tenant’s public data.

2. API and MCP endpoint

Assets: the same data and actions as REST; the permission model; the parity promise “an MCP tool never does more than REST with the same permission” (CLAUDE.md rule 8).

Entry points: POST /mcp and /mcp/<module> (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC): tools/list, tools/call, resources/list|read, prompts/list|get, server/discover (crates/kernel/src/http/mcp.rs, http/mcp/protocol.rs, http/mcp/transport.rs; D-068, D-20261121-mcp-server). The manifest is docs/mcp-tools.json (about 310 tools).

Trust assumptions:

  • MCP is authenticated exactly like REST (Authorization: Bearer access token or API key), in a layer before the protocol code.
  • A tool handler is a thin adapter: it calls the same service function as the REST handler, and passes the Principal whenever REST limits that permission by scope.

3. Kernel

The kernel (crates/kernel) holds what every module relies on. The authentication module auth is a module, but its guarantees are kernel-level for this model, so it is covered here.

Assets: signing keys and sealed secrets; accounts, passwords, second factors, sessions, API keys; the permission catalog and role assignments; the organization tree; idempotency records; the outbox and the job queue; configuration.

Entry points: /api/v1/auth/* (sign-in, refresh, logout, MFA, passkeys, sign-in links, reset, invitations, OIDC, SCIM, API keys, roles, delegations, support grants); /api/v1/kernel/* (settings, tenants, domains, jobs, records, tags…); background jobs and the event dispatcher; process configuration.

Trust assumptions:

  • A business module checks permissions only through Principal (security/access/mod.rs) and never depends on auth (D-046).
  • Jobs and event handlers receive their tenant from the stored row, not from a request.
  • Configuration comes from the environment through ConfigReader; per-tenant settings go through the tenancy settings API.

4. Modules

Assets: each module’s tables and invariants (stock, money, publication state); the contracts between modules (traits in api, events); the public Rust API used by modules outside the repository.

Entry points: a module’s routes, tools, event subscriptions, jobs; context.require::<dyn Trait>(); Autoxide::new().module(…) for external modules (crates/app/src/lib.rs).

Trust assumptions:

  • Modules in this repository follow the boundary rules, enforced by cargo xtask check (D-031): a module exposes only pub mod api and pub fn module(…), does not import another module’s internals (module-import), does not query the database in handlers (handler-database), does not read the environment (env-access).
  • A module owns its tables (<module>_…), with no foreign key across modules and no join into another module’s tables (rules 1 and 4).
  • External modules are trusted code. They are compiled into the same process, with the same database connections and keys (D-20261121-external-modules). The repository’s gate rules do not run on code outside the repository.
STRIDEThreatExisting controlResidual / open

EExperimental modules weaken the coreOff by default; an official module never depends on an experimental one (docs/MODULES.md)Experimental modules got the same automated tests but less review

5. Database

Assets: all data at rest; schema integrity; backups; the migration history; the audit chain.

Entry points: the server’s connections (read pool and write connection per database); autoxide migrate, autoxide backup, autoxide restore, autoxide copy (CLI on the server); scheduled backups to the file store; the tenant export job.

Trust assumptions:

  • Every feature runs on SQLite and PostgreSQL (CLAUDE.md “Luật số một”); a check that only holds on one database is a finding.
  • Every tenant-level table has tenant_id, and every query on it filters through .scoped(&tenant) (data/tenancy/scope.rs, D-253) — also when the tenant has its own database.
  • Only the operator can reach database files, credentials and backups.

6. Placement

Assets: which database and file store hold each tenant; placement connection URLs; domain → tenant mapping; data residency promises; tenants during a move, split or merge.

Entry points: autoxide tenant move and the platform-only REST / MCP endpoints for placements, moves and relocations (data/tenancy/placements.rs, moves*, relocate*; permissions kernel.placements.read, kernel.tenants.move, kernel.tenants.relocate); domain endpoints of each tenant (data/tenancy/domains*); sandboxes (data/tenancy/sandbox*).

Trust assumptions:

  • Only accounts of the platform tenant can move, split, merge or erase tenants (require_platform); a staff member who entered a tenant through support access cannot.
  • A tenant on its own database is still filtered by tenant_id (defence in depth).

7. External providers

Assets: money flows (payments, refunds, bank credits — the core never holds buyers’ money, D-187); shipment state; tax invoices; per-tenant provider credentials; outbound webhook secrets; the server’s network position (SSRF).

Entry points:

  • Inbound: /api/v1/ledger/webhooks/{provider}/{hook}, /api/v1/ledger/bank-feeds/{provider}/{hook}, /api/v1/shipping/webhooks/{carrier_code}/{hook}/{token} (and older forms); MoMo IPN, SePay bank feed, GHN status callbacks (modules/momo, modules/sepay, modules/ghn).
  • Outbound: payment, carrier, SMS (modules/esms), e-invoice (modules/einvoice_sepay) and mail calls; outbound webhooks (modules/webhooks, Standard Webhooks signatures, D-081); OIDC discovery; tenant SMTP; web push (WebPushSender contract).
  • Addresses chosen by users: webhook targets, OIDC issuers, SMTP hosts, push subscription endpoints, payment return_url, KYC return_url.

Trust assumptions:

  • Every provider account belongs to a tenant and is configured by that tenant; the server never falls back to another tenant’s account (crates/kernel/src/contracts/provider.rs, D-20261121-provider-accounts).
  • Provider connectors in this repository are experimental: written from public documentation, not yet run against the live services (header of each connector’s lib.rs).

RDisputes about what a provider saidProvider calls logged without secrets, with metrics (contracts/provider.rs send); ledger entries append-only—
IProvider secrets leakSecret settings sealed per tenant and row, write-only through the settings API (contracts/provider.rs, D-257)—
IOpen redirect after payment or identity checkPayment return_url must be https:// on a verified domain of the tenant or a listed origin (P-5, ledger.return_url_not_allowed)KYC return_url has no allow-list yet (L-11, P16); no identity provider connector ships today
ISSRF: the server calls internal addressesShared filter crates/kernel/src/security/net.rs (D-149, D-20261121-ssrf-targets): non-public IPs refused at save; names resolved through PublicOnly at connect time (DNS rebinding), redirects off, system proxy ignored (L-4); non-HTTP protocols resolve once and connect to that IP65 SSRF cases per database: nothing reached the local listener
IWeb push to internal addressesPush subscriptions accept public hosts only; the WebPushSender contract requires public-IP connections (PT-10, contracts/push.rs)No real web push sender ships in this repository
DOutbound calls hang or return huge bodieshttp_client with timeout and no redirects; response bodies capped by AUTOXIDE_PROVIDER_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES (I-2); webhook bodies capped per route (ledger webhook_max_bytes)—
DSMS cost abuse (each SMS paid by the shop)Per-number, per-client-block and per-hour limits (P-2, PT-4)—
EProvider calls inside a write transaction lock the databaseRule: no network call inside a write transaction (CLAUDE.md “Luật dữ liệu”, contracts/provider.rs)Enforced by review, not by a gate
EOutbound webhooks leak events the receiver’s owner may not seeCreating a webhook requires the event’s stream permission; payloads signed (modules/webhooks)—

8. AI

Assets: tenant content sent to a model; the operator’s model budget; integrity of what gets published; the instructions given to the model.

Entry points: features that call TextModel or Embedder (crates/kernel/src/contracts/ai.rs, published by modules/ai): SEO and alt-text suggestions, translations, product description drafts (catalog), support reply drafts (support/src/ai.rs), review summaries (orders/src/reviews.rs), conversation drafts, search by meaning. AI agents as API clients are covered by boundaries 1–3.

Trust assumptions:

  • AI is off until the installer configures a provider (docs/AI.md).
  • Model output is untrusted data: it must match a JSON Schema and only becomes a suggestion or draft; a person (or an agent with the publish permission) decides (D-109).
  • Rules for the model are in instructions; user data is only in input (Prompt::new(…).input(…)).
STRIDEThreatExisting controlResidual / open
SContent an attacker controls (a review, a ticket, a product text) tells the model to do something else (prompt injection)Instructions and input separated; output must match a JSON Schema (ai.output_invalid); the model has no tools and no credentials; results are drafts only (D-109)Injection can still bias a draft; the human reviewer is the control. AI-generated entries carry ai_generated and publication records ai_reviewed (docs/AI.md)
TA draft overwrites a human editTranslation saves only if nobody changed the target since the request (content.translation_conflict)—
TModel output carries unsafe markup or linksTranslation keeps links, images and ids from the original; numbered tags must round-trip exactlySanitising of every AI draft before it is shown by a client (to verify per feature)
RWho published AI-generated textai_reviewed with person and time on publication; audit chain—
ISending personal or private data to a providerDocumented list of what is sent; private images only with AUTOXIDE_MEDIA_AI_SEND_PRIVATE=true; support history sent without email and phone; prompts, content and keys never logged (docs/AI.md, modules/support/src/ai.rs)The provider is chosen by the installer; data processing agreements are theirs
DBudget exhaustionDaily token limit per tenant, from its plan (ai.daily_tokens) or AUTOXIDE_AI_DAILY_TOKEN_LIMIT, counted in the database across servers (modules/ai/src/config.rs, ai_usage); jobs cut off and retried; per-key rate limits—
EAn AI agent publishes or deletes beyond its role_own permissions limit an agent key to entries created with the same key; no archive / delete without the permission (content.write_own, content.publish_own)—

Out of scope

  • The operator: anyone with a shell, the environment, the database or the backups. Misconfigurations that SECURITY.md lists (CORS *, public /metrics, rate limits at 0, client-address header without a proxy, unset secrets).
  • Volumetric denial of service; cheap single-request amplification is in scope.
  • Administrators doing what administrators may do inside their own tenant.
  • User interfaces and SDK consumers (separate repositories), the reverse proxy, TLS configuration, the operating system, the container runtime, DNS of tenants’ domains.
  • Real provider accounts (payments, bank, SMS, carrier, e-invoice, identity) and AI providers; their own security.
  • Supply chain beyond what cargo deny, gitleaks, pinned actions and signed releases cover (docs/VERIFYING.md).
  • Legal compliance as such (see docs/COMPLIANCE.md); this model covers its technical controls only.

Known open items

Status lives in docs/ROADMAP.md, step 70, items P16 (follow-ups of the November 2026 review) and P17 (fixes from the November 2026 test), and in the status table of docs/security/pentest-2026-11/README.md. At the time of writing, the open classes are:

ClassBoundaryWhere tracked
Open redirect class: identity verification return_url without an allow-list7P16 (L-11)
Grant-rule inconsistencies (permission name vs. scope; status codes; narrowing a role someone else holds; SCIM pending members, creator of a SCIM link)3P16
Automation rules: owner’s scope not captured; revocation event in dead letter does not pause a rule3P16
Events of unit-level data without org_id in some modules4P16
Cache eviction under random Host floods; WebSocket Origin; deterministic test of the domain-claim race and of a hung domain snapshot read1, 6P16
Expensive public search (full-text index behind a trait)1P17 (PT-15)
Information exposure of low value: unused taxonomy terms, analytics pollution, newsletter confirmation cap1P17 (PT-11, PT-12, PT-18)
Very large prices or weights saturating instead of being refused; currency checks in some purchase / POS paths4, 7P17
Records pointing at unknown organization units created before PT-83P17
SMS sign-in shared cap can lock a number for a while3P17 (PT-7 follow-up)
address-key gate catches only one textual pattern1P17
Tamper-resistant audit log (keyed or anchored chain); field-level encryption of sensitive personal data with managed and rotated keys3, 5G13 (this step)

Only classes are named here. Details of an open issue are shared privately, through the channel in SECURITY.md.

How to use this for the external test

Set-up. Use AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_MODE=multi, at least two tenants plus the platform tenant, an organization tree with unit-scoped staff, and both databases. The scripts of the November 2026 round (docs/security/pentest-2026-11/scripts/) build such a set-up and a case matrix; reuse them as a baseline rather than repeating the generated groups. Point every provider at a local fake or a sandbox account you own; test only your own installation.

Suggested focus, most value first:

  1. What the earlier rounds did not cover: passkeys and OIDC end to end in a browser; payment, bank-feed and carrier callbacks with real provider signatures (sandbox accounts); tenant move, split and merge between databases under load; tenants on their own database; file and media uploads at their size limits; WebSocket beyond the per-user cap; ai with a real model.
  2. Grant and scope logic (boundary 3): roles, memberships, delegations, support grants, SCIM, API key scope ∩ owner, automations’ run_as, step-up — look for any path where a principal ends up with more than its creator or holder. The P16 list names the areas known to be inconsistent.
  3. Tenant and branch isolation where the gate is blind (boundary 5): code paths the tenant-scope and mcp-principal rules do not see (generic queries, helpers, named handler functions) — compare MCP tools with their REST endpoints one by one.
  4. Host-based tenant resolution and CORS (boundary 1): verified domains, ?site=, domain changes between tenants, cache TTLs across several servers, suspended tenants.
  5. Money paths (boundaries 4, 7): currency and amount checks across every payment, refund, POS, stored-value and promotion path; races on both databases.
  6. AI drafts (boundary 8): whether injected content in reviews, tickets or product text can produce a draft that a client would render unsafely or that misleads a reviewer.
  7. Each control marked (to verify) below.

Reporting. Use the severity scale of the November 2026 review and the private channel in SECURITY.md. Name the boundary and STRIDE category from this document.

Controls to verify

Controls described by the design or documentation but not traced end to end in the code for this document:

  1. Every throttle and idempotency table has an expiry and a cleanup job (boundary 3).
  2. Every module that holds personal data registers it for export and deletion; nothing enforces it for new modules (boundary 4).
  3. A sandbox copies configuration only, for every module (boundary 6).
  4. Inbound provider callbacks: the replay / deduplication mechanism of each connector (boundary 7).
  5. AI drafts: output sanitising for every feature that stores model text (boundary 8).

Keeping this document current

Update this file in the same pull request as a change that adds a boundary, an entry point class (a new kind of credential, a new inbound callback, a new outbound protocol) or a control listed here, and keep the Vietnamese version in step.

Verifying a release

English · Tiếng Việt

Every Autoxide release is built and signed by the Release workflow of this repository on GitHub Actions. There is no long-lived signing key: Sigstore issues a short-lived certificate tied to the identity of the workflow run (GitHub’s OIDC token), and the signature is recorded in the public transparency log Rekor. Checking a signature tells you that the file or image was built by this repository’s release workflow from a release tag, and has not changed since. It does not tell you the code is free of bugs.

Replace X.Y.Z below with the version you install (for example 1.0.0 or 1.0.0-rc.1).

What is signed

Release itemBuild provenance (SLSA)cosign signature
Docker image ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:X.Y.Zyes, plus an SBOM attestationyes, on the image
Linux binaries autoxide-X.Y.Z-<target>.tar.gzyes, for each filethrough SHA256SUMS
TypeScript SDK autoxide-sdk-X.Y.Z.tgzyesthrough SHA256SUMS
SBOM of the image sbom.spdx.jsonyesthrough SHA256SUMS
SBOM of the Rust crates autoxide.cdx.json (CycloneDX)yesthrough SHA256SUMS
License texts of third-party crates THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.htmlyesthrough SHA256SUMS
SHA256SUMS (checksums of the files above)—SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json (Sigstore bundle)

Linux binaries, SHA256SUMS and the cosign signatures are attached to releases after 0.18.0. Older releases have the image attestations only.

You need either the GitHub CLI (gh 2.49 or newer) or cosign (3.0 or newer). Either one is enough.

The Docker image

With the GitHub CLI:

gh attestation verify oci://ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:X.Y.Z --repo thuongtamduy/autoxide

With cosign:

cosign verify ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:X.Y.Z \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/thuongtamduy/autoxide/\.github/workflows/release(-image)?\.yml@refs/(tags/v.+|heads/main)$'

The identity allows two workflows: release.yml, which publishes a release, and release-image.yml, which the maintainers run from main to publish the image of an existing release tag again.

A tag such as X.Y.Z can in principle be moved; a digest cannot. After the check, deploy by digest:

docker buildx imagetools inspect ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide:X.Y.Z --format '{{json .Manifest}}' | jq -r .digest
# then use ghcr.io/thuongtamduy/autoxide@sha256:… in compose.yml or your manifests

Release files

Download the files you want from the release page, together with SHA256SUMS and SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json, into one folder.

With the GitHub CLI, check each file directly:

gh attestation verify autoxide-X.Y.Z-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz --repo thuongtamduy/autoxide

With cosign, check the signature of the checksum list, then the files against it:

cosign verify-blob SHA256SUMS \
  --bundle SHA256SUMS.sigstore.json \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github\.com/thuongtamduy/autoxide/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v.+$'
sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS

Both commands must succeed. sha256sum prints OK for each file you downloaded.

The Linux binaries

autoxide-X.Y.Z-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (64-bit Intel and AMD) and autoxide-X.Y.Z-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz (64-bit ARM) hold the same autoxide program as the Docker image, copied out of it, plus the licence files. It is built on Debian 13, so it needs a Linux system with a C library (glibc) at least as new as Debian 13’s. If ./autoxide --version fails with GLIBC_2.… not found, use the Docker image instead.

Release candidates

Versions such as 1.0.0-rc.1 are release candidates: test versions published before a major release. They are signed and checked exactly like final releases. GitHub marks them as pre-releases, and their image has only the tag X.Y.Z-rc.N: never latest and never X.Y, so you only get one if you ask for it by name. Do not run them in production.

If a check fails

Do not run the file or image. Download it again from the release page; if the check still fails, report it privately as described in SECURITY.md.

Guides

Task-by-task guides to the Autoxide API. Each has curl examples, which run as tests against every build, and TypeScript examples with the SDK in sdk/typescript.

Vietnamese: README.vi.md.

The curl examples send JSON with --json '…', which needs curl 7.82 or newer (curl --version). With an older curl, replace --json '…' with -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json' -d '…'.

  • Showing posts and pictures on a website: public endpoints, srcset and WebP, ETag and 304

  • Signing in and staying signed in: access and refresh tokens, signing out
  • Signing in with Google, Microsoft, GitHub or OpenID Connect: providers per tenant, linking accounts safely
  • Syncing staff from your identity provider (SCIM 2.0): Entra ID, Okta and Google Workspace create, change and disable staff accounts
  • API keys for programs and AI agents: least permissions, rate limit, revoking
  • Retrying safely: Idempotency-Key
  • Reading long lists: limit, cursor, order
  • Upgrading clients: every list is a page: data + pagination, count, default orders, MCP tools
  • Reading errors: code, errors, Retry-After
  • Connecting an AI agent over MCP: a key for the agent, client setup, the tools
  • Connecting MCP clients with OAuth sign-in: Claude, ChatGPT and other clients without a key, the consent page, revoking
  • Receiving events in real time: Server-Sent Events, Last-Event-ID, limits
  • Uploading large files straight to storage: signed links to S3, completing, checks
  • Trying changes in a sandbox: a test copy of your tenant, simulated partners, bringing drafts back
