        assert_eq!(data["g1"]["products"][0]["price_minor"], 120_000);
    })
    .await
    .unwrap();
}
}

Also check that a block of a record that is not public answers null, and that the data of every block of a page is read in one query. Run the test on SQLite and PostgreSQL, like every test.

Checklist

  • Name <module>.<block>, label and AI hint in English, translated in locales/vi.json.
  • Closed props schema; media as x-media, links as x-link, colors as theme tokens.
  • Prices, stock and sale dates come from with_data(), never from text.
  • BlockData reads every block of a type in one query and returns only public data of the website.
  • Tests on both databases.

Reading long lists

Vietnamese: pagination.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com), and the TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

Every list answers one page: {"data": [...], "pagination": {"limit", "next_cursor"}}. Ask for the next page with cursor set to next_cursor; null means there is no more. limit is 1 to 200 (50 by default); order is desc (newest first, the default) or asc. The cursor stays valid while you read, even when records are added.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token
# save: REFRESH=.data.refresh_token

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --json '{"kind":"post","title":"One"}'
# expect: 201

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Two"}'
# expect: 201

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Three"}'
# expect: 201

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries?limit=2&order=asc" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# save: CURSOR=.pagination.next_cursor

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries?limit=2&order=asc&cursor=$CURSOR" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Keep the other parameters (limit, order, filters) the same from page to page; a cursor from another list answers 422.

With the SDK

paginate() follows the cursors for you:

import { createClient } from "@autoxide/sdk";

const api = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com", token: "axk1_…" /* read it from your secret store */ });

let count = 0;
for await (const entry of api.paginate("/api/v1/content/entries", { query: { limit: 100, order: "asc" } })) {
  count += 1;
  console.log(entry.id, entry.title);
}
console.log(`${count} entries`);

Writing a provider adapter

An adapter connects Autoxide to one outside service: a payment gateway, a bank feed, a carrier, an SMS provider, an e-invoice provider. This guide is for developers who add one. Every adapter is built the same way, so that a tenant sets up any of them with the same API.

Vietnamese: provider-adapters.vi.md.

The rules

  1. One small module crate per adapter, modules/<name>, that depends only on the kernel (and on the module that publishes the contract, when the contract is not in the kernel, e.g. autoxide_shipping::api). It implements a contract (PaymentGateway, BankFeed, SmsSender, EInvoiceProvider, ShippingCarrier…) and is registered before the module that uses it.
  2. The account at the provider belongs to the tenant. API keys, shop ids and webhook secrets are tenant settings in the connection group, never environment variables. Two tenants on one server use two different accounts. A tenant that has not set its account gets the error provider.not_configured; an adapter never falls back to another account.
  3. Secrets are write-only. A secret setting is stored encrypted, is never returned by the API, and never appears in logs, events or errors. People set secrets over REST; the MCP tool kernel.set_setting refuses secret settings, so a secret never passes through an agent.
  4. Written from the provider’s public documentation. Do not write from memory. Put the URL of each page you used, and the date you read it, in the comment at the top of the module. Until the adapter has run against the real service, the crate description and its documentation say so: “written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service”. Adapters are experimental until then.
  5. No network call inside a write transaction, and every outbound call has a timeout.
  6. Works on SQLite and PostgreSQL, like everything else. Most adapters have no table at all.

1. Declare the account

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_kernel::tenancy::{CONNECTION_GROUP, TenantSetting};

// One setting per field of the tenant's account: `<module>.connection.<kind>.<field>`.
pub(crate) const API_KEY: TenantSetting = TenantSetting::new(
    "acme.connection.api.key",
    "API key of this tenant's Acme account (Acme dashboard > Developers).",
)
.secret()
.group(CONNECTION_GROUP);

pub(crate) const SHOP_ID: TenantSetting = TenantSetting::new(
    "acme.connection.api.shop_id",
    "Shop id of this tenant's Acme account.",
)
.group(CONNECTION_GROUP);
}

Return them from Module::tenant_settings. The tenant then manages them with the API that already exists:

WhatRESTMCP tool
See what a connection needs and what is setGET /api/v1/kernel/settings?group=connectionkernel.list_settings
Set a fieldPUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}kernel.set_setting (not for secrets)
Remove a fieldDELETE /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}kernel.delete_setting
Test the connectionPOST /api/v1/kernel/settings/{name}/testkernel.test_connection
See the webhook addressesGET /api/v1/kernel/connections/webhookskernel.list_connection_webhooks

All of them need the permission kernel.settings.manage, which is marked as sensitive. Setting or removing a connection setting also needs a recent sign-in (step_up_required otherwise), because it changes where money or data goes; every change is in the audit log, by name only.

A setting that holds an address chosen by the tenant must be checked when it is stored (.checked(…) with autoxide_kernel::net::check_target_url) and the client must use Target::TenantChosen, so the server only connects to public addresses.

2. Read the account when called

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_kernel::provider::ProviderAccounts;

// In `Module::start`:
let accounts = context.require::<ProviderAccounts>()?;

// In every trait method (the traits pass `TenantId`):
let tenant = self.accounts.tenant(tenant_id).await?;
let key = self.accounts.require(&tenant, &API_KEY).await?; // `provider.not_configured` when unset
let shop = self.accounts.get(&tenant, &SHOP_ID).await?; // optional field
}

3. Call the provider

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_kernel::provider::{Target, http_client, send};

let client = http_client(Duration::from_secs(15), Target::Fixed)?;
let request = client
    .post(format!("{}/v1/orders", self.base_url))
    .bearer_auth(key.as_str())
    .header("content-type", "application/json")
    .body(serde_json::to_vec(&body).map_err(Error::internal)?);
let reply = send(request, "acme", "create_order")
    .await
    .map_err(|_| payment::provider_unavailable())?;
if !reply.is_success() {
    return Err(payment::provider_rejected("…the partner's documented error code…"));
}
}

send logs the provider, the purpose and the HTTP status, never the address, headers or body, and counts calls in kernel_provider_calls_total. The provider’s own address is not a tenant setting: declare it as an operator setting (AUTOXIDE_<NAME>_API_URL, with the provider’s production address as the default) so tests and sandboxes can point it elsewhere.

Send the id Autoxide gives you (payment_id, document_id, reference…) as the provider’s own idempotency or merchant reference, so a retried call does not create a second payment, parcel, message or invoice.

Register a ConnectionProbe (context.connection_probe) that makes one cheap authenticated call, so the tenant can test the account from the settings page. Report each use with context.connection_status().record(…); the message must not contain a secret.

4. Receive webhooks

Every tenant has its own webhook address. Its last part identifies the tenant and cannot be guessed; the receiving module finds the tenant from it first, and the adapter then checks the notification with that tenant’s secret.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_kernel::provider::{WebhookAck, WebhookEndpoint, constant_time_eq, hex, hmac_sha256};

// In `Module::start`: the tenant then finds its address in `GET /api/v1/kernel/connections/webhooks`.
accounts.register_webhook(WebhookEndpoint::new(
    "acme.connection.api",
    "/api/v1/ledger/webhooks/acme",
    "Paste into Acme dashboard > Webhooks > Endpoint URL.",
));

// In the trait:
async fn verify_webhook(&self, tenant: TenantId, headers: &HeaderMap, body: &[u8])
    -> Result<GatewayNotification, Error> {
    let tenant = self.accounts.tenant(tenant).await?;
    let secret = self.accounts.require(&tenant, &WEBHOOK_SECRET).await?;
    let wanted = hex(&hmac_sha256(secret.as_str().as_bytes(), body)); // on the RAW body
    let given = headers.get("x-acme-signature").and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok()).unwrap_or("");
    if !constant_time_eq(wanted.as_bytes(), given.as_bytes()) {
        return Err(payment::signature_invalid());
    }
    // …only now read the body…
}

fn webhook_ack(&self) -> Option<WebhookAck> {
    Some(WebhookAck::json(200, r#"{"received":true}"#)) // what the partner's documentation asks for
}
}
  • Check the signature (or API key) in constant time, on the raw body, before reading anything.
  • Give every notification a stable id (event_id, provider_txn_id): the receiving module stores each id once per tenant, so a notification sent again changes nothing.
  • The address alone proves nothing. A provider that offers no signature or key at all cannot be connected safely; do not accept unauthenticated notifications.

The receiving routes are POST /api/v1/ledger/webhooks/{provider}/{hook} (payment gateways) and POST /api/v1/ledger/bank-feeds/{provider}/{hook} (bank feeds). A module that receives another kind of webhook adds a route of the same shape and resolves the tenant with ProviderAccounts::resolve_webhook.

The webhook address in a request

Some providers want the address in every request (an ipnUrl, a CallbackUrl). Ask for the tenant’s full address with ProviderAccounts::webhook_url(&tenant, path): it is built from the server’s AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL and fails with public_url_missing when that is not set. Never build it from the Host header of a request. ProviderAccounts::webhook_token(&tenant, path) gives only the last part.

Sandbox accounts

A provider’s test account usually works only against the provider’s sandbox address. When the provider has one, declare a tenant setting <module>.connection.<kind>.environment checked with Environment::check (production, the default, or sandbox), and two operator settings, AUTOXIDE_<NAME>_API_URL and AUTOXIDE_<NAME>_SANDBOX_API_URL. The tenant chooses between the two fixed addresses with Environment::pick; it never types an address. A kernel sandbox tenant never reaches a real adapter at all: the kernel gives it the simulated partners.

Carriers use the carrier accounts of shipping

A shipping adapter is different: the module shipping already keeps carrier accounts per tenant (several per tenant, credentials encrypted), and ShippingCarrier receives the account in every call. Such an adapter declares no connection settings and no ConnectionProbe — the account is tested with ShippingCarrier::check — and uses only http_client, send, the signature helpers and the webhook functions above.

5. Test without the network

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
use autoxide_testkit::{FakeProviderServer, TestApp, TestDatabase};

let server = FakeProviderServer::start().await.unwrap();
server.reply("POST", "/v1/orders", 200, json!({"id": "A1"}));
let app = TestApp::builder(test)
    .setting("AUTOXIDE_ACME_API_URL", server.url())
    .tenant("one")
    .tenant("two")
    // …
    .module(crate::module())
    .build()
    .await
    .unwrap();
// …each tenant sets its own account, call the adapter, then:
let seen = server.take_requests();
assert_eq!(seen[0].header("authorization"), Some("Bearer key-of-one"));
}

Test, on both databases: the request the provider’s documentation describes (path, headers, signature, body), the documented error answers, a webhook with a wrong signature, the same webhook twice, and two tenants with two accounts that never mix.

6. Register and document

  • Add the module to crates/app/src/modules.rs, before the module that uses the contract, and its crate to Cargo.toml and crates/app/Cargo.toml.
  • Implement Module::description, Module::stability (Stability::Experimental until the adapter has run against the real service) and Module::depends_on (what start requires).
  • Add the module’s name to the experimental list in crates/app/src/e2e/module_selection.rs, a line to the table in docs/MODULES.md and docs/MODULES.vi.md, and its name to the module list expected in crates/app/tests/integration/cli.rs.
  • Tests that need another module (ledger, invoices, shipping…) go in crates/app/src/e2e/; a module’s own tests may not call another module’s module().
  • Say in the adapter’s guide how to turn it on: AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,<name>.
  • Add locales/vi.json for every error code of the adapter.
  • Add a changelog fragment and, for a compliance feature, the legal basis in a decision record.

Receiving events in real time

Vietnamese: realtime-events.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com), and the TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

GET /api/v1/kernel/events/stream keeps a connection open and pushes events to you as they happen, as Server-Sent Events: an admin screen refreshes when a post is published, a moderation queue when a comment comes in. Only events a module declares streamable are sent, with the same permission as reading the record over REST — the stream never pushes raw table changes. Systems that must not miss anything while they are offline for longer than a week use webhooks instead.

The server must set AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM=true; otherwise the endpoint answers 404 kernel.stream_disabled.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token

Which events stream

The module catalog lists each event with its stream_permission; events without it are not streamed. Today: content.entry_published (content.read), comments.comment_created (comments.moderate), media.item_uploaded (media.read).

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/modules/content" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

Open a stream

Name the events in names, comma-separated: module.event, or module.* for every streamable event of a module that you may see. This server does not enable streaming, so here it answers 404; with AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM=true it answers 200 and keeps the connection open (curl -N prints each event as it comes).

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/events/stream?names=content.entry_published,comments.*" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# expect: 404

Each event is one frame:

id: 0193f1c2-5a7e-7c3d-8e21-4b6f0a9d2c11
event: content.entry_published
data: {"id":"0193f1c2-5a7e-7c3d-8e21-4b6f0a9d2c11","name":"content.entry_published","occurred_at":"2026-11-18T09:30:00Z","subject":"content.entry:0193…","actor_kind":"user","payload":{"after":{…}}}

A : ping comment comes every 15 seconds so proxies keep the connection open.

Who sees what

  • Only events of your tenant.
  • For each event, the permission in stream_permission. Naming an event you may not see answers 403 permission_denied; with module.* such events are left out.
  • With a permission narrower than the whole tenant (a role at one organization unit), you receive only the events you caused yourself: events do not yet carry their unit.

Reconnect without losing events

Delivery is at least once. When the connection drops, reconnect with the Last-Event-ID header set to the last id you received — the browser’s EventSource does this for you — or with last_event_id= in the query when you cannot set headers. You then receive what you missed, and possibly a few events again: skip ids you already have.

Events are kept 7 days. When your last id is older, the stream sends event: reset first: reload your data over REST, then keep listening. The server also closes each stream after 30 minutes (so a removed permission takes effect) and when it shuts down; reconnect the same way. Several servers behind a load balancer are fine: every server reads events from the database, so you may reconnect to any of them.

Two-way: WebSocket

Apps that also send live signals (“typing”, “online”) — chat, a courier’s position screen — use GET /api/v1/kernel/events/ws instead: the same events, permissions, resuming and limits over a WebSocket, plus control messages from the app. Data is still written over REST. See Building a mobile or desktop app.

Limits

Each server keeps at most AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM_MAX_PER_USER streams per user (default 5), AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM_MAX_PER_TENANT per tenant (200) and AUTOXIDE_EVENTS_STREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS in all (1000); more answer 429 kernel.stream_too_many. Open one stream per screen with every event name it needs, not one per event. Behind Nginx, the response already carries X-Accel-Buffering: no; other proxies must not buffer text/event-stream.

With the SDK

EventSource cannot send an Authorization header, so read the stream with fetch:

const baseUrl = "https://api.example.com";
const token = "axk1_…"; // read it from your secret store
let lastId: string | undefined; // keep it across reconnects
const seen = new Set<string>(); // ids already handled
declare function handle(event: unknown): void; // your code

// Call it again when it returns: it resumes after lastId.
export async function listen(): Promise<void> {
  const response = await fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/v1/kernel/events/stream?names=content.entry_published`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`, ...(lastId ? { "Last-Event-ID": lastId } : {}) },
  });
  const reader = response.body!.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader();
  let buffer = "";
  for (;;) {
    const { value, done } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break; // closed by the server: reconnect with lastId
    buffer += value;
    let end;
    while ((end = buffer.indexOf("\n\n")) >= 0) {
      const frame = buffer.slice(0, end);
      buffer = buffer.slice(end + 2);
      const id = frame.match(/^id: (.*)$/m)?.[1];
      const data = frame.match(/^data: (.*)$/m)?.[1];
      if (frame.includes("event: reset")) { /* reload over REST */ }
      if (id && data && !seen.has(id)) { seen.add(id); lastId = id; handle(JSON.parse(data)); }
    }
  }
}

Retrying safely

Vietnamese: retries.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com), and the TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

A network error after you sent a write leaves you unsure whether it happened. Send an Idempotency-Key header (a random UUID per logical operation) with every write: a repeat with the same key within 24 hours returns the first result, with Idempotent-Replayed: true, instead of doing it twice.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token
# save: REFRESH=.data.refresh_token

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 0193e3a4-7b1c-7f00-9a51-6f2b8c0d4e11' \
  --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Written once"}'
# expect: 201
# save: ID=.data.id

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 0193e3a4-7b1c-7f00-9a51-6f2b8c0d4e11' \
  --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Written once"}'
# expect: 201
# expect-header: idempotent-replayed: true

Using the same key for a different request is a mistake the server refuses (idempotency_key_reused, 422): make a new key for each distinct operation.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: 0193e3a4-7b1c-7f00-9a51-6f2b8c0d4e11' \
  --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Something else"}'
# expect: 422

Notes:

  • A request still running answers 409 idempotency_key_in_progress with Retry-After; retry after that many seconds.
  • A result that holds a secret shown once (a new API key) is not kept: a repeat answers 409 idempotency_result_not_kept. Read the key list to see whether it was created.
  • Business commands that move goods or money also take a reference of your own (reference), unique per operation, so even a retry after 24 hours is not done twice.

With the SDK

import { AutoxideError, createClient } from "@autoxide/sdk";

const api = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com", token: "axk1_…" /* read it from your secret store */ });

// One key per logical operation, reused on every retry of it.
const key = crypto.randomUUID();
for (let attempt = 1; ; attempt++) {
  try {
    const entry = await api.post("/api/v1/content/entries", {
      body: { kind: "post", title: "Written once" },
      idempotencyKey: key,
    });
    console.log(entry.id);
    break;
  } catch (error) {
    const retryable = error instanceof TypeError || (error instanceof AutoxideError && error.status >= 500);
    if (!retryable || attempt === 3) throw error;
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, attempt * 1000));
  }
}

Common Rust compiler errors when writing a module

Seven errors that almost everyone meets in the first week, with the line to look for, why it happens in an Autoxide module, and the fix. The messages are real output of the pinned toolchain. When the error is not here, run rustc --explain E0xxx (the code in the first line) and read the “help:” lines: they are usually right.

1. no field … on type impl Future (E0609)

error[E0609]: no field `title` on type `impl Future<Output = Result<Note, String>>`

A call to an async fn returns a future, not the value. Add .await: let note = find(1).await?;. Services, database calls and Outbox::record are all async.

2. `?` couldn't convert the error to `Error` (E0277)

error[E0277]: `?` couldn't convert the error to `Error`
  the trait `From<ParseIntError>` is not implemented for `Error`

? turns the error on the right into the error type of your function using From. In a module your functions return autoxide_kernel::error::Error, which converts from the database error and from validation errors. For anything else map it yourself and give it a stable code: .map_err(|_| Error::bad_request("notes.invalid_number", "…"))?.

3. borrow of moved value (E0382)

error[E0382]: borrow of moved value: `title`
  value moved here  /  value borrowed here after move

Passing a String to a function gives it away. Either pass a reference (&title, and take &str in the function), or .clone() it when you really need two owners. Prefer the reference: the compiler’s own hint says “consider changing this parameter type … to borrow instead”.

4. future cannot be sent between threads safely

error: future cannot be sent between threads safely
  the trait `Send` is not implemented for `Rc<i32>`
  future is not `Send` as this value is used across an await

Handlers and services run on several threads, so everything alive across an .await must be Send. Rc and RefCell are not (use Arc and a lock); a std::sync::MutexGuard is not either: end its scope (or drop it) before the .await. Never hold a database transaction guard and a lock at the same time across a slow call.

5. async block may outlive the current function (E0373)

error[E0373]: async block may outlive the current function, but it borrows `name`
help: to force the async block to take ownership of `name` … use the `move` keyword

A spawned task (tokio::spawn, a job handler) can run after the function returns, so it must own what it uses. Write async move { … } and clone what you still need afterwards, before the block.

6. non-exhaustive patterns (E0004)

error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `Status::Published` not covered

A match must handle every variant. Add the arm. For an enum of the kernel marked #[non_exhaustive] the compiler also asks for a final _ => arm, on purpose: the kernel may add variants in a minor release, and your code must not break when it does.

7. no method named … found although the method exists (E0599)

error[E0599]: no method named `find` found for struct `S` in the current scope
  items from traits can only be used if the trait is in scope
help: … perhaps you want to import it: use crate::api::Notes;

Trait methods need the trait imported. For another module’s service that is use autoxide_<name>::api::<Trait>;. Same for ScopeExt (.scoped(&tenant)) and the sea_orm traits (EntityTrait, QueryFilter) in the current SeaORM-based API.

Errors from the repository’s own checks

cargo xtask check and cargo xtask check-module print how to fix: under every violation. Start there.

Trying changes in a sandbox

A sandbox is a test copy of your tenant. Change pages, roles, templates or settings there, try payments and notifications without touching real customers or real partners, then bring what you like back as drafts. Sandboxes exist when the server runs several tenants (AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_MODE=multi).

Vietnamese: sandbox.vi.md.

Create a sandbox

You need kernel.sandboxes.manage in your tenant. Your plan sets how many sandboxes you may keep at the same time (kernel.sandboxes, 1 when the plan does not say).

TENANT=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenant" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq -r .data.id)
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenants/$TENANT/sandboxes" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  --json '{"name": "Try the new theme", "role_id": null}'

The answer is 201 with the sandbox (status: "provisioning") and job_id. Follow the job at GET /api/v1/kernel/jobs/{job_id}; when it is done the sandbox is active.

What is copied: settings that are not secret, roles, pages (published pages stay published), the notification templates in use. What is never copied: users, buyers, orders, ledger, documents, notifications, private files, secrets and partner connection details, domains, API keys. Not copied either: products, prices, stock, delivery methods and rates, the tax profile, invoice series. To try a sale, build the shop inside the sandbox; the shop guide lists the steps.

Work inside it

Holders of role_id in your tenant (the admin role by default) enter the sandbox with one header; there is no separate account:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenant" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX"

Send the header with every call, the public ones too (a guest’s cart and checkout, address codes): without a sign-in it is the header that picks the shop. The sandbox’s slug works there as well as its id.

Every answer from a sandbox carries Autoxide-Sandbox: true and X-Robots-Tag: noindex, nofollow. Its public website has an empty sitemap and shows a “test copy” label instead of the ministry badge.

Inside a sandbox:

  • Partners are always simulated. Payments are created at a simulated partner and stay pending until you complete them (below); refunds and payouts succeed; e-invoices are accepted with references starting with SANDBOX- (provider_ref, lookup_code, authority_code; the invoice number is the usual one); identity checks pass. Nothing reaches a bank, a carrier, a tax provider or an SMS gateway, whatever your tenant has set up. These results are never legal evidence.
  • Mail reaches only the verified e-mail of staff who may enter the sandbox. Mail to anyone else is kept, not sent.
  • Webhooks go only to URLs that start with a prefix in the tenant setting kernel.sandbox.webhook_urls (set it inside the sandbox; empty by default). Other deliveries get the status sandboxed.

Everything kept back is listed in the sandbox message box:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/sandbox/messages?channel=mail" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX"

Complete a simulated payment

No partner notifies a sandbox, so a payment made there (an order paid by card or wallet, for example) stays pending until you play the partner. The server operator first allows it with AUTOXIDE_LEDGER_SANDBOX_SIMULATION=true (off by default; it never works outside a sandbox). Then, with ledger.reconcile, find the order’s payment in the ledger (an order’s payments carry source_id = the order’s id; an order’s payment action also gives it as ledger_payment_id) and answer for the partner. The newest payment comes first: after a failed one, starting the payment again (payment-link) creates a new one.

# The order's payment at the partner (the order's id is $ORDER).
LEDGER_PAYMENT_ID=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/ledger/payments?source_module=orders&source_id=$ORDER" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX" | jq -r '.data[0].id')

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/ledger/payments/$LEDGER_PAYMENT_ID/simulate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX" \
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"outcome": "succeeded"}'

It goes through the same path as a partner notification: the payment becomes succeeded and the order confirmed a moment later. {"outcome": "failed"} makes the payment fail; an amount other than the amount due ({"outcome": "succeeded", "amount": {"amount": "100000", "currency": "VND"}}) puts it in needs_review, to practise resolving a difference. Only pending payments created inside the sandbox can be simulated; bank transfer (VietQR) payments are not supported yet. AI agents use the MCP tool ledger.simulate_payment.

Bring changes back

From your real tenant (without Autoxide-Tenant), promote records of the sandbox. List the kinds with GET /api/v1/kernel/sandboxes/promotable.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/sandboxes/$SANDBOX/promote" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" \
  --json '{"items": [{"kind": "content.page", "id": "'"$PAGE"'"}]}'

Each record gets an outcome:

OutcomeMeaning
created_draftA new draft in your tenant (the record was made in the sandbox)
updated_draftThe draft of the original was replaced; what is live is unchanged until you publish
unchangedAlready promoted with the same content
conflictA slug, name or code is taken in your tenant; see conflict.field

Nothing is published or enabled for you, and you need the permission of the module too (for example content.write for a page). Agents do the same with the MCP tools kernel.list_promotable and kernel.promote_sandbox.

Extend or delete

POST /api/v1/kernel/sandboxes/{id}/extend gives it another AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_SANDBOX_DAYS days (30 by default) from now. DELETE /api/v1/kernel/sandboxes/{id} deletes it and everything tried in it at once; promote first what you want to keep.

Syncing staff from your identity provider (SCIM 2.0)

Vietnamese: scim.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

A company that keeps its people in Microsoft Entra ID, Okta or Google Workspace can let that system manage their Autoxide accounts over SCIM 2.0: someone added there gets a staff account here; someone who leaves is disabled at once — their sessions, refresh tokens and API keys are revoked in the same step, with no one having to remember.

The SCIM endpoint is /api/v1/auth/scim/v2 (Users, Groups, ServiceProviderConfig, ResourceTypes, Schemas). It follows the SCIM standard, not the usual Autoxide conventions: bodies are application/scim+json, lists are ListResponse with startIndex / count, and errors use the SCIM error schema (status, scimType, detail).

1. Create a SCIM token

Needs the permission auth.scim.manage, a plan with the feature auth.scim, and a signed-in session: an API key cannot create one (auth.session_required). The token belongs to the tenant, works only on the SCIM endpoint, and is shown once.

A token can do only what the person who created it can do now. It can create accounts, but it gives, takes away, disables or deletes only within that person’s current permissions: an account with permissions they lack cannot be disabled or deleted with it, and a group’s role they could not give themselves cannot be given or taken away through it (403). Create the token from an account that holds every role your group mappings give — usually an administrator.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/scim/tokens" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --json '{"name":"Microsoft Entra ID"}'
# expect: 201
# save: SCIM=.data.token_secret

The response also has scim_base_path (/api/v1/auth/scim/v2): put your server’s public address in front of it for the provider. List tokens with GET /api/v1/auth/scim/tokens (never with their secret). To rotate, create a new token, switch the provider to it, then DELETE /api/v1/auth/scim/tokens/{id} the old one. A tenant has at most 5.

Rotate the token when its creator leaves or loses roles. Otherwise removing people from mapped groups and disabling leavers fails quietly in the provider (it receives 403). GET /api/v1/auth/scim/tokens shows creator_status for each token: disabled, deleted or missing_permission (no longer holds auth.scim.manage) means rotate now. A creator who was only demoted shows active but the token is limited to their new roles: rotate then too.

2. Set up the provider

  • Microsoft Entra ID — Enterprise applications → New application → Create your own application (not in the gallery). Under Provisioning, choose Automatic; Tenant URL https://api.example.com/api/v1/auth/scim/v2, Secret Token the SCIM token; Test Connection. In Mappings, keep userName ← userPrincipalName, map emails[type eq "work"].value ← mail, and prefer externalId ← objectId. Entra disables people with PATCH active=false and deletes them later.
  • Okta — open the app integration, General → Provisioning: SCIM. In Provisioning → Integration: SCIM connector base URL as above, Unique identifier field for users userName, actions Push New Users, Push Profile Updates and Push Groups, Authentication Mode HTTP Header with the SCIM token. Under To App, turn on Create Users, Update User Attributes and Deactivate Users.
  • Google Workspace — automatic provisioning only reaches apps in Google’s catalog. Until Autoxide is listed there, use a SCIM bridge that reads Google Workspace, or let staff sign in with Google (oidc.md) and give new accounts a role there.

Check what the server supports (no token needed):

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/scim/v2/ServiceProviderConfig"

3. What each call does

Provider callIn Autoxide
GET /Users?filter=userName eq "…"Finds the linked account (userName without case; externalId with case).
POST /UsersCreates a staff account without a password — the person signs in with your sign-in provider or sets a password by reset. An existing staff account with the same email, not yet linked, is taken over instead of duplicated.
PUT / PATCH /Users/{id}Changes userName, externalId, the name and the work email (treated as verified). Never the password or two-step sign-in. Any change to an account with permissions the token’s creator lacks is refused (403) — so a provider using a token created by someone who is not an administrator gets 403 whenever it changes anything about an administrator. Changing the email of a linked account also signs it out everywhere and removes its password, passkeys, two-step sign-in and API keys: the person signs in through your provider or resets the password at the new address. SCIM tokens the account created are revoked too. Run machine-to-machine integrations with an API key of a separate service account whose email your provider does not manage, or they stop when the provider changes a person’s email (for example a new email domain). The same goes for the SCIM token itself: create it from a separate staff account whose email the provider does not manage, or changing (or disabling) its creator revokes the very token the provider is using and syncing stops with 401.
active: falseDisables the account and, in the same transaction, revokes every session, refresh token and API key. Turning it back on does not bring the API keys back. The last active administrator cannot be disabled (409).
DELETE /Users/{id}Deletes the account like any account deletion; other modules delete what they keep about the person.

Example calls, as a provider makes them:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/scim/v2/Users" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM" \
  --json '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:core:2.0:User"],"userName":"grace@example.com","externalId":"8f2c1e","name":{"givenName":"Grace","familyName":"Hopper"},"emails":[{"value":"grace@example.com","type":"work","primary":true}],"active":true}'
# expect: 201
# save: USER=.id

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/scim/v2/Users?filter=userName%20eq%20%22Grace%40example.com%22" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM"

curl -sS -X PATCH "$API/api/v1/auth/scim/v2/Users/$USER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $SCIM" \
  --json '{"schemas":["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:PatchOp"],"Operations":[{"op":"replace","path":"active","value":false}]}'

Every change is in the audit log with the actor kind scim.

4. Groups and roles

The provider can also push its groups (/Groups; Okta: Push Groups, Entra ID: assign groups to the app). A group gives nothing by itself: the tenant decides what it means with mapping rules — “members of group X hold role R at unit N”.

  1. Let the provider push the group, then find its id with GET /api/v1/auth/scim/groups (member count, rule count). Groups without a rule also show up in the work inbox (auth.scim_unmapped_groups).
  2. Add a rule with POST /api/v1/auth/scim/group-mappings and {"group_id": "…", "org_id": "…", "role_id": "…"} (org_id is the tenant id for the root unit). You must be able to give that role at that unit yourself. Current members get the role at once; the response lists who holds it now in granted_user_ids, and who could not be given it (for example the plan’s staff limit is reached) in failed with an error code — they get it on the next successful sync. Check a group’s members before mapping it to a powerful role: while a group has no rules, anyone holding a SCIM token can add people to it.
  3. From then on, people added to or removed from the group gain or lose the role at once — if the SCIM token’s creator can give that role; otherwise the change is refused (403) and nothing is written. A role someone was given by hand is never removed by SCIM, and a role two groups give stays while the person is in either.

Remove a rule with DELETE /api/v1/auth/scim/group-mappings/{id} (you must be able to give its role yourself, auth.role_beyond_you otherwise); deleting the group in the provider removes its rules and the roles it gave.

5. What is supported

  • Filters: eq, ne, co, sw, ew, pr, joined with and / or and parentheses. Users by userName, externalId, emails, active, id. Anything else answers 400 with scimType invalidFilter.
  • PATCH (RFC 7644 §3.5.2): add, replace, remove, with paths such as active, name.givenName, emails[type eq "work"].value, or without a path. Attributes Autoxide does not keep (enterprise extension, phone numbers, title…) are ignored.
  • Paging: startIndex (from 1) and count (at most 200).
  • Not supported: bulk, sorting, ETags, password change.

Errors: 401 without a valid SCIM token, 403 when the plan lacks auth.scim or the change goes beyond the token creator’s permissions (no scimType), 404 for an id of another tenant, 409 uniqueness when userName, externalId or the email belongs to another account, 400 invalidValue / invalidSyntax / invalidPath / noTarget / mutability for a wrong body.

Personal data

The tenant is the controller of its staff data and Autoxide processes it on the tenant’s instructions (Vietnam’s Personal Data Protection Law 91/2025/QH15 — check the original text with a legal expert). Only the attributes listed above are stored; the SCIM link is exported with the account and deleted with it.

Issuing e-invoices through SePay eInvoice

With the einvoice_sepay adapter, an invoice issued in Autoxide is sent to the tax authority through SePay eInvoice, and its result (accepted, with the tax authority’s code, or refused, with the reason) comes back onto the document.

Vietnamese: sepay-einvoice.vi.md.

Experimental. This adapter was written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service. Try it against SePay’s sandbox before relying on it. You stay responsible for the content of your invoices; this guide is not legal advice.

The operator turns the adapter on by naming it: AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,einvoice_sepay (experimental modules are off by default). Each tenant connects its own SePay eInvoice account. The client secret is stored encrypted and is never shown again.

1. Store your SePay eInvoice account

You need the permission kernel.settings.manage.

for field in client_id client_secret provider_account_id; do
  read -r -p "$field: " value
  curl -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/einvoice_sepay.connection.api.$field" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d "{\"value\": \"$value\"}"
done

# Test it: gets a token and reads the provider accounts
curl -X POST "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/einvoice_sepay.connection.api.client_id/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
SettingWhat it is
einvoice_sepay.connection.api.client_idClient id of your SePay eInvoice account.
einvoice_sepay.connection.api.client_secretIts client secret.
einvoice_sepay.connection.api.environmentproduction (the default) or sandbox. Set sandbox for a SePay eInvoice test account: it then talks to SePay’s sandbox and issues test invoices only.
einvoice_sepay.connection.api.provider_account_idWhich e-invoice provider account to issue with. May be left unset when your SePay account has exactly one active provider account.

2. Point an invoice series at SePay

Set einvoice_provider of the invoice series to sepay. Documents of that series are then sent when they are issued, and asked about until the tax authority answers.

What is sent, and what is not

  • VAT invoices (SePay template 1) and sales invoices (template 2), in Vietnamese dong.
  • The invoice symbol comes from your SePay account; the one of the Autoxide series is not used.
  • Tax rates 0, 5, 8 and 10 %, and “not subject to tax”. Another rate is refused before anything is sent.
  • A corrected invoice is sent as a replacement or an adjustment of the original one.
  • Sending the same document again never creates a second invoice: SePay knows it by the document’s id.
  • The invoice number is given by the provider. Once the invoice is accepted it is on the document as provider_number, next to the tax authority’s code; the document’s own number in Autoxide may differ.
  • Cancelling is not available through SePay’s API: correct an invoice with a replacement or an adjustment.

Confirming bank transfers with SePay

SePay reports the transactions of your own bank account. With the sepay adapter, a VietQR payment created in Autoxide is confirmed by itself when the buyer’s transfer arrives: the money goes straight to your bank account, and Autoxide only reads the report.

Vietnamese: sepay.vi.md.

Experimental. This adapter was written from the provider’s public documentation; not yet verified against the live service. Try it with a small real transfer (or SePay’s test mode) before relying on it.

The operator turns the adapter on by naming it: AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,sepay (experimental modules are off by default). Each tenant connects its own SePay account. Nothing here is a server-wide setting, and the secrets you store are encrypted and never shown again.

1. Store your SePay account

You need the permission kernel.settings.manage.

# 1. The webhook secret you chose at SePay (HMAC-SHA256)
curl -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/sepay.connection.bank.webhook_secret" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value": "<secret key of the SePay webhook>"}'

# 2. The API token, to read transactions a webhook missed and to test the connection
curl -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/sepay.connection.bank.api_token" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"value": "<API token of the SePay company>"}'

# 3. Test it
curl -X POST "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/sepay.connection.bank.api_token/test" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
SettingWhat it is
sepay.connection.bank.webhook_secretSecret Key of the SePay webhook with HMAC-SHA256 authentication (recommended).
sepay.connection.bank.webhook_api_keyAPI Key of the SePay webhook with API Key authentication. Used only when no secret key is set.
sepay.connection.bank.api_tokenAPI token of your SePay company (Company settings > API Keys).

Notifications are refused until one of the two webhook settings is set. Autoxide never accepts a notification without authentication, so do not choose “no authentication” at SePay.

2. Create the webhook at SePay

Ask Autoxide for your webhook address. It is yours alone; its last part identifies your tenant.

curl "$API/api/v1/kernel/connections/webhooks" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

At my.sepay.vn > Webhooks, add a webhook with:

  • URL: the url of the line sepay.connection.bank (or the server’s public address followed by path).
  • Data format: JSON.
  • Authentication: HMAC-SHA256, with the same secret key you stored in step 1.
  • Resend when the server answers with an error: on, so a notification refused during maintenance is sent again.

Autoxide answers {"success": true} as SePay expects, checks the signature on the raw body, refuses a notification signed more than 5 minutes ago, and stores a notification that is sent again only once.

3. Say which bank account SePay reports

curl -X POST "$API/api/v1/ledger/bank-accounts" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"bank_bin": "970436", "account_number": "1017588888", "account_name": "CUA HANG A", "feed_provider": "sepay"}'

From then on, create payments with POST /api/v1/ledger/payments/vietqr. A transfer whose description keeps the payment’s transfer_code and whose amount is exact marks the payment as paid. Another amount, an unknown code or a second transfer waits for a person in GET /api/v1/ledger/exceptions.

Good to know

  • SePay sends no webhook for transactions made with a static NAPAS QR code. With the API token set, Autoxide reads the transaction list instead when the bank account is polled.
  • A transaction that reaches Autoxide by webhook and again from the transaction list is stored once when the bank gave it a reference code. Without a reference code the second copy is not matched to a payment twice: it waits in the exceptions list.
  • The SePay API allows 3 requests per second; when SePay answers “too many requests” the work is retried later.
  • The checkout page of the SePay payment gateway (cards, NAPAS) is not connected by this adapter.

Opening a shop: your first order from product to e-invoice

This guide takes a fresh quickstart server to a first real sale: a product with a price and stock, a guest buyer’s cart, delivery quoted by Giao Hàng Nhanh (GHN), payment with MoMo, an SMS through eSMS for each step, the parcel booked with GHN, and the e-invoice issued through SePay eInvoice once the parcel is delivered. Every command is a curl call you can paste. The same flow runs as a test on SQLite and PostgreSQL on every build (crates/app/src/e2e/shop.rs).

Vietnamese: shop.vi.md.

Experimental connectors. The four provider adapters (MoMo, GHN, eSMS, SePay eInvoice) were written from each provider’s public documentation and are not yet verified against the live services. Use each provider’s sandbox first, then a small real order. Money always goes straight from the buyer to your own MoMo account; Autoxide never holds it.

What you need

  • A server from the quickstart, reachable from the internet over HTTPS (MoMo and GHN send their notifications to it). For a test on your computer, a tunnel (for example cloudflared or ngrok) to http://127.0.0.1:8080 is enough.
  • An account at each provider, in your shop’s name: a MoMo business account (Partner Code, Access Key, Secret Key), a GHN shop (API token and ShopId), an eSMS account with a registered brandname (ApiKey, SecretKey) and a SePay eInvoice account (client id, client secret, provider account id). Each guide below says where to find these values.
  • curl and jq (the examples read answers with jq).
  • No provider account yet? Go through Try it without real accounts first: the same steps inside a sandbox, where every partner is simulated.
  • Before selling to the public in Vietnam: notify your sales website to the Ministry of Industry and Trade (Decree 52/2013/ND-CP as amended) and publish your terms; see the compliance module. This guide does not replace legal advice.

1. Turn on the connectors

The quickstart runs the official modules only. Add these lines to .env next to compose.quickstart.yml, then start again:

cat >> .env <<'EOF'
AUTOXIDE_MODULES=official,momo,ghn,esms,einvoice_sepay
AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL=https://shop-api.example.com
EOF
docker compose -f compose.quickstart.yml up -d

AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL is the HTTPS address at which the internet reaches your server (your tunnel’s address when testing). The quickstart already loaded the reference data this guide needs: Vietnamese administrative units (address.import) and the tax pack (tax.import_pack).

Sign in and keep the token (it lasts 15 minutes; sign in again when a call answers 401). Storing a provider account needs a recent sign-in, so sign in again before step 2 if it has been a while.

API=http://127.0.0.1:8080
TOKEN=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"<your password>"}' | jq -r .data.access_token)
ORG=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/organizations/units?limit=1" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq -r '.data[0].id')

ORG is your shop: the root unit of your organization tree.

2. Connect your provider accounts

Every value is stored for your shop only; secrets are encrypted and never shown again. The details of each provider are in its own guide: MoMo, GHN, eSMS, SePay eInvoice.

MoMo — payments:

for pair in partner_code=MOMOXXXX access_key=<Access Key> secret_key=<Secret Key>; do
  curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/momo.connection.account.${pair%%=*}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"value\": \"${pair#*=}\"}"
done

The page a buyer returns to after paying must be one of your shop’s own addresses: an https:// address on a domain you verified (POST /api/v1/kernel/domains), or an origin you list here — your website, your app’s universal link domain, http://localhost:3000 while developing. Any other return_url is refused, so a payment link cannot send your buyers to someone else’s site:

curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/ledger.payments.return_origins" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"value": "https://shop.example.com"}'

eSMS — the SMS sent to buyers. Until you set it, SMS notifications are skipped with the reason channel_disabled (nothing is retried, nothing fails):

for pair in api_key=<ApiKey> secret_key=<SecretKey> brandname=<Brandname>; do
  curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/esms.connection.sms.${pair%%=*}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"value\": \"${pair#*=}\"}"
done

SePay eInvoice — e-invoices, and an invoice series that uses it:

for pair in client_id=<client id> client_secret=<client secret> provider_account_id=<provider account id>; do
  curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/kernel/settings/einvoice_sepay.connection.api.${pair%%=*}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d "{\"value\": \"${pair#*=}\"}"
done
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/invoices/series" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind": "vat_invoice", "symbol": "1C26TAA", "year": 2026, "einvoice_provider": "sepay"}'

GHN — delivery. The carrier account answers with webhook_path once: keep it. Then a delivery method that uses the account and books each parcel with GHN by itself (auto_book):

GHN=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/shipping/carrier-accounts" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"carrier_code\": \"ghn\", \"name\": \"GHN\", \"credentials\": {\"token\": \"<GHN token>\"}, \"settings\": {\"shop_id\": <ShopId>}}")
echo "$GHN" | jq -r .data.webhook_path
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/shipping/methods" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"code\": \"ghn\", \"kind\": \"carrier\", \"names\": {\"vi\": \"Giao Hàng Nhanh\", \"en\": \"GHN\"}, \"currency\": \"VND\", \"carrier_account_id\": \"$(echo "$GHN" | jq -r .data.id)\", \"auto_book\": true}"

No e-invoice account yet? A series without einvoice_provider still numbers your invoices inside Autoxide (internal documents, not sent to the tax authority). Without any series no invoice is issued at delivery; with two series of the same kind, year and unit, pick one when issuing (series_id). Ask for an order’s invoice again with POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/invoice.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/invoices/series" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind": "vat_invoice", "symbol": "1C26TAA", "year": 2026}'

Tax profile — who sells and under which tax rules. Tax on the cart and the seller on every invoice (name, tax code, address) come from it; without it tax is computed as vat_credit and invoices carry no seller details. regime is vat_credit, vat_direct, household or exempt; business_lines are goods, services, production_transport or other:

curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/tax/profiles/$ORG" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jurisdiction": "VN", "regime": "vat_credit", "tax_code": "0101234567", "legal_name": "Công ty TNHH Trà Việt",
       "business_lines": ["goods"]}'

Your own delivery fees (no carrier account): a zone, a method with fixed rates by weight. A zone listing a province ({"country": "VN", "province_code": "01"}) wins over the whole country. Items without a weight use default_item_weight_grams:

ZONE=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/shipping/zones" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"name\": \"Viet Nam\", \"regions\": [{\"country\": \"VN\"}]}" | jq -r .data.id)
METHOD=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/shipping/methods" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"code\": \"standard\", \"kind\": \"table_rate\", \"names\": {\"vi\": \"Giao tiêu chuẩn\", \"en\": \"Standard\"},
       \"currency\": \"VND\", \"default_item_weight_grams\": 500}" | jq -r .data.id)
curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/shipping/methods/$METHOD/rates" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"rates\": [{\"zone_id\": \"$ZONE\", \"min_weight_grams\": 0, \"amount\": {\"amount\": \"30000\", \"currency\": \"VND\"}}]}"

In the GHN dashboard, register AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL + webhook_path as the status webhook (see the GHN guide). MoMo needs nothing: Autoxide sends your notification address with every payment.

3. A product with a price and stock

Give the weight and size of one item: GHN prices the parcel from them.

PRODUCT=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/catalog/products" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kind": "physical", "tax_category": "vat.standard", "locale": "vi", "text": {"name": "Ấm trà"},
       "variant": {"sku": "TEA-1", "weight_grams": 600, "length_mm": 300, "width_mm": 200, "height_mm": 100}}')
PRODUCT_ID=$(echo "$PRODUCT" | jq -r .data.id)
VARIANT=$(echo "$PRODUCT" | jq -r '.data.variants[0].id')

LIST=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/catalog/price-lists" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "Retail", "currency": "VND", "tax_inclusive": true}' | jq -r .data.id)
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/catalog/price-lists/$LIST/prices" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"reference\": \"opening\", \"prices\": [{\"variant_id\": \"$VARIANT\", \"amount\": {\"amount\": \"150000\", \"currency\": \"VND\"}}]}"

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/inventory/adjustments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"org_id\": \"$ORG\", \"reference\": \"opening-1\", \"lines\": [{\"variant_id\": \"$VARIANT\", \"quantity\": 10, \"reason_code\": \"found\", \"unit_cost\": {\"amount\": \"90000\", \"currency\": \"VND\"}}]}"

curl -sS -X POST "$API/api/v1/catalog/products/$PRODUCT_ID/status" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'If-Match: *' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"status": "active"}'

4. Buy it as a guest

This is what your website does. No sign-in: the cart is identified by the Cart-Token it returns. Prices, discounts, tax and delivery fee are always computed by the server.

CART=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/carts" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}')
CART_ID=$(echo "$CART" | jq -r .data.id)
CART_TOKEN=$(echo "$CART" | jq -r .data.cart_token)

curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/orders/carts/$CART_ID/lines/$VARIANT" -H "Cart-Token: $CART_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"quantity": 2}'

# Where to deliver: codes from GET /api/v1/address/provinces and GET /api/v1/address/units?province=<code>.
curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/orders/carts/$CART_ID/delivery" -H "Cart-Token: $CART_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"recipient_name": "Nguyễn An", "phone": "0912345678",
       "address": {"country": "VN", "province_code": "01", "commune_code": "00004", "line": "12 Tràng Tiền"}}' \
  | jq '.data.shipping.options'

The options list GHN’s fee for this parcel (the recipient, the address and the parcel’s weight and size are sent to GHN). Choose one by sending its option_key with the same address, then place the order. Keep the Idempotency-Key: sending the same request again returns the same order.

QUOTE=$(curl -sS -X PUT "$API/api/v1/orders/carts/$CART_ID/delivery" -H "Cart-Token: $CART_TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"recipient_name": "Nguyễn An", "phone": "0912345678", "shipping_option": "<option_key>",
       "address": {"country": "VN", "province_code": "01", "commune_code": "00004", "line": "12 Tràng Tiền"}}' \
  | jq -r .data.quote_token)

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/checkout" -H "Cart-Token: $CART_TOKEN" -H 'Idempotency-Key: first-order-1' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"cart_id\": \"$CART_ID\", \"quote_token\": \"$QUOTE\", \"payment_method\": \"wallet\",
       \"return_url\": \"https://shop.example.com/thank-you\",
       \"contact\": {\"name\": \"Nguyễn An\", \"phone\": \"0912345678\"}}"

return_url is the page of your website the buyer comes back to after paying (on one of your shop’s addresses, see step 2); MoMo requires one (or set momo.connection.account.return_url once for your shop). The answer has the order (pending_payment) and payment_actions[0]: a redirect to MoMo’s payment page. When the buyer has paid, MoMo notifies your server, and the order becomes confirmed / paid on its own. The buyer receives an SMS for the order placed and for the payment confirmed.

payment_method is cod (cash on delivery, when the cart has a delivery), bank_transfer, or a method of the payment partner (wallet, card…); the cart’s payment_methods lists cod, bank_transfer and gateway, where gateway stands for any method of the partner. Checkout gives a guest no token to read the order later: the buyer asks for one with the order number and phone, and confirms the code sent by SMS. The access_token then goes in the Order-Token header of /api/v1/orders/public/orders/… calls:

LOOKUP=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/public/orders/lookup" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{"number": "<order number>", "phone": "0912345678"}' | jq -r .data.lookup_id)
ORDER_TOKEN=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/public/orders/lookup/$LOOKUP/confirm" -H 'Content-Type: application/json'   -d '{"code": "<code from the SMS>"}' | jq -r .data.access_token)

5. Ship it

Note the order id from the checkout answer. Requesting the shipment accepts the order (preparing); GHN books the parcel by itself because the method has auto_book:

ORDER=<order id>
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/$ORDER/shipments" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}'
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/shipping/shipments?order_id=$ORDER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

From then on GHN’s status webhook moves the order: picked up → shipping, delivered → delivered. At delivery the e-invoice is issued through SePay eInvoice (orders.invoice_timing is on_delivered by default) and the buyer receives an SMS.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/orders/$ORDER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" | jq '.data | {status, payment_status}'
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/invoices/documents?source_module=orders&source_id=$ORDER" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  | jq '.data[0] | {status, number, authority_code}'

Try it without real accounts

Before you have provider accounts, run the whole flow in a sandbox: a test copy of a shop where every partner is simulated (payments, delivery, SMS, e-invoices) and nothing reaches a real one. A sandbox needs a server with several tenants, and its payments are completed by hand, so allow that too (both settings are off by default):

# Next to compose.quickstart.yml: several tenants, and simulated payments allowed inside sandboxes.
cat > compose.try.yml <<'EOF'
services:
  autoxide:
    environment:
      AUTOXIDE_TENANCY_MODE: multi
      AUTOXIDE_LEDGER_SANDBOX_SIMULATION: "true"
EOF
docker compose -f compose.quickstart.yml -f compose.try.yml up -d

# A shop tenant and its first administrator (the command prints the password).
X="docker compose -f compose.quickstart.yml -f compose.try.yml exec autoxide autoxide"
$X tenant create --slug demo --name "Demo shop"
$X user create --tenant demo --email owner@demo.example --name "Owner" --admin

# Sign in to the shop, then create a sandbox of it.
API=http://127.0.0.1:8080
TOKEN=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" -H 'Autoxide-Tenant: demo' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"owner@demo.example","password":"<printed password>"}' | jq -r .data.access_token)
TENANT=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenant" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Autoxide-Tenant: demo' | jq -r .data.id)
SANDBOX=$(curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenants/$TENANT/sandboxes" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Autoxide-Tenant: demo' -H "Idempotency-Key: $(openssl rand -hex 16)" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name": "First sale"}' | jq -r .data.id)
curl -sS "$API/api/v1/kernel/tenant" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX" | jq .data.status

The status is active once the copy is done (a few seconds). Then do steps 1 to 5 with two changes:

  • Send -H "Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX" with every call, the public ones too (cart, checkout, address codes): without a sign-in, that header is what picks the shop. Skip step 2’s provider accounts; in step 1 AUTOXIDE_MODULES still names the connectors, so their simulated twins exist.
  • A new sandbox is empty: it copies settings, roles and pages, not products, prices, stock, delivery methods, the tax profile or invoice series. Create them inside it (step 2’s series without einvoice_provider, the tax profile, your own delivery fees; step 3). If there are several payment partners, set the default one inside the sandbox too.

After checkout the payment stays pending, because no partner notifies a sandbox. Complete it as the partner would: see Complete a simulated payment. The order then becomes confirmed / paid, and you continue with step 5. Delete the sandbox when you are done (DELETE /api/v1/kernel/sandboxes/{id} from the shop, without Autoxide-Tenant: $SANDBOX).

When something does not happen

What you seeWhy, and what to do
A call answers provider.not_configuredA field of that provider account is not set. GET /api/v1/kernel/settings?group=connection lists what each connection needs.
An SMS has status skipped, reason channel_disabled (GET /api/v1/notifications/messages)eSMS is not set up for your shop yet. Messages before that are not sent again.
Checkout answers that provider is requiredThe server has several payment partners. Set your default one: PUT /api/v1/kernel/settings/ledger.payments.default_provider with {"value": "momo"}.
payment_actions[0].kind is noneThe payment could not be started at MoMo; payment_actions[0].error says why (code and message, e.g. momo.return_url_required). Fix it, then start the payment again: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/payment-link (shop staff), POST /api/v1/orders/me/orders/{id}/payment-link (a signed-in buyer) or POST /api/v1/orders/public/orders/{id}/payment-link with the Order-Token header (a guest buyer); the buyer may send {"return_url": "…"}.
payment_actions[0].error.code is orders.return_url_not_allowed (or payment-link answers 422 with that code)return_url is not on one of your shop’s addresses. Add its origin to ledger.payments.return_origins (step 2) or verify the domain, then start the payment again.
GET /api/v1/ledger/payments/{id} answers 404 for a payment_idpayment_actions[].payment_id is the order’s own payment. Use payment_actions[].ledger_payment_id with the ledger endpoints.
payment-link returns a new payment_idThe partner reported the previous collection failed (the buyer declined or gave up), so a new attempt was started (status superseded on the old one). Show the buyer the new action and use its status_token. If the partner still collects the old one, that money is refunded through the partner on its own.
A payment is needs_review and the order stays pending_paymentThe partner reported another amount than the amount due. A corrected notification for the same transaction does not clear it: someone with ledger.reconcile finds the amount_mismatch item (GET /api/v1/ledger/exceptions?status=open) and resolves it with POST /api/v1/ledger/exceptions/{id}/resolve: {"action": "accept_received", "payment_id": "<ledger payment id>"} records the amount collected and confirms the order if it is still waiting for payment. Resolve it before the order’s payment deadline (30 minutes by default, AUTOXIDE_LEDGER_PAYMENT_EXPIRY_MINUTES): after it, the order is already cancelled, so the amount collected is refunded through the partner on its own and the order is not reopened. refunded_outside or ignore close the item and the order is cancelled at its deadline.
A late_payment item is open in GET /api/v1/ledger/exceptionsMoney arrived after the payment’s deadline or after the partner reported it failed. The order decides: if it still counts the money (the order goes on), the item closes on its own (resolution kept) within moments; when the order no longer needs it, Autoxide refunds it through the partner on its own, and the item closes once the payment is refunded in full (resolution refunded). Never refund an item whose order went on. An item still open means the partner refused that refund: first check refunds in GET /api/v1/ledger/payments/{id} (a refund may still be pending at the partner), and only then refund outside Autoxide and resolve the item with refunded_outside, so the buyer is not refunded twice.
A refund_failed item is open in GET /api/v1/ledger/exceptionsThe partner refused a refund of that payment, or the refund could not be sent at all (for example a bank transfer, which no partner refunds, of an order cancelled after the money arrived). Nothing is sent again on its own. Refund the buyer outside Autoxide, then resolve the item with refunded_outside; if a later refund through the partner returns the whole payment, the item closes on its own. A refund answered with 409 or 429, or with a server error, was not refused: it stays pending and is sent again with the same reference.
The order stays pending_paymentMoMo could not reach AUTOXIDE_HTTP_PUBLIC_URL. Check the address and look at GET /api/v1/kernel/settings?group=connection for the last error.
GHN’s option is missing from the cartGHN refused the quote. The carrier account shows the last error (GET /api/v1/shipping/carrier-accounts); check the item’s weight and the address.
The order does not move after GHN picked the parcelThe GHN webhook is not registered, or GHN has not applied it yet (about 15 minutes).
An ETag / If-Match errorRead the record again and send its current ETag (If-Match: * skips the check).

Building a shop’s home page from the API

Vietnamese: storefront.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com), and the TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

The website draws its own pages; Autoxide gives it the data: banners in named spots of the page, product collections, and the shop’s brand and contact details. Changing a banner or a collection is a data change (REST, or an AI agent over MCP), never a change of the website’s code. Full reference: docs/CONTENT.md (banners), docs/CATALOG.md (collections).

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token

Placements: where banners go

A placement is a named spot (top_strip, home_hero, sidebar_left, popup…) that says how its banners are shown (single, carousel, grid, stack, strip, popup), which picture ratio and size it takes, on which devices and kinds of pages. A new tenant gets a standard set; a tenant made before this feature adds the missing ones:

curl -sS -X POST "$API/api/v1/content/placements/presets" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

A banner

A text banner in the top strip, linking to a page of the website. tone is a role of the theme (primary, secondary, accent, neutral), never a colour code, so a new theme recolours it. Image banners take a public picture (media_id) with the placement’s ratio; a link can also point to an object, e.g. {"kind": "catalog.collection", "id": "…"}.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/banners" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --json '{"placement":"top_strip","locale":"en","kind":"text","title":"Free delivery over 500,000 VND","tone":"accent","link":{"url":"/shipping"},"status":"active"}'
# expect: 201

An AI agent does the same with the MCP tools content.save_banner, content.order_placement, catalog.save_collection: they only write drafts marked ai_assisted, and a person turns them on.

A collection

A collection groups products for a page: chosen by hand in order (manual), or by a rule (categories, attributes, price range, new, on promotion), sorted by newest, price_asc, price_desc or best_selling.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/catalog/collections" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --json '{"kind":"rule","rules":{"new_within_days":30},"status":"active","texts":{"en":{"title":"New this month"}}}'
# expect: 201

The home page, as the website reads it

Three public calls, no sign-in. Every placement of the page in one call — banners active now, in their order, with href ready and picture variants for srcset:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/public/placements?keys=top_strip,home_hero,home_middle,popup&locale=en&page_kind=home"
# save: PLACEMENTS_ETAG=header:etag

The shop’s brand, contact details, address and opening hours:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/organizations/public/storefront"

A collection page, with one page of its products (same cards as the product list):

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/catalog/public/collections/new-this-month?locale=en"

A shop selling online in Vietnam also shows its owner and the Ministry of Industry and Trade badge in the footer: GET /api/v1/compliance/public/owner and GET /api/v1/compliance/public/badge.

Cache

Public answers carry an ETag (send it in If-None-Match for 304) and a Cache-Control that ends when the next banner starts or ends, so a CDN never keeps an expired banner:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/public/placements?keys=top_strip,home_hero,home_middle,popup&locale=en&page_kind=home" -H "If-None-Match: $PLACEMENTS_ETAG"
# expect: 304

Rules for the website

  • Draw banners in the order given; never shuffle them.
  • A popup has a visible close button, respects its frequency, and never shows on cart, checkout, sign-in or account pages.
  • A carousel does not autoplay when the viewer asks for reduced motion (prefers-reduced-motion) and can be paused.
  • Banners and collections with ai_assisted: true carry an “AI-assisted” label (Vietnam’s Law on Artificial Intelligence — check the original text).

With the SDK

import { createClient } from "@autoxide/sdk";

const api = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com" });

const [placements, shop, collection] = await Promise.all([
  api.get("/api/v1/content/public/placements", {
    query: { keys: "top_strip,home_hero,home_middle,popup", locale: "en", page_kind: "home" },
  }),
  api.get("/api/v1/organizations/public/storefront"),
  api.get("/api/v1/catalog/public/collections/{slug}", {
    path: { slug: "new-this-month" },
    query: { locale: "en" },
  }),
]);

for (const placement of placements.placements) {
  console.log(placement.key, placement.display, placement.banners.length);
}
console.log(shop.brand.name, collection.title, collection.ai_assisted);

Showing posts and pictures on a website

Vietnamese: website.vi.md. Examples use curl with API set to your server (export API=https://api.example.com), and the TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript). They run as tests against every build, so they match the server of this version.

The website reads public endpoints, which need no sign-in and only ever return published versions. The admin steps below (upload, write, publish) set up something to read.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/auth/login" \
  --json '{"email":"admin@example.com","password":"correct horse battery staple"}'
# save: TOKEN=.data.access_token
# save: REFRESH=.data.refresh_token

Upload a picture and make it public

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/media?name=photo.png" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: image/png' --data-binary @photo.png
# expect: 201
# save: MEDIA=.data.id

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/media/$MEDIA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# save: MEDIA_ETAG=header:etag

Changes take the ETag you read in If-Match, so two people never overwrite each other (412 if someone changed it meanwhile).

curl -sS -X PATCH "$API/api/v1/media/$MEDIA" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "If-Match: $MEDIA_ETAG" \
  --json '{"visibility":"public"}'

Write and publish a post

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  --json '{"kind":"post","title":"Hello world","featured_media_id":"'"$MEDIA"'"}'
# expect: 201
# save: POST=.data.id

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries/$POST" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
# save: POST_ETAG=header:etag

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/entries/$POST/publish" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "If-Match: $POST_ETAG" \
  --json '{}'

Read it as the website does

The newest posts, one page at a time:

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/public/posts?locale=en"

For an address the visitor opened, resolve says what to show: entry (render it), redirect (send the visitor on) or gone (answer 410). A missing translation is 404.

featured_media and body_media give each picture its url, alt (in the post’s language), size, and variants: smaller copies, each with a WebP twin in sources. Use them for <picture> and srcset:

<picture>
  <source type="image/webp" srcset="…/content?v=…&w=480&format=webp 480w, …">
  <img src="…/content?v=…" srcset="…&w=480 480w, …" sizes="(max-width: 600px) 100vw, 600px" alt="…" width="…" height="…">
</picture>

Smaller copies are made in the background a moment after the upload; until then variants is empty and the original is served.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/public/resolve?locale=en&path=/blog/hello-world"
# save: PAGE_ETAG=header:etag

Cache: ETag and 304

Every public answer has an ETag. Send it back in If-None-Match: when nothing changed the answer is 304 without a body, and you keep using your copy. Picture URLs carry their version (?v=…) and are cached for a year (Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable): a changed picture gets a new URL.

curl -sS "$API/api/v1/content/public/resolve?locale=en&path=/blog/hello-world" -H "If-None-Match: $PAGE_ETAG"
# expect: 304

With the SDK

import { createClient } from "@autoxide/sdk";

// Public endpoints need no token.
const api = createClient({ baseUrl: "https://api.example.com" });

const page = await api.get("/api/v1/content/public/posts", { query: { locale: "en", limit: 10 } });
for (const post of page.data) {
  console.log(post.title, post.path, post.featured_media?.url);
}

let etag: string | undefined;
const answer = await api.request("get", "/api/v1/content/public/resolve", {
  query: { locale: "en", path: "/blog/hello-world" },
  ifNoneMatch: etag,
});
if ("notModified" in answer) {
  // Keep showing the copy you have.
} else if (answer.type === "entry") {
  console.log(answer.entry.title);
}

Writing a module in your own repository

Vietnamese: writing-a-module.vi.md.

Autoxide is a core that modules plug into. Your module does not have to live in the Autoxide repository, and you do not fork anything: you keep a repository of your own with your module (a library crate) and your server (a five-line binary that runs the official modules plus yours). Your module gets everything a built-in module gets: settings, migrations, permissions, events, background jobs, REST routes in the OpenAPI document, MCP tools for AI agents, and translations.

This guide goes from an empty directory to a module that runs, has tests on SQLite and PostgreSQL, and is part of a server. Everything shown here is the example in examples/external-module, which CI builds and tests on every change — when in doubt, read the file there. The reference for each part of the module contract is docs/MODULE_GUIDE.md.

What you need

  • Rust, in the version of the Autoxide release you build on (its rust-toolchain.toml) or newer; rustup installs it.
  • Nothing else for SQLite. For the PostgreSQL tests, a PostgreSQL 16 or newer server and a user that may CREATE DATABASE (for example docker run --rm -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=postgres -p 5432:5432 postgres:16-alpine).

1. The workspace

One repository, two crates: the module and the server. To get this whole layout generated — a copy of the example with your names — run cargo xtask new-module --external <dir> <module> <entity> in a checkout of Autoxide (for example cargo xtask new-module --external ../acme bookmarks bookmark), then read on to see what each part does.
